events.id: French Film Festival - The Son Of-The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: French Film Festival - The Son Of
events.venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
events.long_description:
One week after a chaotic presidential election, France urgently needs a new Prime Minister. A hapless but ambitious young parliamentary assistant (Jean Chevalier) has a plan: convince his retired and highly erratic politician father (François Cluzet, The Intouchables) to return from exile and seize the top job. What follows is a breakneck political comedy that transforms into a razor-sharp portrait of power, ambition, and the flexibility of principle.

With The Son Of, former political journalist Carlos Abascal Peiró makes an audacious debut, dynamically navigating the treacherous corridors of the French Republic, his camera stalking the backrooms where ideology evaporates and egos dominate, capturing politicians, fixers and media operators engaged in verbal warfare with astonishing ferocity. Filmed before France’s current political turmoil, the narrative hums with uncanny and prophetic resonance. Think Veep with a distinctly Gallic accent; anyone appreciative of Armando Iannucci’s savage political dissections and Succession will find much to savour here.

Newcomer Chevalier is perfectly cast as the slippery modern opportunist, supported by an hilarious, never-better Cluzet’s reluctant patriarch, Karin Viard’s irresistible party operative and Alex Lutz (The Stolen Painting) rounding out a stellar ensemble. Sharp, unsparing, and mischievously satisfying, The Son Of is a winning satire.

events.id: French Film Festival - Santiago: The Camino Therapy-The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: French Film Festival - Santiago: The Camino Therapy
events.venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
events.long_description:
Experience the breathtaking scenery of the Camino de Santiago in this life-affirming drama centred on an unforgettable pairing of characters.

Adam (a powerful performance from up-and-comer Julien Le Berre) is a teenager who’s lost and heading in the wrong direction. After a run-in with the law, a judge hands over a surprising sentence: he must walk the 800 kilometre Camino de Santiago to think about his future.

Assigned to walk the path with Adam is Fred (an excellent-as-always Alexandra Lamy, Miss Violet), a tough and outspoken woman coming to terms with her own chequered history. The two begin a journey that could change their lives. The pair make an unlikely team; Fred is looking to heal from her past, while Adam is struggling to channel his anger and feelings of abandonment. With every mile travelled, they inevitably endure exhaustion, clashes and arguments.

But among the points of tension are moments of peace. As the miles rack up, Fred and Adam begin to form a strong bond. Walking The Way, they each discover an inner strengh they didn’t know they had. Will it be enough to accomplish the goals they set out to achieve?

Santiago: The Camino Therapy is an uplifting and inspirational story with gorgeous vistas that deserve to be seen on the big screen.

events.long_description:
Each Wednesday afternoon, The Animal Medical Centre and Family Kitchen with Mark team up to serve hot, tasty, family-friendly meals and freshly made, slowly fermented sourdough doughnuts.
Set up in a gazebo outside the clinic, Mark prepares a fresh batch of doughnuts and generously portioned meals.
This week's hot dish is Peri Peri Chicken with Pasta Mushroom Alfredo (not spicy).
Although we are using a peri-peri-based recipe, I can assure you that this dish won’t be spicy hot.
We marinade whole chickens that have been butterflied open to maximise flavour and taste. Rubbing the mixture, leaving to settle overnight, then grilling on both sides and roasting at a high temperature over onions and lemons.
After resting, we remove the meat and skin from the carcass and toss with green vegetables, baby spinach leaves and fresh lemon juice.
Served with pasta in a mushroom Alfredo sauce.
We can have your food ready in 5 minutes. If you'd like to pick up outside our event hours, don't hesitate to get in touch with the team to arrange it.
Nothing is served spicy, making it perfect for everyone. Products can be pre-ordered through our website or picked up on the day.
We plan and update the menu on a Monday or Tuesday.
This week's menu has been put to a vote between 4 chicken-based dishes. See my post to see which dish is leading.
Go to our website for a full list of flavours and ingredients.
https://familykitchenwithmark.co.nz/weekly-menu/
Eftpos is available at all our sales.

events.name: Sunset Guided Tour
events.venue: Stonehenge Aotearoa, 51 Ahiaruhe Rd, Carterton
events.long_description:
Experience Stonehenge Aotearoa at its most breathtaking — as the sun dips below the Wairarapa horizon.
Our Sunset Guided Tour blends astronomy, storytelling, and the natural beauty of twilight for an evening you will never forget.

Led by one of our knowledgeable guides, this 90-minute experience explores how ancient cultures used the Sun to track time and mark the turning of the seasons. You’ll discover the scientific and cultural thinking behind the Henge’s unique Southern Hemisphere design before watching the sunset alignment from inside the stone circle.

Weather permitting, you’ll witness how the setting Sun interacts with the structure — a striking moment that links ancient knowledge with the rhythms of the natural world.

Duration and Schedule
• Allow: Approximately 90 minutes
• Start Time: Begins one hour before sunset
• Availability: Offered any day with advance booking

Boost Your Business Series – Lower Hutt 2026

events.id: French Film Festival - The Richest Woman in the World-The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: French Film Festival - The Richest Woman in the World
events.venue: The Screening Room, 435 Queen St, Masterton
events.long_description:
- OFFICIAL SELECTION: Festival de Cannes (Out of Competition) -
- CÉSAR AWARD WINNER: Best Actor – Laurent Lafitte -

Few modern scandals have captivated France as the astonishing events surrounding Liliane Bettencourt, the billionaire heiress to the L’Oreal fortune and doyenne of Parisian society. Now writer/director Thierry Klifa has freely adapted the incredible story into a captivating dark comedy, featuring a jaw-dropping, tailor-made role for one of France’s most iconic stars.

Marianne Farrère (Isabelle Huppert), the head of the Windler Group, is the richest woman in the world. Pierre-Alain Fantin (Laurent Lafitte, who won a César award for his performance) is a vivacious dandy, writer and photographer. After meeting on a photo shoot, the two quickly become inseparable. Their friendship surprises, amuses, intrigues, and eventually unsettles the billionaire’s entourage and family.

Most of all, Marianne’s daughter (Marina Foïs) struggles with her mother’s sudden complicity with this younger man, but her husband (André Marcon) and loyal butler (Raphaël Personnaz) share her concerns. Surreptitious queries soon transition into a private investigation, resulting in extraordinary ramifications for all involved…

With several twists too good to spoil, The Richest Woman in the World makes the most of its fabulous ensemble cast, but Huppert and Lafitte simply eat up the screen. This wildly entertaining film became an enormous box-office hit in France for good reason.

events.long_description:
Toi Whakaari: NZ Drama School presents Whaea Kairau: Mother Hundred Eater by Apirana Taylor, as part of our 2026 Double Bill season.
Aotearoa, the 1840s. The land is fracturing, and one woman will do whatever it takes to survive. Whaea Kairau is dispossessed, displaced, and utterly without illusion as she navigates the chaos of the New Zealand Wars not with nobility, but with a cunning eye for opportunity.
Apirana Taylor's landmark Māori theatre classic is black-hearted and uncomfortably funny. A journey through colonisation's darkest chapters that refuses to offer easy villains, easy victims, or easy answers.
Together with Van Badham's Animal Farm, they form an unmissable double bill from Toi Whakaari: NZ Drama School, one that refuses to look away from the oldest story in the book: who gets power, who loses it, and who pays the price.
We invite you to witness the bold work of our students across Acting, Production, Design, Costume, and Set & Props construction, and come away with more questions, more fire, and more hope than you arrived with.
By arrangement with Playmarket NZ
Whaea Kairau: Mother Hundred Eater | Recommended for ages 16+
Contains references to war, colonial violence, death, coarse language, sexual violence, sexual assault, use of imitation weapons, and themes of colonisation and racial conflict. See our website for more information.
Special School Group Price - Enquire by contacting marketing@toiwhakaari.ac.nz

events.id: NZCFS Wellington Branch Monthly Meeting June 2026: Overview of National Conference and AGM-16 Mein St, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand-Facebook
events.name: NZCFS Wellington Branch Monthly Meeting June 2026: Overview of National Conference and AGM
events.venue: 16 Mein St, Newtown, Wellington 6021, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Every year in May the New Zealand China Friendship Society holds a National Conference and AGM. Last year National Executive committee members, branch delegates, and members from all over the country gathered together in Christchurch. It was a chance to renew old friendships, exchange stories about the year just gone past, and plan new activities for the year to come. This year the National Conference and AGM was held in Whanganui 22–24 May 2026 with the theme “Our Heroes, Heritage & Horizons.”
Speakers at the conference celebrated the rich history of connection between New Zealand and China, honouring those who helped shape those connections and exploring the new directions ahead for our people-to-people relationships.
The Wellington Branch was well represented, with Wellington Branch President Chris Lipscombe, Central Region Vice President (and Wellington Branch Treasurer) Juping Zhou, Branch Secretary Vera Xu, and Committee Member Paul Sayers all attending the conference and AGM.
At our members’ meeting on Wednesday 17 June, Chris, Juping, Vera and Paul will report back on what happened during the weekend, sharing highlights of the conference, what was presented and discussed, who stepped down (and who stepped up), and key actions and priorities for the organisation over the coming year. A key outcome was the adoption of a five-year plan, including some exciting events and activities to take place here in New Zealand and in China from 2027 onwards to commemorate the 100th anniversary of Rewi Alley’s arrival in Shanghai.

Grab a spot on our couch and enjoy the noise at The Racket Lounge - a chill classical music series showcasing up-and-coming Pōneke musicians.

If you’ve never been to a classical concert before, or if you have and now you want to see talented emerging musicians experimenting and playing what they want to play, then The Racket Lounge is for you. Over the past two seasons we’ve seen classical covers, jazz ensembles, video game soundtracks, original compositions, loop pedals, poetry and much more. Our 2026 season is shaping up to be just as epic, plus with your tickets starting at just $5 you can afford to take a chance on something new.

Each concert will feature a different line up of musicians and genres, to be announced a week before each session. If you’re a musician looking to perform at The Racket Lounge, then head to the New Zealand String Quartet’s website to see how to apply.

Our first Racket Lounge concert, With a Twist, perfectly encapsulates the spirit of the Racket Lounge. There will of course be your typical classical concert ingredients – pianos, strings, a wind instrument or two. But this concert’s line up that is not all that it seems. With a cocktail of genres and styles, this programme will surprise and delight. From 4-hand piano pieces to unconventional jazz trios and more, there’ll be something for everyone to sink their teeth into - while enjoying a treat from the bar of course. Come ready to taste what Wellington’s new music scene has to offer.

The Racket Lounge is created and presented by the New Zealand String Quartet Trust - Te Rōpū Tūrū o Aotearoa, New Zealand’s longest-running professional string quartet. With support from Wellington City Council.

Tickets are choose your price starting from just $5.

Please note that Bedlam & Squalor is a licensed venue, so under 18s must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. Everyone must bring ID.

events.name: Alex Trask Quintet
events.venue: 37 Vivian St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Local saxophonist Alex Trask presents a set of original music for two horns and rhythm. Inspired by folk music from around the world and infused with jazz performance practice, these tunes have a simplicity in common. Free improvised sections contrast carefully arranged melodies, allowing creativity and structure to coexist. The fiddle-esque melodies and straightforward harmonies create an open and inviting sound that changes depending on the musicians on stage. Performing this music as a group invites each member to paint their private imaginings, creating a unique collective folklore.
This is the first of a two gig series where the band will be exploring some new compositions. On this gig the band will perform some previously unheard songs, come and catch the debut of this new set.
Doors 7pm, music 7:30pm
$25/$10
Personnel:
Alex Trask - saxophone
Michael Costeloe - Trumpet
Duncan Haynes - piano
Elijah Mulheron - bass
John Rae - Drums

events.id: Julia-Circa Theatre, 1 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Julia
events.venue: Circa Theatre, 1 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
In 2012, Julia Gillard delivered a speech that ricocheted across Australia, New Zealand, and around the world. Now, the woman and the moment is brought to the stage in Julia. This gripping one-woman show puts us inside a very public storm, and reveals the life and career that led to it.

From idealistic young advocate to leader under relentless scrutiny, Julia takes us behind the microphone of the landmark “misogyny speech.” It steps into the personal, political and socio-cultural forces that forged it. Blending real excerpts with scenes inspired by true events, this is more than one leader’s story. It’s a sharp, human look at how we judge power, how we listen to women, and what we demand of those who lead us.

Against a backdrop of progress and pushback on gender equality, Julia takes on fresh resonance here in Aotearoa. It draws the line between conviction and compromise, private life and public duty. And it asks what it costs to stand your ground and say “not now, not ever” in a world that still questions women who lead.

events.long_description:
Love, lies and glorious chaos...

NZ Opera’s 2021 season of The Marriage of Figaro – the world-premiere of a sumptuous staging by the superstar trans-Tasman creative duo of Lindy Hume and Tracy Grant Lord – remains a high-water mark in the company’s history. For its centrepiece mid-year season, with a cast boasting an almost-unbelievable wealth of talent from Aotearoa and Australia, NZ Opera is thrilled to finally bring this incredible opera to the fair city of Te Whanganui-a-Tara Wellington.

Picking up narratively where The Barber of Seville left off, The Marriage of Figaro is renowned for its wit and musical sophistication – truly an example of the legendary Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart operating at the height of his powers.

With an outstanding principal cast joined on stage by the Freemasons Foundation New Zealand Opera Chorus and accompanied by Orchestra Wellington – conducted, for the first time, by James Judd – this season offers opera at its most gorgeous, its most vivid, its most unforgettable.

Each concert will faithfully recreate an album and follow up with a set of classics and deep cuts that span each artist’s catalogue.

Their endeavours have drawn thousands of fans, cementing Come Together as a must-see event on the music calendar.

events.name: The Marriage of Figaro
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Written when Mozart was operating at the top of his powers, The Marriage of Figaro is considered one of the great operas. New Zealand Opera’s production in 2026 promises to bring the 240-year-old masterpiece to life in a sumptuous setting. 
Picking up narratively where The Barber of Seville left off, The Marriage of Figaro is renowned for its wit and musical sophistication. It follows Figaro and his bride-to-be, Susannah, on their wedding day. Figaro’s employer, Count Almaviva, tries to seduce Susanna, so the engaged couple seek revenge. The cast boasts an unbelievable wealth of talent from Aotearoa and Australia, including runner-up at the 2022 Lexus Song Quest Felicity Tompkins, Julien Van Mellaerts, and James Clayton. 
Trans-Tasman creative duo Lindy Hume and Tracy Grant Lord take the helm with direction and design while Orchestra Wellington and conductor James Judd lead from the pit. This season offers opera at its most gorgeous, its most vivid, its most unforgettable.

events.venue: Circa Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Inside Circa Theatre’s waterfront venue, you’ll find two performance spaces. Both offer a smorgasbord of professional theatre throughout the year. Playwrights from international heavy hitters to brilliant Kiwi voices are represented. It also includes programming from comedies and cabarets to contemporary dance and pantomime. 
Before or after your show, visit the on-site café, brasserie and restaurant, Chouchou. It opens out onto a deck, where you can take in views across the harbour. Look up to admire the art installation above. Called ‘Velarium’, it undulates in the wind, mirroring the water in the harbour. 
Circa Theatre began its life in 1976. A breakaway group of actors and theatre practitioners decided that Aotearoa needed a new and innovative approach to theatre. Five decades later, it is still pushing boundaries, making people laugh and cry, and creating theatrical memories. 
If you don’t have your own Circa memory yet, there’s an opportunity to create one nearly every night of the week.

Masterton Street Eats & Beats

Formerly known as Thursday Night Food Trucks, Masterton Street Eats & Beats is Masterton's favourite weekly food truck and community event, bringing together great food, live music, and a relaxed family-friendly atmosphere every Thursday evening.

With a rotating lineup of food trucks and street food vendors, no two weeks are ever quite the same. From gourmet burgers and international cuisine to sweet treats, coffee, and local favourites, there's something to satisfy every craving. Add live music, plenty of seating, and a welcoming community vibe, and you've got the perfect way to kick off your weekend early.

Whether you're catching up with friends, bringing the family out for dinner, or simply looking for an easy meal after work, Masterton Street Eats & Beats offers a fun and affordable night out for all ages.

Event Details
Every Thursday
4:30pm – 7:00pm (rain or shine)
Outside the Masterton Club, Chapel Street (SH2), Masterton
Free Entry

What to Expect
• rotating food and beverage vendors throughout the season
• Live music and entertainment
• Family-friendly atmosphere
• outdoor seating available or bring a picnic blanket
• New vendors regularly joining the lineup
• EFTPOS and cash accepted by most vendors

Food truck and street food vendors are always welcome to enquire about joining the event.

Come hungry, bring your friends, and enjoy one of the Wairarapa's favourite weekly community gatherings.

After winning Best Event at last year’s WOAP, our celebrated Tanzanian Cuisine Dinner is back — for two weeks only.

Experience an evening designed for discovery, comfort, and generous sharing. Guests are invited to order as many dishes as they wish from a specially curated menu showcasing classic Tanzanian flavours, traditions, and vibrant spices. This is not a set menu, but a relaxed dining experience that encourages exploration at your own pace.

To complement the food, an optional pairing menu featuring wines, beers, and thoughtfully crafted non-alcoholic beverages will be available each evening.

May 7th, 8th, 9th
May 14th, 15th, 16th
June dates added due to high demand!

Charred first, then simmered in spiced coconut gravy.

Traditional doughnut

Plated Culinary Experience — $82 per person

Mini Mandazi
Lightly spiced coconut doughnut

Zanzibar Seafood Supu
Prawns and fish in coconut broth

A bright palate cleanser.

Nyama Choma (Chef’s Selection)
Charcoal-grilled lamb or beef
served with fragrant Swahili pilau rice,
kachumbari and pili pili sauce.

Grilled chicken in rich coconut curry sauce
Charred first, then simmered in spiced coconut gravy.
Served with chapati.

Dessert
Spiced Chocolate & Cardamom Mousse
with candied coconut and sesame shard.

events.long_description:
Ultra violet lights and neon nights in Wellington. Prepare to experience Paintvine like you’ve never experienced it before – in the dark!

Paintvine After Dark is New Zealand’s original glow in the dark paint party – a completely unique night out where creativity, neon paint, and UV lights come together for an unforgettable experience. Watch your artwork come to life as fluorescent colours glow under the lights and your canvas transforms before your eyes.

Our artist guides you step-by-step, so absolutely no art experience is needed. Whether you’re planning a date night, organising a catch-up with friends, or just keen to try something different, Paintvine After Dark is all about good vibes, glowing paint, and outrageous fun from start to finish.

It’s part art class, part neon party, and absolute fun! Who knew you could have so much fun in the dark?

Drinks: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available for purchase.

Food: A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, neon acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit. All our events are in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip as you create! At the end of the night you will leave with your own fluro painting and a fun memory to go with it.

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

events.name: Looking for a New Sport? Try Ultimate Frisbee
events.venue: Ākau Tangi Sports Centre, 72 Kemp Street, Kilbirnie, Wellington
events.long_description:
Looking for something active and social to try on a Thursday night?

Come along to our free beginner Ultimate Frisbee taster sessions at Ākau Tangi Recreation Centre. These relaxed games are designed for people who have never played before or want a casual introduction to the sport.

Ultimate frisbee is a fun, fast-moving team sport played with a flying disc. It is easy to pick up, very social, and a great way to meet new people while getting some exercise.

Each Thursday night is a stand-alone session, so you can drop in whenever it suits you. You do not need to have attended earlier weeks, and there is no commitment to come every week.
These sessions focus on beginners and newer players, with guidance available to help people learn the basics, build confidence, and enjoy their first games.

Most people who attend are in their 20s and 30s, but anyone curious to try ultimate frisbee is welcome.

Bring a friend, try something new, and see why so many people love ultimate.

Event Details
What: Beginner Ultimate Frisbee “Taster” Sessions
When: Thursdays, 7:00pm
Dates: 16 April – 18 June
Where: Court 1, Ākau Tangi Recreation Centre, Kilbirnie, Wellington
Cost: Free
Who: Beginners and anyone curious about trying ultimate frisbee
What to bring: Comfortable sports clothes and running shoes

No experience needed. Just show up and join in.

events.long_description:
Melanie Bracewell is back with a brand-new hour-long show. It took a long time to write because she got distracted by a Sudoku puzzle. Melanie Bracewell — Dilly Dallying is about procrastination. Come along (don’t be late) to hear the Kiwi comic’s hilarious observations about avoidance. The UK comedy guide Chortle described Melanie as a “phenomenal storyteller”. Expect some wild stories as she dissects why she ‘puts things off’ for another day. 
Stand-up comedy, radio announcing, radio producer, script writing — Melanie Bracewell has found success in multiple disciplines. Her TV appearances include ‘The Cheap Seats,’ ‘Taskmaster’ (NZ), ‘Have You Been Paying Attention,’ and ‘Thank God You’re Here.’ She has won multiple awards as well, including the Billy T Award for the country’s best emerging comedian in 2018. The same year, she won Breakthrough Comedian of the Year at the NZ Comedy Guild Awards.

events.id: REforms: Shayne P. Carter and the NZSO-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: REforms: Shayne P. Carter and the NZSO
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
It’s an amalgamation of two musical worlds, and the result is set to be mesmerising. Shayne P Carter has been active on the New Zealand popular music scene since 1979. The singer-songwriter has penned many great tunes. Now, some of those tunes are getting an orchestral treatment thanks to the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra. REforms reimagines ten of Shayne’s songs in magical orchestra colour. 
With arrangements by Tane Upjohn Beatson and conducted by Hamish McKeich, the concert promises to enhance Shayne’s songs through a new lens while keeping their original integrity. Classic songs like Randolph’s Going Home and If I Were You sit alongside new numbers like Left To Defend. Songs from Shayne’s solo album Offsider also feature. 
Shayne is best known for leading indie rock band Straitjacket Fits from 1986 to 1994, and rock band Dimmer (1995–2012). He is a member of the New Zealand Music Hall of Fame and the recipient of several Aotearoa Music Awards.

Victoria University’s Classics Museum examines the complex afterlives of antiquities through two remarkable objects—a Roman portrait head now subject to repatriation after being identified as illicitly excavated, and a richly carved child’s sarcophagus later revealed to be a modern forgery. Associate Professor Diana Burton explores the investigations behind these discoveries and what they mean for museum stewardship and the study of the ancient world.

events.id: Speed Dating 45-59 and 60+-Kanteen Cafe, 7 Waterloo Quay, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Speed Dating 45-59 and 60+
events.venue: Kanteen Cafe, 7 Waterloo Quay, Wellington
events.long_description:
Come join us for a fun night of Speed Dating! It’s a fun and safe way to meet other genuine singles looking for a real connection. We will have a private function space for this event. Price includes a drink and delicious food at the break!

Speed Daters will be split into 2 age groups which will run simultaneously. There will be an opportunity to mix with the other group during the break.

When you arrive you will get a name label and your complimentary first drink, and will have time to settle in and mingle a little. You will be Speed Dating with around 10 people over the course of the evening. You will have 7 minutes to chat to each person. You then decide if you want to meet your Speed Dates again and tick interested on your form if you do. Only if the feeling is mutual will we email you each other’s contact details.

Speed dating does not have to be stressful or frightening; you will be pleasantly surprised how fun and positive it is.

Our event is designed to be inclusive and foster open, honest communication. Not everyone you meet will be your type, but we expect you to be polite. You only have to chat to them for seven minutes!

events.id: Waenga-Toi Pōneke Arts Centre, 3-6 Market Lane, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Waenga
events.venue: Toi Pōneke Arts Centre, 3-6 Market Lane, Wellington
events.long_description:
Created by Hariata & Tamati Moriarty and directed by Jim Moriarty, 'Waenga' centres on a young wahine Māori who is arrested and finds herself in a police holding cell. Alongside her journey is Peyton, who is coming to understand what a Tangata Tiriti partnership is and Grayson, a young Māori lawyer navigating his role in the system.

Performed by an ensemble cast, including well known rangatahi Hariata and Tamati Moriarty, the play is presented in Te Rākau’s unique Theatre Marae framework, creating space for collective reflection and shared experience.

Te Rākau is the longest running Māori theatre company in Aotearoa founded in 1989.

Recommended age 12+ contains swearing and depicts some violence. Children under 12 can accompany for free with a paying adult.

events.id: Beans and Don plus Stan Antonio-Abandoned Petone,38 Fitzherbert St, Petone, Lower Hutt 5012, New Zealand, Lower Hutt-All Events In
events.name: Beans and Don plus Stan Antonio
events.venue: Abandoned Petone,38 Fitzherbert St, Petone, Lower Hutt 5012, New Zealand, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
Beans and Don plus Stan Antonio
An evening of folky stuff at the taproom.
Stan Antonio from 7pm-ish, Beans and Don from 8pm-ish.

Beans and Don - Wellington based singer songwriters and multi-instrumentalists Beans Wright and Don Mackay have been performing together as a duo since early 2025, and were previously both members of the trio Don and The Divorcees over the previous couple of years. They play a mixed repertoire of Beans songs and Dons in a set that ranges across folk, country and acoustic rock styles, including most of the songs from Don and The Divorcees 2025 album “Bit Players”. The 13th Floor described “Bit Players” as “an album that trusts in the detail, honesty, and strength of three distinct songwriting voices working in harmony. Alongside the sadness and stillness, there is wit, warmth, and a sense of the comfort of friends.”

Stan Antonio - Phoebe and Alex grew up attending folk festivals and have played around Wellington as part of various folk groups. They dabble in the realms of Americana, folk, and bluegrass, and have recently been writing music together. Their influences include classic artists such as Gillian Welch and Dave Rawlings, more contemporary artists such as Adrianne Lenker. They aspire to use the banjo as a force for good in this world, alongside close harmonies and acoustic guitar.

events.id: REforms: Shayne P. Carter and the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra-Michael Fowler Centre, 111 Wakefield Street, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: REforms: Shayne P. Carter and the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, 111 Wakefield Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
The heft and glory of the NZSO collide with the Shayne P. Carter songbook for the world premiere of this formidable work. Ten tracks ‘reformed’ in orchestral technicolour while maintaining the integrity of the originals.

Classic songs like Randolph’s Going Home and If I Were You spar with new numbers like Left To Defend. Guitar and orchestra do battle on the mighty Crystalator. Songs from Carter’s solo Offsider album expand from their original two-finger piano primitivism into widescreen epicness. Other songs glower with the drama of orchestral restraint.

With arrangements by Tane Upjohn Beatson and conducted by Hamish McKeich, REforms is a singular and purposeful artistic statement; an immersive and all-encompassing performance from a world-class orchestra and one of Aotearoa’s greatest singer/songwriters.

events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Sludgy noise superstars CHAT PILE have announced their first ever Australia & New Zealand tour for June 2026. Fusing elements of post-punk, nu metal, grunge, they have earned a cult following for their eclectic take on what they simply deem ‘noise rock.’ 
Formed in 2019, the band took their name from piles of chat, byproducts of mining which are commonly found throughout northeast Oklahoma. Their adopted stage names Raygun Busch, Luther Manhole, Stin and Cap’n Ron were conjured as a way of avoiding identification from previous employers.
Following the band’s self-released debut ‘This Dungeon Earth’, they were signed to The Flenser in 2020 and released their debut album ‘God’s Country’. The album received broad acclaim, including ‘Best New Music’ on Pitchfork. 
Their second full-length record ‘Cool World’ was releasing in 2024. They went on to headline Roadburn Festival 2025 and tour extensively, earning a reputation for an incendiary live show.
Joining Chat Pile in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Auckland & Wellington is Kiwi sludge metal band BEASTWARS. The veteran group originally formed in the late 1980s and have abided by one steadfast maxim ever since: obey the riff. It’s time. 
Dig into Chat Pile this June.

events.venue: Valhalla, Wellington
events.long_description:
Edgy music for edgy people.

Alternative sounds of the Eighties and beyond to make you move.

Your host is DJ Matai, known for sets spanning vintage goth, new wave and post-punk. Expect to hear the classic and the obscure. Not only a selector, but a genuine alternative music fanatic, he is also known for running Razored Raw and drumming in bands such as No Sector and Maced.

Joined by guests:

DJ Nightmare: Three decades deep and still dragging the dancefloor into the dark — DJ Nightmare is a fixture of the scene and a genuine authority on all things goth, post-punk, industrial, cold wave, new romantic, angular electronic, neo goth and synth pop, with a blast beat or two thrown in for the brave. Known to his people as Ol' Nighty, he has spent years as a promoter, radio host, and noise terrorist, and every set carries that hard-won knowledge: equal parts floor-filler and deep-cut excavation, crafted to pull even the most committed wallflowers out of the shadows. Expect the unexpected. Expect the dark, Expect to dance.

DJ Shade is an 80s deep-cut enthusiast. Digging up rare gems from New Zealand alongside obscure B-sides that span electro, new wave, post punk dancefloor cuts. Expect a carefully curated set of grooves and underground energy guaranteed to move the floor. Beyond the decks, Shade is also an active musician, performing in bands such as Whirlwind and The Mermmen.

Brought to you with the support of Creeps Record Parlour!

events.id: The Keeper's Dance: an Evening of Butoh-BATS Theatre, 1 Kent Tce, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: The Keeper's Dance: an Evening of Butoh
events.venue: BATS Theatre, 1 Kent Tce, Wellington
events.long_description:
With Lime presents

Two bodies. Three Butoh dances. Infinite transformations.

Here’s something you don’t often see: two artists on opposite sides of the world building a work together — over Zoom. Rosemary Candelario is in Austin, Texas. Miki Seifert is in Wellington. For months they’ve been meeting across time zones to plan, imagine, and develop The Keeper’s Dance. They won’t be in the same room — or the same country — until Rosemary arrives in Wellington on 11 June. Then, just eight days before opening night, they’ll visit five Wellington lighthouses together and let the land shape the work.

This is how Butoh travels.

Butoh is visceral and cathartic, ethereal and poetic. A Butoh performance is not merely seen, but experienced and felt.

Followed by a post-show Q&A.

AFTER A HUGE RUN OF SHOWS OVER SUMMER, CARU & BRANDN SHIRAZ BRING THEIR MUCH HYPED LIVE SHOW BACK TO THE MIGHTY TE-WHANGANUI-A-TARA. PLAYING AT MOON BAR FOR ONE NIGHT ONLY!

PRESENTED BY GARAGE SALE

JOINED BY AN ALL-STAR CAST OF LOCAL SELECTORS:
⟡ CLOVA
⟡ NOYER & YOUNG GHO$T
⟡ ULTRAVIOLET

⌁₊˚⊹ ⊹˚₊⌁

Caru and Brandn Shiraz join forces to celebrate the sounds of UK Garage. The pair combined their unique musical styles with the 2025 release of their EP ‘Back 2 Back’, a project inspired by the pioneers of pirate radio. Their music combines both artists' respective styles to create a fresh take on the classic 2000’s dance genre, with Brandn Shiraz’s boundary pushing MC skills effortlessly complementing Caru’s refined production. The duo have had notable sets across Aotearoa, with a recent summer tour which showcased the fusion of their energy at festivals such as Northern Bass, The Others Way, Cuba Dupa and Twisted Frequency, and most recently opening for Bakey and Capo Lee.

⌁₊˚⊹ ⊹˚₊⌁

This night will be curated by Garage Sale, one of the capital’s longest running garage nights, who have chosen a range of the finest DJs in town to keep the vibes flowing. Opening things up we have Noyer and Young Gho$t the masterminds of Garage Sale, who will be easing things in with some selections across UKG, funky and grimey beats accompanied by Ghost’s bars.

Warming up for the headliner we have CLOVA, a rising star and local legend who recently released her debut album ‘Spiral’ to widespread applause. For Garage Sale she will hone in some of her favourite tracks, new and old, delivering her unique take on the sound.

Finally on closing duties we have none other than Ultraviolet, making his Garage Sale debut. A seasoned veteran with releases on Big Fresh, Echo Train and Club Unique, UV is one of the country’s best kept musical secrets, and we can’t wait to see what he pulls out the bag for this set.

events.id: Porirua Parkrun-Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana-Event Finder
events.name: Porirua Parkrun
events.venue: Bothamley Park, Champion Street, Porirua - Mana
events.long_description:
What is Porirua parkrun? It is a free 5km walk or run event - It’s not about coming first or winning. You can go at your own pace and just enjoy being with other people. It is inclusive and the perfect way to start your weekend in the outdoors chatting to people.

The start occurs just upstream of the Bothamley Park carpark. This car park is off Champion street, opposite the intersection with Windley Street. Head to end of carpark where the concrete ends and there is a gate. For location see https://goo.gl/maps/wEohfp9bRu82.

The course is following the old coach road (circa 1870's) established for the early farms in the area. Today this historic track is located within a park, away from cars and now used by walkers, runners and cyclists.

The track is generally 3 metres wide with a gentle gradient and a compacted gravel surface beside the Kenepuru Stream through a picturesque wooded wild valley. (Note there is a pinch point for a short section after the 2km marker where participants need to go single file each direction for approx 30 metres)

The valley runs east-west with mature trees which means this has to be one of the most sheltered places, out of the wind to exercise in Wellington.

What does it cost to join in? Nothing - it's free! but please register before your first run or walk, so you can get your timing results. You only need to register with parkrun once, to participate at any of the parkrun events around the world. Don't forget to bring a copy of your barcode. If you forget it, you won't get a time.

How fast do I have to be? Walking is fine as long as you can finish the 5km. Please come along and join in whatever your pace!

One dog per adult is welcome, as long as it is on a short hand held lead.

Children welcome but those 10 years and under need to be kept within arms reach of a supervising adult.

Note there is no toilets in the park, so go before you go.

We're friendly! Every week we grab a post park run/walk coffee/tea at Get Fixed within Kai Tahi at 20 Parumoana Street, to mix exercise with socialising.

There are volunteering opportunities even week. So those doing Duke of Edinburgh or similar challenges can get volunteer credits. Ensure you contact us well in advance at "porirua@parkrun.co.nz"

events.name: Auditions - Social Climbers by Roger Hall
events.venue: 22 Ghuznee Street,Atlas House, 22 Ghuznee St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Auditions - Social Climbers by Roger Hall
A group of female teachers, along with one reluctantly accompanying daughter, set off on a weekend bushwalking trip in the mountains to escape it all. But when torrential rain and a washed-out bridge leave them stranded in a remote hut for three days, tensions begin to rise.

The women’s carefully constructed social facades begin to crumble as they challenge each other, strip away professional distance, and grow into a bond of support, understanding, and friendship. This insightful and witty situation comedy explores truth, consequences, and unexpected revelations through humour, honesty, and emotional depth.

The play delves into the complexities of relationships, resilience, and the bonds of female friendship. With rich, relatable roles for women and a compelling mix of comedy and heartfelt moments, this is a wonderful opportunity to bring dynamic, authentic female characters to life on stage.

We’ll be looking to cast women who will enjoy the creative process and work collaboratively. Strong on-stage chemistry and the ability to connect authentically with others will be key.

If you’re interested in auditioning you can find more information and fill out the form at https://www.stagecraft.co.nz/auditions

KEY DATES
Callbacks if needed will be Sunday 21st June and the performance dates are Wednesday 23rd September - Saturday 3rd October.

ROLES
Maxine (The Drama Queen): 50s-60’s. Outgoing, flamboyant, and boisterous. While she can be snide and opinionated, her character undergoes a convincing emotional journey.

Kath (The Lovable Older Teacher): 50s-60’s. The “old girl” of the group. Loveable, grounded, and no-nonsense.

Emily (The Eternal Doormat): 40’s-50’s. A put-upon woman who has been a “doormat” her whole life.

events.long_description:
A group of female teachers, along with one reluctantly accompanying daughter, set off on a weekend bushwalking trip in the mountains to escape it all. But when torrential rain and a washed-out bridge leave them stranded in a remote hut for three days, tensions begin to rise.
The women’s carefully constructed social facades begin to crumble as they challenge each other, strip away professional distance, and grow into a bond of support, understanding, and friendship. This insightful and witty situation comedy explores truth, consequences, and unexpected revelations through humour, honesty, and emotional depth.
The play delves into the complexities of relationships, resilience, and the bonds of female friendship. With rich, relatable roles for women and a compelling mix of comedy and heartfelt moments, this is a wonderful opportunity to bring dynamic, authentic female characters to life on stage.
We’ll be looking to cast women who will enjoy the creative process and work collaboratively. Strong on-stage chemistry and the ability to connect authentically with others will be key.

events.long_description:
Flesh and Blood Nationals 2026 – New Zealand
Card Merchant Wellington is incredibly proud to be hosting the New Zealand Nationals for Flesh and Blood this year. We’re excited to welcome qualified players from across the country to compete for the title of New Zealand National Champion.
This is a two-day championship event featuring both Classic Constructed and Draft play for a total of 10 rounds before breaking into our top 8.
Nationals will be hosted at our Store here in Wellington, which can comfortably accommodates up to 120 players with spacious seating.
While the store is located on the first floor, we have private access via a side elevator for anyone with accessibility requirements. If you require lift access or any additional assistance, please let our team know in advance and we’ll be happy to accommodate.
We’re located in central Wellington, with a Wilson Parking garage directly behind the venue, providing convenient parking across the entire weekend. There are also numerous cafés, restaurants, and takeaway options within walking distance. Our team will be more than happy to recommend great spots for breakfast, lunch, or dinner before, during, or after the event.
If you have any additional questions or specific requirements, please don’t hesitate to reach out, we’re here to help make the weekend as smooth as possible.
---
Day One – Saturday, June 20th
Doors open at 8:00am, with the player meeting beginning at 9:00am. We’re aiming to start Round 1 shortly after, around 9:15am.
The morning will consist of four rounds of Classic Constructed, finishing just after 1:00pm. We’ll then take a short lunch break before transitioning into the Draft portion of the event.
Draft seating will be announced at 2:00pm, with the draft beginning shortly after. Once drafting is complete, players pools will be registered and players will build decks before we head into three rounds of Draft to close out Day One.
We expect play to conclude around 6pm, depending on match pace.
---
Day Two – Sunday, June 21st
Day Two will also begin at 9:00am with a short player meeting before jumping straight back into play.
We’ll complete three additional rounds of Classic Constructed, after which we’ll break for lunch after final standings are confirmed. Top 8 players will leave their decks with our judging team during this break to allow deck checks.
Following the lunch break, we’ll invite our Top 8 players back for photos/interveiws (where applicable) before beginning the Top 8 playoff to determine the 2026 New Zealand National Champion.
---
As always, the best-laid plans aren’t immune to delays or hiccups, so these timings should be treated as guidelines rather than exact guarantees. We’ll keep players informed throughout the day if any adjustments are needed.
We’re looking forward to an incredible weekend of high-level competition and bringing the Flesh and Blood community together here in Wellington.

events.name: FREE Neurodiversity Workshop
events.venue: Fors, 298 Taranaki St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents. Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
This one-day workshop introduces you to the topic of neurodiversity and considers some of the key conditions that people live with. We look at:
•ADHD – Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
•Autism
•The “Dys family” – dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia (Development Coordination Disorder)
•OCD – Obsessive Compulsive Disorder
•Tourette’s Syndrome
Tik Tok creator and public speaker on neurodiversity, Nigel Sutton, will introduce the subject and facilitate you in discovering the definitions and impacts of each of the key kinds of neurodiversity. Working together with other participants, you will consider many key commonalities that those living with various neurodivergent conditions experience. We will expose the realities of being neurodivergent in a “neurotypical world” and this will allow you to develop empathy and practical strategies to support neurodivergent people to be their best.
You will be able to ask anything you want about neurodiversity.
Find out from those offering “lived experience” what it is really like to have a different kind of brain. This one day workshop is: ”Neurodiversity in a Nutshell” – whether you know a little or a lot, whether you are a relative, employer, partner, friend, or just interested to know more about neurodiversity – this workshop is for you!

Stella Carruthers, textile artist and eco lifestylist, will guide you on this one-day workshop to learn about sustainable living from a reduce and reuse perspective. -Identify and describe the 8 pillars of the zero-waste movement and how they apply to recycling practices in contemporary Aotearoa New Zealand society.
- Understand what greenwashing is and have debunked some common greenwashing myths prevalent in society.

events.id: Get the Job: STARR Interview Technique And Preparation-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Get the Job: STARR Interview Technique And Preparation
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Get the best results in job interviews. Learn how to approach behavioural questions and impress the interview panel. Ace interviews using the potent Starr method. Use it to your advantage by answering competency focused questions with winning replies.

Meet the demand for excellence in the job market head on. Learn how to utilise the Starr technique in the way that recruiters use it. That is, to define and seek out the skills and qualities of the best candidate. Master the Starr skills and feel confident in your next job interview.

Familarise yourself with the skills needed to ace your next interview. Learn the STARR method as an approach to responding to behavioural based questions. Understand how to use concrete examples from your life as proof that you possess the experience and skills for the job you are applying for. You’ll develop the key interview skill of being able to share your accomplishments through real-life examples.

In this course, you are taught how to identify specific example situations that are unique to you. You’ll learn how to confidently talk about the tasks involved and describe how you completed the key task and met its challenges. We’ll also consider the context of jobs you are interviewing for and how to choose examples that best show the desired skills interviewers are seeking.

By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
- Develop a higher level of confidence in approaching job interviews.
- Identify the different components of the STARR acronym and apply them to the job interview context.
- Identify what behavioural based questions are and why recruiters use them.
- Successfully answer behavioural based interview questions by applying the STARR technique.
- Develop skills in using real life examples to show transferable skills in the workplace.

Note: You must be a NZ citizen or resident to qualify for the free course fee option.  A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

events.long_description:
Neurodiversity Workshop
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
This one-day workshop introduces you to the topic of neurodiversity and considers some of the key conditions that people live with. We look at:
•ADHD – Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
•Autism
•The “Dys family” – dyslexia, dysgraphia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia (Development Coordination Disorder)
•OCD – Obsessive Compulsive Disorder
•Tourette’s Syndrome
Tik Tok creator and public speaker on neurodiversity, Nigel Sutton, will introduce the subject and facilitate you in discovering the definitions and impacts of each of the key kinds of neurodiversity. Working together with other participants, you will consider many key commonalities that those living with various neurodivergent conditions  experience. We will expose the realities of being neurodivergent in a “neurotypical world” and this will allow you to develop empathy and practical strategies to support neurodivergent people to be their best. 
You will be able to ask anything you want about neurodiversity.
Find out from those offering “lived experience” what it is really like to have a different kind of brain. This one day workshop is: ”Neurodiversity in a Nutshell” – whether you know a little or a lot, whether you are a relative, employer, partner, friend, or just interested to know more about neurodiversity – this workshop is for you!

If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Together, workshop participants will demystify how artificial intelligence actually works, acknowledge some of the harms of this new technology, learn about the characteristics of mis/disinformation, build resilience against fake news, and explore why our brains weren’t built for the infinite scroll. You will walk away from the workshop with a better understanding of the hidden forces shaping your screen, equipped with real-world tools to cut through the digital noise.
  Dr. Andrew Chen is a leading New Zealand specialist at the intersection of digital technology ethics and public policy. With a PhD from the University of Auckland in Computer Systems Engineering, Andrew brings a deep technical understanding and applies it towards systemic issues and interventions. events.id: Exploring Figure & Form-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Exploring Figure & Form
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
In this course we will study the human figure through drawing and sculpture. Both mediums use close observation as a focus and encourage the study of the curves, angles, and subtleties of the human body to accurately depict it.

Students will be guided in experimentations with size and volume, as well as exercises that will sharpen one's attention to detail, improving an artist's overall observational skills and enhancing their artistry across all subjects and styles.

In this course you will -

- Learn how to imbue a sense of the models personality into your drawing and sculpture
- Learn different approaches to rendering the surface of your sculpture
- Explore traditional working methods in both drawing and sculpting

Course fee includes model, tutor, air-dry modelling clay, necessary tools & equipment

events.long_description:
Wellington Ice Rink at Queens Wharf

Paradice EVENTS returns to Wellington this winter with the Wellington Ice Rink at Queens Wharf. Located on Wellington’s waterfront, the pop-up ice rink transforms Queens Wharf into a seasonal skating destination for visitors of all ages.

Now in its seventh year in Wellington, the event offers a winter skating experience in the heart of the city, featuring music, lighting effects, and sessions suitable for both experienced skaters and first-time visitors.

The rink measures 30 metres by 15 metres and provides approximately 400 pairs of ice skates for hire.
Throughout the season, a range of themed sessions will be held, including:
• Student Wednesdays – Midweek skating sessions with student-focused pricing
• Skate & Date Thursdays – Evening sessions with music and ambient lighting
• Groovy Fridays – Top 40 music sessions to start the weekend

Wellington Ice Rink is suitable for families, groups, students, corporate outings, and casual visitors looking for a winter activity on the waterfront.


Whether visiting for a daytime skate or an evening session under the lights, Wellington Ice Rink offers a seasonal experience in one of the city’s most iconic locations.

Wellington
20 June – 19 July
Location: Queens Wharf
10 am – 10 pm daily
Ice Skating Prices
Adults $26 (13 years plus)
Children $21 (5-12 years)
Pre schoolers $16 (3 and 4 year olds)
Family pass $70
Student night Wednesday 7pm – 10pm $18 Student ID required
Please note: all skaters are required to wear a helmet or Paradice safety approved headband when skating.

Risk Disclosure
Please bear in mind that ice skating and ice sliding is an extreme sport which can result in harm or injury. The risks and hazards include, but are not limited to tripping, falling, collisions and cold exposure. By participating in the activities offered by the Wairakei Estate Ice Rink and MB Century Ice Slide you acknowledge these risks could result in injury and you skate/slide at your own risk.

Keep Yourself Safe
The wearing of a helmet or Paradice approved safety headband is compulsory and we recommend the wearing of gloves. Children 6 years and under only have the option of wearing a helmet not the safety headband. Please follow our rink rules and the advice of staff
Please note minimum age for ice skating is 3 years old.

Tickets are available inside the rink and online www.paradiceevents.co.nz
For more information
Contact Paradice Events
09 281 5645 or 027 233 0972 | events@paradice.co.nz

events.venue: Otari Montessori School, 166 Wilton Rd, Wellington
events.long_description:
Otari Montessori Preschool
Where children grow into confident, capable, and caring people — through play, exploration, and real-world discovery.

We warmly invite Wellington families to come and explore Otari Montessori Preschool at our Open Day.

Come and meet our wonderful teachers, explore our environment, learn about our holistic and well-rounded programme, and see your child in action. Children will have the chance to engage with a variety of discovery activities, as well as explore our purpose-built outdoor deck and playground.
This is also a lovely opportunity to meet our warm parent community and enjoy a conversation over a warm drink and a snack.

At Otari Montessori, we are committed to delivering high-quality early childhood education, supporting our tamariki in their interests and learning about the world around them, while building strong foundations for social-emotional development.

We are also lucky to be situated in one of the most beautiful natural environments in Wellington, with Wilton’s Bush right on our doorstep for children to explore and enjoy.

As a result, our preschool environment supports children to:
• feel happy and secure coming to preschool
• build friendships and connect with others easily
• focus, persist, and stay engaged in what they do
• take initiative and grow in independence
• show kindness, empathy, and care for others

Our programme offers:
• learning through hands-on experiences, purposeful play, time outdoors, and plenty of free play with rich opportunities for social interaction with peers
• a rich and diverse holiday programme featuring arts, environmental exploration, and physical activities, including interactive Kelly Sports games
• weekly music sessions
• weekly bush walks
• a strong transition pathway: Playgroup → Preschool → Primary
• quarterly parent information sessions

This is a relaxed opportunity to visit, ask questions, and get a feel for whether Otari Montessori could be the right fit for your child and family — whether you are new to Montessori or already familiar with its core principles.

Please register your interest if you can, so we can plan for numbers — but you’re also very welcome to pop in on the day, even if you haven’t registered:
https://www.otaripreschool.school.nz/contact-us

We’d love to welcome you.

events.venue: Rewa Rewa Station, 166 Rewa Rewa Road, Tinui, Masterton
events.long_description:
Our on-farm Craft Open Days are aimed primarily at knitters, spinners, crocheters and other fibre crafters.

Nestled in the small rural community of Tinui is Rewa Rewa Station. Operating as a hill country Sheep & Beef breeding farm with a strong focus on NZ Wool & Fibre. Romney, Corriedale cross Romney, Polwarth & Gotland sheep provide the fleeces to create fibre products for crafters, which are sold via the Rewa Rewa Station website, and at Fibre Markets. Our Studio Shop is also open during Craft Days or by appointment outside of these days.

Our Craft Days allow you to work on your own project, seek advice, learn a new fibre skill or maybe just spend time with fellow fibre crafters while potentially ticking off a project or two in the process.

Please bring your knitting, crocheting, spinning, hand sewing, or any project you are working on and enjoy a drive in the country!

Coffee, tea and snacks provided, but bring your lunch and stay awhile.

Everyone is welcome, the more the merrier!

Note: Craft Days are primarily held on the 3rd Saturday of every mont,h but occasionally we do have to juggle the dates.

events.name: Vietnamese Crab Noodle Soup - Bánh Canh Cua
events.venue: 9 Batchelor Street, Newlands, Wellington 6037,Newlands Community Centre, 9 Batchelor St, Newlands, Wellington 6037, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Vietnamese Crab Noodle Soup - Bánh Canh Cua
Join Viet Hub NZ for a comforting winter cooking workshop featuring Bánh Canh Cua, a rich and hearty Vietnamese crab noodle soup known for its thick, silky noodles and flavourful seafood broth.

In this hands-on session, you will learn how to:

• Prepare and season a traditional crab-based broth

• Work with thick tapioca or rice noodles

• Balance flavours and textures with crab meat and fresh herbs

• Present the dish beautifully, Vietnamese style

Bánh Canh Cua is a beloved Southern Vietnamese dish, often enjoyed as a nourishing family meal. Its naturally thick broth and delicate sweetness from crab make it perfect for cooler days.

Participants will cook together, share stories, and enjoy tasting the finished bowl as a group.

To help keep these classes sustainable and support ongoing community activities, there will be an additional $10/person (13+ years old) contribution if you pay online. Walk-ins are accepted but the fee would be $12/person (13+ years old).

This helps cover:

• Facilitator effort and preparation

• Admin and coordination work

• The ability to continue running and expanding community workshops

Please prepare to show your booking evidence before the class

This workshop continues our collaboration with I Love Viet Food and is made possible thanks to the generous support of:

• Hutt City Council

• E Tū Whānau

• Pomare Taita Trust

• Te Mako Community Centre

• Newlands Community Centre

Spaces are limited to ensure a quality, interactive experience.

Come warm your hands, learn a new skill, and celebrate Vietnamese heritage through food.

On Target is your chance to try something completely new, build on your existing skills, or get back into shooting in a safe, supportive and seriously fun environment.
Hosted at the beautiful Boomrock Wedding & Events Venue, this women-only experience gives you the opportunity to try shotgun shooting and axe throwing, guided by experienced professionals who make learning feel relaxed, confidence-building and empowering.

After the session, stay on and celebrate your wins at the fully licensed bar with your new Wild Chix friends – because confidence earned absolutely deserves to be toasted.

events.long_description:
Greater Wellington is developing a long-term plan to guide how Belmont Regional Park is cared for, used, and invested in over the next 50 years. This community drop-in is part of early engagement to help shape that plan.
Drop-in to learn about what the plan will cover, like tracks and access, restoration, landscapes, and visitor experiences. Share what you think is important for the future of Belmont Regional Park.
Whether you use the park often, live nearby, or simply value it as a regional open space, your perspective can help shape the future of Belmont Regional Park.
This is an informal session with the project team. You can come along at any time, ask questions, learn more about the project, and share your thoughts and ideas for the future of Belmont Regional Park.
Find out more about master planning: www.gw.govt.nz/belmontplan

events.name: Meri Hōhepa Suzanne Aubert: an afternoon with Jessie Munro
events.venue: Our Lady's Home of Compassion, 2 Rhine St, Island Bay, Wellington
events.long_description:
Venerable Meri Hōhepa Suzanne Aubert was one of the most remarkable women in Aotearoa New Zealand’s history: a tireless nurse, social reformer, and Catholic nun who dedicated her life to the poor, the sick, and the forgotten. Founder of the Sisters of Compassion, she bridged Māori and Pākehā worlds with deep respect, practical care, and extraordinary courage. This talk brings to life a woman whose compassion reshaped communities and whose legacy still speaks powerfully today.
As part of "Rua Tau Pūaroha | Celebrate Compassion 2026", commemorating 100 years since the passing of Venerable Meri Hōhepa Suzanne Aubert, you are warmly invited to an afternoon with acclaimed biographer and award-winning writer/historian Jessie Munro as she brings to life the story of this extraordinary woman - her life, work, influence and enduring legacy.
Jessie Munro is the author of 'The Story of Suzanne Aubert', the highly commended biography that won the Book of the Year award in the Montana Book Awards in 1997. For her talk, Jessie has chosen four fascinating elements:
- the early New Zealand narrative
- our tightly compressed history
- a meeting of cultures
- a women’s agency.

‘ Always alert, and responsive to her context, Suzanne lived nearly seven decades here in Aotearoa New Zealand, amidst fast-changing societal and political times and places. The strands of her active, wide-ranging engagement are interwoven with our historical fabric.’ - Jessie Munro
This free and informative event invites you to discover a woman of deep faith, sharp intelligence, and relentless compassion whose story remains profoundly relevant.
All are welcome and there is ample parking available.

events.name: Baybayin Workshop
events.venue: 293 Cuba St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
BAKLA presents…
BAYBAYIN WORKSHOP
Hosted by Jas Sabrine
Saturday 20 June
3pm - 5pm
at Thistle Hall, 293 Cuba St
Baybayin is one of many pre-colonial scripts used within the Philippine archipelago, primarily in the Tagalog language.
The word ‘baybayin’ derives from ‘baybay’ meaning shore/coast and ‘to spell’ or ‘to write’. It was part of the everyday life of Tagalogs until its near erasure by the Spanish and eventual replacement with the English alphabet.
Today, we are seeing a resurgence in the use of baybayin from artists of differing mediums, to Philippine government documentation.
In this workshop, Jas Sabrine will guide us through a brief history of baybayin; where it comes from, the origin of its shapes, and how it was used.
You will then learn the fundamentals of the alphasyllabary writing system and how to form words using baybayin.
For this workshop, as it is part of the BAKLA exhibition, Jas will be teaching everyone how to write queer Tagalog slang in baybayin.
No experience required.
Tara na mga bakla!

Free / Koha Entry.
RSVP to get your tickets

Image from cover photo is by Samson Dell.

events.name: Live Art: Ossia
events.venue: Toi Mahara, 20 Mahara Place, Waikanae
events.long_description:
Ossia (Italian for “alternate musical passage”) is a newly formed ensemble built on the idea of musical exploration. Featuring Jess Deacon (vocals), Jessica Murphy (keys, melodica), Robert Kingi (guitar, bass), and Cam Steel (drums, percussion), Ossia creates space for music to evolve beyond its original form — stretching into improvisation, reinterpretation, and moments of spontaneous connection.

Blending jazz-adjacent textures with soul, folk, groove, and a touch of sass, Ossia invites audiences into an intimate live music experience where curiosity leads the way. This is music that listens, responds, and breathes in the moment: familiar songs reimagined, unexpected turns embraced, and musical conversations unfolding in real time.
This event is part of Toi MAHARA’s Live Art programme.

About Ossia:
Jessica Murphy — keys, melodica
Jazz and contemporary pianist and vocalist Jessie Murphy delivers smooth, captivating performances with a soulful, dynamic sound. Born in Nelson and trained at the Christchurch School of Jazz, Jessie blends a rich musical background with heartfelt performances that move effortlessly across genres, creating an engaging live music experience.

Jess Deacon — vocals
Jess Deacon is a cross-genre vocalist and songwriter whose music draws from jazz, folk, soul, and classic rock. An engaging and intuitive performer, her love of music began with an eclectic musical upbringing. Her studies have included cello, piano, guitar, composition, and jazz performance, shaping a creative practice that is both technically diverse and deeply expressive. Jess has fronted multiple bands, been commissioned as a composer, recorded on a variety of projects, and performed at festivals and events across Aotearoa, bringing curiosity, vulnerability, and musical storytelling to every performance.

Robert J. M. Kingi — guitar, bass
Based in Taitoko (Levin), Robert J. M. Kingi is a guitarist and bassist whose music traverses the soulful landscapes of blues, jazz, country, and gospel. Originally from Darwin, Australia, and of Māori and American descent, Robert brings a unique cultural perspective to the Horowhenua music scene.

A graduate of Whitireia with a Bachelor of Applied Arts in Music, Robert combines academic discipline with the instinctive flair of a seasoned performer. His recent work explores the use of live looper technology, allowing him to weave complex musical textures on the spot. From the intimacy of local cafés to the energy of regional festivals, Robert delivers performances that are technically impressive and deeply rooted in the joy of musical expression.

Cam Steel — drums, percussion
Cam Steel is a versatile drummer and percussionist known for his instinctive groove, dynamic musicality, and ability to shape immersive rhythmic soundscapes. A graduate of the Whitireia School of Music, Cam has spent years performing across Wellington’s diverse music scene, moving fluidly between jazz, soul, folk, funk, and experimental music settings.

Whether anchoring a groove or exploring more textural and atmospheric terrain, Cam approaches rhythm as both foundation and conversation — bringing energy, sensitivity, and spontaneity to every performance. His playing is deeply collaborative, driven by a love of improvisation and the shared experience of live music in the moment.

events.long_description:
SOLD OUT: Dark Sky Experience @ Wainuiomata Regional Park
Bring the family along for a magical night under the stars at Wainuiomata Regional Park and help us celebrate the opening of the brand-new Dark Sky Museum!

Set away from city lights, Wainuiomata Regional Park offers a superb dark sky location for stargazing. This special FREE dark sky experience begins with the official opening of the Dark Sky Museum, where you’ll learn about the wonders of the night sky and why protecting our dark skies from light pollution matters.

After exploring the museum, step outside to meet expert stargazers from Wellington Astronomical Society who will guide you through the night sky. With the help of telescopes, you’ll be able to spot stars, planets, constellations, and other celestial highlights visible on the night, including favourites of the southern sky.

Marshmallow toasting, hot drinks and a fun glow wall activity will be available to keep everyone warm and entertained between telescope viewings, making this a relaxed and family-friendly evening for all ages.

Come along to discover the beauty of the cosmos, learn something new, and celebrate this exciting new dark sky destination—no experience needed.

Session 1: 6.15pm – 7.45pm (SOLD OUT)
Session 2: 7.45pm – 9.15pm (SOLD OUT)

This event is now SOLD OUT, if you would like to go on the waitlist please email

events.long_description:
Flesh and Blood - New Zealand Nationals 2026
Flesh and Blood Nationals 2026 – New Zealand

Card Merchant Wellington is incredibly proud to be hosting the New Zealand Nationals for Flesh and Blood this year. We’re excited to welcome qualified players from across the country to compete for the title of New Zealand National Champion.

This is a two-day championship event featuring both Classic Constructed and Draft play for a total of 10 rounds before breaking into our top 8.

Nationals will be hosted at our Store here in Wellington, which can comfortably accommodates up to 120 players with spacious seating.

While the store is located on the first floor, we have private access via a side elevator for anyone with accessibility requirements. If you require lift access or any additional assistance, please let our team know in advance and we’ll be happy to accommodate.

We’re located in central Wellington, with a Wilson Parking garage directly behind the venue, providing convenient parking across the entire weekend. There are also numerous cafés, restaurants, and takeaway options within walking distance. Our team will be more than happy to recommend great spots for breakfast, lunch, or dinner before, during, or after the event.

If you have any additional questions or specific requirements, please don’t hesitate to reach out, we’re here to help make the weekend as smooth as possible.

---

Day One – Saturday, June 20th

Doors open at 8:00am, with the player meeting beginning at 9:00am. We’re aiming to start Round 1 shortly after, around 9:15am.

The morning will consist of four rounds of Classic Constructed, finishing just after 1:00pm. We’ll then take a short lunch break before transitioning into the Draft portion of the event.

Draft seating will be announced at 2:00pm, with the draft beginning shortly after. Once drafting is complete, players pools will be registered and players will build decks before we head into three rounds of Draft to close out Day One.

We expect play to conclude around 6pm, depending on match pace.

---

Day Two – Sunday, June 21st

Day Two will also begin at 9:00am with a short player meeting before jumping straight back into play.

We’ll complete three additional rounds of Classic Constructed, after which we’ll break for lunch after final standings are confirmed. Top 8 players will leave their decks with our judging team during this break to allow deck checks.

Following the lunch break, we’ll invite our Top 8 players back for photos/interveiws (where applicable) before beginning the Top 8 playoff to determine the 2026 New Zealand National Champion.

---

As always, the best-laid plans aren’t immune to delays or hiccups, so these timings should be treated as guidelines rather than exact guarantees. We’ll keep players informed throughout the day if any adjustments are needed.

We’re looking forward to an incredible weekend of high-level competition and bringing the Flesh and Blood community together here in Wellington.

events.id: Sound Therapy, Gong Bath with Hammocks-The Yoga Studio, 6/149 Karori Rd, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Sound Therapy, Gong Bath with Hammocks
events.venue: The Yoga Studio, 6/149 Karori Rd, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join Nick for this therapeutic Gong Bath to unwind from the stress of your day/week/year, while being supported and held by your choice of a hammock. Hammocks and gongs aren't a common mix, but they work perfectly by allowing you to rest at ear level with the gongs, while having the extra comfort of not having a hard floor beneath you. If you prefer, there is space for floor seating along the edges of the studio.

If you haven't been to an event like this before, some of the benefits come from the sounds assisting the brain to reach deeper, more restful brainwave states, while the steady drones invite the nervous system to relax into the rest & digest mode. The sounds themselves are unlike anything else really, and sound like some kind of rich, harmonic, electronic music. Nick uses three medium-large Paiste gongs, full moon Tibetan singing bowls, monochord, zither, percussion, and a singing pyramid, and strucutres the set using his extensive training in Mindful Somatic Therapy and Music studies.

Nick has been producing and playing with music since his earliest teens, having graduated from The New Zealand School of Music, and later with a University qualification and work experience in experiential Psychology, combining those two worlds with events like these throughout Wellington and the lower North Island for the past 2.5 years.

If you live with any of these, please talk to your Doctor first, to make sure the event will be suitable:
-have a pacemaker or other implanted medical device
-live with epilepsy or a sound-sensitive condition
-are in the first trimester of pregnancy
-are experiencing severe or unmanaged mental health challenges (such as psychosis, schizophrenia, or PTSD)

Please bring along anything that'll help you feel more comfortable (pillow, eye mask, blanket, or earplugs if you live with tinnitus).

events.long_description:
The Undercurrent presents Folk & Funk!
Join us for a night of wonderful sonic textures fortified by Traditional Irish Music and Indie-Folk.
To start we have the debut of Múinteoir. Her music takes influence from contemporary Irish folk artists like Lankum and Lisa O'Neill. Her vocals will make you feel the pull of Ireland’s soul from 19,000km away.
Followed by Pohātu's EP release featuring new friends and old. Folk, Funk, and Fun all bundled into one. Good grooves, stupid stories, and heartfelt music. Pōhatu leans funk with an emphasis on the silly. Sounds between Vulfpeck and Kendrick Lamar, with a bit of fun sprinkled in.

10th Grade Tournament

Timona Park, Feilding | Hosted by Feilding United AFC Juniors

Feilding United AFC invites all 10th Grade teams registered to play in Central Football Manawatū to attend the 2026 10th Grade Festival in Feilding.

There is a 10th Grade Cup to be won, with runner-up medals awarded for second place. A minimum of eight teams is required for both awards to be presented.

No academy teams or tournament specific teams to enter.

WHEN & WHERE

The festival will be held on: Sunday 21 June 2026
(Postponement date: Sunday 28 June 2026)

📍 Timona Park, Feilding – Home of Feilding United AFC Juniors

· 8:30am – Coaches Meeting at the Feilding AFC Gazebo

· 9:00am – First games kick off

REGISTRATIONS

Registrations must be completed via Tournify using the link below:

https://tournifyapp.com/live/feildingafc10thgradetournament

Registration fee: $110 per team

The first 16 teams registered by 8th June 2026 will secure a place in the tournament.

RULES

Tournament rules will follow the current Central Football Regulations for Youth Leagues, which can be viewed here:

https://www.sporty.co.nz/asset/downloadasset?id=7eabcc5d-0023-4a42-9383-cb93c07e4814

DRAW & FORMAT

· Teams will play a minimum of four games.

· Games will consist of:

o 2 x 10-minute halves

o 2 -minute halftime

Points System

· Win = 3 points

· Draw = 1 point

The team with the most points will win their group.

If teams are tied on points, placings will be determined by:

1. Goal difference

2. Most goals scored

3. Toss of a coin

If a semi-final or final ends in a draw, the match will go directly to a penalty shootout. No extra time will be played.

REFEREES

Referees will be provided for most games. However, if a referee is unavailable, teams may be asked to provide a suitable person to control one half of the game.

The referee’s decision is final.

POSTPONEMENTS / CANCELLATIONS

The tournament will proceed regardless of weather conditions unless:

· Manawatū District Council closes the grounds, or

· A Health & Safety risk is identified by the Feilding United AFC Junior Football Committee.

Please remember that everyone involved in organising and refereeing this tournament are volunteers. Without them, this event could not take place.

Enjoy the day and the opportunity to watch the kids play the beautiful game!
