events.name: Mindful Kelp Walk
events.venue: 321 Massey Rd, Karaka Bays, Wellington 6022, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Do you care about the kelp forests of Te Whanganui-a-Tara / Wellington Harbour? Does it inspire you, concern you, or simply spark your curiosity?
Perhaps you regularly walk the coastline, swim, snorkel, or dive, enjoy seaweed events, or you are keen to just come along and find out more. This is an opportunity to come together as a community of harbour stewards – something we all are, in one way or another, when we live in Whanganui-a-Tara.
Join us for a mindful coastal walk along Te Whanganui-a-Tara / Wellington Harbour hosted by marine scientist Dr Marjan van den Belt and Explore Your Coast. Part of the walk will be in silence, creating space to connect more deeply with the harbour and our relationship with it.
We will also reflect on the state of the harbour and explore questions about its future. We might look at beach cast seaweeds, explore what’s under the surface or look through a VR headset. We will learn from each other, from the harbour, and from the questions that emerge along the way.
Along the way, you might meet like-minded people, future collaborators, or simply leave feeling inspired.
Registration is free. We'd simply like to know how many people are planning to attend. If the weather requires a change of plans, we'll contact registered participants with an update.
Please note: this is a slow, contemplative walk. The route may include sections of beach and rocky shore, depending on conditions and the group.
Bring: Suitable clothing and footwear for a stroll along the coastal road, conditions permitting, on the beach or rocky shore.

events.long_description:
Craft a beautiful, personalised ring - a perfect treat for yourself or a thoughtful gift for someone special! This 3-hour taster class is designed for absolute beginners, though all skill levels are welcome to join the fun.
You will be guided step-by-step through the core techniques of silversmithing. You'll start by practicing basic texturing, cutting, and shaping with traditional jewellery tools using copper or brass. Once you’re comfortable, you'll move on to crafting your final piece in sterling silver.
In this hands-on workshop, you will learn to:
Measure your finger and cut the metal strip to the perfect length.
Create unique surface textures using a rolling mill, hammers, punches, and even natural elements like feathers or leaves. You can stamp names, dates, whatever you like.
Work safely with a jeweler's torch for heating and soldering the metal.
Finish your ring with sanding and polishing techniques.
By the end of the class, your beautiful, custom-made sterling silver ring will be ready to wear.
This is an ideal activity for individuals, groups of friends, or visitors to the city looking for a creative experience.
What's Included:
All practice materials (copper and brass).
A strip of sterling silver for your final ring.
All necessary consumables (sandpaper, solder, chemicals).

events.long_description:
Weaving Wellness Wānanga at Longbush Cottage: Harvest. Weave. Restore.
Join us at Longbush Cottage for a full-day Weaving Wellness Wānanga — a hands-on opportunity to connect with the land, learn the art of harakeke (flax) weaving, and create your own wellness plan for yourself and your whānau.

💚 Create Your Wellness Plan — Interwoven with the weaving, we'll hold space for kōrero about health and wellbeing. You'll leave with a tangible wellness plan — written, woven, and real — for you and your whānau.

Your hosts:

Whaea Edith Rolls & Leah Hemi — weaving tutors and wellness guides
Luke Gardner — host, Longbush Cottage
Larrisa — photographer capturing the day

Included: All materials, full catering, and your take-home creations.
Spaces limited to 20 participants.

Ticket price: Free - you must book before the day.

events.id: BrainPlay Science for young kids - States of Matter-30 Waikowhai St, Ngaio, Wellington 6035, New Zealand-Facebook
events.name: BrainPlay Science for young kids - States of Matter
events.venue: 30 Waikowhai St, Ngaio, Wellington 6035, New Zealand
events.long_description:
*** Exploring how the world changes ***
In our upcoming States of Matter workshop, children experiment with solids and liquids through hands-on activities and unusual materials that don’t always behave the way we expect.
As they stretch, pour, mix and test different substances, they begin to notice patterns, compare behaviours, and explore how materials can change under different conditions.
It’s less about “learning science facts” and more about:
→ Why does this feel different?
→ How can something act like both a solid and a liquid?
→ What happens if we change it?
These kinds of experiences help children develop curiosity, observation skills, early scientific thinking, and confidence in exploring how the world works.
They also support a deeper learning skill: becoming comfortable with uncertainty. When children experiment, they practise making predictions, testing ideas, noticing unexpected results, and trying again. This builds flexible thinking, problem-solving confidence, and the ability to see “I don’t know yet” as the beginning of discovery — not a failure.
Arrival & discovery activities: 11-11.30am
Workshop: 11.30am-12.30pm
Snacks & social time: 12.30-1pm
Limited to 8 children (ages 3½-6yo)
Location: Ngaio Scouts Hall, 30 Waikowhai street
Cost: $59, all materials, snacks & drinks included
***

events.name: First Burials Tour SOLD OUT
events.venue: 76 Old Karori Rd, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
events.long_description:
SOLD OUT
From 1840 to 1900 Wellington went through an extraordinary period of development and change. A small rugged beach under cliffs was transformed into NZ’s major port, NZ’s largest commercial centre and the seat of government. The Friend’s walking tour 'First Burials - an introduction to the oldest parts of Karori Cemetery' visits the graves of the industrialists, merchants, artists, doctors, lawyers, teachers, politicians, engineers, architects and scientists who made all this happen. We bring to life the early history of Wellington by telling the story of their experiences and exploits. The tour visits the old Public, Anglican, Catholic, and Servicemens Cemetery sections that lie at the centre of the Cemetery. This is a relatively compact area and the tour, though taking up to 2 hours, does not involve any difficult terrain.

The tour visits the old Public, Anglican, Catholic, and Servicemens Cemetery sections that lie at the centre of the Cemetery.

events.long_description:
Climate anxiety is becoming increasingly common, particularly among people who care deeply about the future of the environment and society.

This thoughtful Conservation Kōrero explores how we can navigate uncertainty without becoming consumed by fear, helplessness or burnout. Through reflections on resilience, values and the restorative effects of nature, Dr Ivan Lin discusses how confidence can emerge from staying present and taking meaningful action aligned with what matters most.

Dr Lin is a medical doctor, speaker and workshop facilitator with experience delivering public and professional wellbeing programmes focused on resilience, emotional wellbeing and the relationship between people and the natural world.

This event will be held in the Pāteke Room on the Visitor Centre, with doors opening at 1.45pm. Parking is available outside the Visitor Centre, along Waiapu Road, and at our overflow carpark on Birdwood Street. Zealandia's free shuttle will be running it's usual schedule.

Photo: Scott Langdale

events.id: Silver Clay Taster-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
events.name: Silver Clay Taster
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Join us to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Precious Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants/earrings. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Precious Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!

Included in the course fee is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant or earrings, or a collection of charms - it's up to you.

Extra findings such as earring hooks and chains will be available to purchase (you can also make your earring hooks if you are feeling adventurous).

This class is great for kids also but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany any person under the age of 16.

events.id: Textured Bracelets-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Textured Bracelets
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
This lively, hands-on workshop is designed for complete beginners, but it’s also a great opportunity for more experienced students to enjoy a creative session making their own unique bangle!

Everyone will leave with a beautifully finished bracelet of their own preferred texture.

We’ll begin by experimenting on a sample strip of copper, where you’ll practice creating textures using hammers, punches and stamps. Once you’re confident, you’ll move on to your main project: a 3mm wide flat strip bracelet in either sterling silver or copper, crafted entirely by you from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll learn essential jewellery-making skills including measuring, texturing, soldering, shaping, and finishing.

Students are free to personalise their bangle with textures or stamped designs. This could be a simple hammered finish, decorative patterns, or meaningful words, names, dates, or poetry lines - making your bracelet truly one of a kind.
Beginners will work with the 3mm strip provided, ensuring a rewarding project that’s manageable to complete. Wider metal is much harder to form and solder, so we are learning to walk before we can run ;)

Copper is included in the course fee; if you wish to work in silver, you can purchase it on the day.

Experienced students may choose to challenge themselves by making a wider bracelet from a flat strip or by creating additional bangles in silver wire. (Please note: extra silver for wider bangles is available to purchase at the workshop for experienced students only, and let us know if you wish to go wider so we can make sure we have the strip in stock.)

This workshop is a taster class: perfect for anyone seeking a fun, creative experience with a beautiful result, or for those looking to dip their toes into jewellery making and build foundational skills.

You’re warmly invited to this Winter Solstice gathering on the afternoon of Sunday 21st June.


A space intentionally created for solace and comfort - with cosy blankets, cushions, candlelight, and warmth to gently hold you like a soft cocoon.

An opportunity to slow down, settle your nervous system, and feel supported and nourished through the depths of winter’s longest night.

events.name: The Marriage of Figaro
events.venue: Courtenay Place, Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Mozart’s Masterpiece
Bursting with wit, romance and glorious music, The Marriage of Figaro is opera at its most irresistible.
Widely regarded as one of the greatest operas ever written, Mozart’s comic masterpiece packs one chaotic day with secret schemes, mistaken identities, jealous lovers and razor-sharp humour, all as Figaro and Susanna’s wedding is thrown hilariously off course.
On the eve of their wedding, Figaro and Susanna must outsmart a philandering Count, untangle a web of romantic mischief and survive a household where everyone seems to be hiding something. Clever, fast-paced and surprisingly relatable, it’s a story where the servants are always one step ahead of the aristocrats.
This sumptuous staging from superstar creative duo Lindy Hume and Tracy Grant Lord features an outstanding principal cast from Aotearoa and Australia, joined by the Freemasons Foundation New Zealand Opera Chorus and Orchestra Wellington. Conducted for the first time for New Zealand Opera by internationally acclaimed British conductor James Judd, this is opera at its most vivid, joyful and entertaining.
Whether you’re discovering opera for the first time or returning to a beloved classic, The Marriage of Figaro is pure joy.
“Glorious, life-affirming” – NZ Herald
“A dazzling piece of theatre with extraordinary voices and inspired acting” – John Daly-Peoples
Sung in English with English and Italian surtitles.

events.id: O Vere Beata Nox – O Truly Blessed Night-Erskine Chapel, 31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: O Vere Beata Nox – O Truly Blessed Night
events.venue: Erskine Chapel, 31 Avon Street, Island Bay, Wellington
events.long_description:
Settle into the rich acoustics of Erskine Chapel for this concert of deep listening, sacred voices, and transformation, as we celebrate darkness and the turning of time on the night of the winter solstice.

Featuring the immersive ambient electronica sounds of Tonic Collective; a taonga pūoro quartet with Riki Gooch, Al Fraser, Sam Palmer, and Ruby Solly; and a very special one-off appearance by Orchestra of Spheres performing on gongs, chimes and other instruments.

They are joined by Baroque Voices singing rarely heard works of 12th Century abbess St. Hildegard of Bingen.

This is a vigil of sound, depth and stillness — a space to rest, reflect, and be carried by sound through the depth of winter’s darkest night.

Live visuals created by Erica Sklenars (aka Lady Lazer Light).

– Music Schedule –
Tonic Collective (in the ballroom, between sets, and at close)
Taonga pūoro quartet: Riki Gooch, Al Fraser, Sam Palmer, Ruby Solly (45 mins)
Orchestra of Spheres (45 mins)
Baroque Voices (45 mins)
Grand Finale (15 mins)

Food and drink available at the venue.
This is a licensed event, U18s must be accompanied by a parent or guardian.
The evening will see the audience alternating between live acts in the upstairs chapel and the ambient electronica in the downstairs ballroom.

events.id: The Bible Course-St John's in the City Presbyterian Church, 170 Willis Street., Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: The Bible Course
events.venue: St John's in the City Presbyterian Church, 170 Willis Street., Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
The Bible can feel big, complex, or hard to navigate, but it doesn’t have to. This winter, St John’s in the City is hosting The Bible Course, an eight‑week journey that helps you see how the whole story of Scripture fits together and why it matters for life today.

This is the first time The Bible Course has been run in New Zealand, and we’re delighted to partner with Bible Society NZ as their pilot group ahead of a national launch during Bible Month in July. Over 140,000 people in the UK have already taken part, finding it accessible, engaging, and confidence‑building.

Whether you’ve read the Bible for years or are just beginning to explore Christian faith, you’re warmly invited.

Each Sunday evening includes:
- A shared meal to begin the night together
- Childcare for preschool and primary-aged children
- A 20‑minute video teaching session
- Time in small groups to talk, ask questions, and explore the themes
- A physical guidebook to use throughout the course (optional purchase: $10)

Spaces are limited, registration is essential

events.long_description:
The Paekākāriki Community Trust would like to warmly welcome you, your family and friends to our Film Festival in the St. Peters Village Hall Paekākāriki.

June 14: "My Favourite Cake" (NZIFF 2024) is a delightful, bittersweet Iranian romantic comedy-drama about a seventy-year-old widow who is inspired to have a bit of excitement after years of duty and repression. (Cake treats in house too for a few extra coins)

June 21: "Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk" (NZIFF 2025) is a heart-breaking but essential portrait of life in Gaza during the Israeli military campaign, centred on courageous Palestinian photojournalist Fatima Hassouna.

events.name: Cooking Classes
events.venue: Sheila's Indian Kitchen, Ashton Fitchett Dr, Wellington
events.long_description:
Authentic Indian cooking classes in Wellington with panaromic views over Wellington Harbour.

In each class, you will learn 4-5 recipes like: potato stuff roti, roasted eggplant curry, wholemeal, roti, naan; shahi paneer; dhal, samosa; palak paneer; gourmet chickpeas; vegetable korma; gulab jamun; kheer; mango lassi; masala chai, and many more...

The classes start at 6 pm or 10:30 am on weekends and weekdays with a 2-hour session followed by a dinner or lunch afterwards. The ingredients, copies of recipes, organic karma drink will be provided with a full course meal in a banquet setting. Custom made classes available for gluten free, dairy free and any other food intolerance and dietary requirements.The ingredients, recipes, complimentary organic karma drinks will be provided with a full course meal.

There are 2 to 8 people in each class in purpose built cooking studio. Also a private cooking classes available.

The menu for the class can be:

1) Spicy potato stuffed paratha and roti, rajasthani tomato relish, aalu matter or spicy peas- potato curry, roasted cumin yogurt raita and fresh mint- coriander chutney.

2) Shahi Paneer (cottage cheese cubes with spices and rich tomato-cashew gravy), garlic coriander naan, cumin jeera basmati rice and sweet fragrant rice pudding with cardamom. Also I will teach how to make fresh paneer.

3) Roasted eggplant curry, plain whole wheat chapatti or roti, jeera aaloo or potato curry, Tuar dahl (split yellow lentil) and Basmati rice with homemade pickle.

4) Palak paneer (creamy spinach curry with cubes of paneer), jeera rice (basmati rice with fragrant spices, panjabi chhole or spicy chickpeas curry and mango lassi. Also fresh paneer making.

5) Khadi (chickpeas fritters in yogurt and chickpeas flour soupy gravy), Aloo-Gobhi (cauliflower and potato curry),  savoury wraps with herbs and spices, fresh pickle and basmati rice.

The total cost is $130 per person, this includes ingredient cost. (As an alternative we also sell cooking class gift vouchers.The food options are unlimited and the class provides fresh and best ingredients)
Please contact for booking: indiancooking@xtra.co.nz

So just bring your taste buds! and Enjoy!!

events.name: Monday Eve 8 Week Block - Mixed Levels
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

This class is a mixed-level class, allowing beginners to work alongside advanced students. It is the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

Beginners start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering. Then we move on to making a practice-ring set with a Cabochon stone (cabochon means it has a flat bottom and a smooth domed top) in a Bezel Setting. As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love.

Level 2 students learn to solder more competently on their own using chainmaking as a way to develop their fine soldering skills. They may create a simple stone setting or ring alongside this challenge project so they have something to hone their skills that they are familiar with, as well as taking on a new skill.

Level 3 and above students are encouraged to work on their design skills and try new and challenging techniques. They should prepare to have one or two simple projects they can work on self-directed in class, alongside a challenge project.

This class fee does NOT include materials for any student.

Beginners should expect to spend at least $60 on materials for their ring making project.
All metals and stones as well as quality findings and chains are available for purchase each week in the studio. Students are encouraged to keep their silver scrap and find ways to use it thriftily in future projects!

A note for young makers: those over 12 years are welcome in this class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

During this course everyone will get to design and build their own awesome LED Neon Sign. The sign can be up to 50cm x 40cm and there are a range of colours available.

events.id: Marlene Dietrich in 'The Blue Angel' - Koha Screening with the Wellington Film Society-10 Kent Ter, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand-Facebook
events.name: Marlene Dietrich in 'The Blue Angel' - Koha Screening with the Wellington Film Society
events.venue: 10 Kent Ter, Mount Victoria, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
In cooperation with the Goethe-Institut, Wellington Film Society is delighted to invite members of the public to attend our screening of Josef von Sternberg's 1930 masterpiece 'The Blue Angel'.
This film marked the beginning of Marlene Dietrich's international stardom. Emil Jannings plays a high school teacher who punishes his students for their infatuation with the local cabaret headliner, Lola (Dietrich). Unfortunately, the professor finds himself just as susceptible to the siren song of Lola as his students are, and he has a lot more to lose than they do...
This tale of lust and jealousy was so successful that Dietrich was hired for Hollywood productions before 'The Blue Angel' even made it to American shores. Few can forget her musical numbers in this film, most famously her crooning performance of 'Falling in Love Again'.

With the election approaching, understanding how different political perspectives shape policy and direction has never been more important for business.

Tuesday mornings just got better!

If you enjoy a good chat, a decent cuppa, and the kind of laughter that makes you forget the time, the Karori Friendship Club is for you. We meet at St Ninian’s, 208 Karori Road, Karori, from 10 am to 12 pm, and for a koha you’ll be treated to morning tea and genuinely friendly company.

Ph: 476 7137 for more info or check out our website.

events.id: Between Dreams: Resistance and Representation in Asian Aotearoa-Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, 65 Victoria St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Between Dreams: Resistance and Representation in Asian Aotearoa
events.venue: Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, 65 Victoria St, Wellington
events.long_description:
This panel discussion will present fresh, progressive perspectives on what it means to be Asian in Aotearoa New Zealand. Te Papa curator and editor of ‘Between Dreams’ Grace Gassin will be joined by contributors Serena Lal, Keith Ng and Sapna Samant to discuss experiences of living between cultures and to explore the legacies of New Zealand’s diverse Asian diaspora histories.

Tue 23 June, 5.30-6.30pm
Ngā Pou Ruahine (Lvl 2), Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library
Free event, all welcome.

About the Speakers:
Dr Grace Gassin is Curator Asian New Zealand Histories at Te Papa. Raised in her mother’s Malaysian Chinese family, Grace proudly identifies as a second-generation Chinese (Hokkien) New Zealander of mixed heritage. Grace’s overarching focus is on highlighting the diverse historical and contemporary experiences of New Zealand’s many Asian diaspora communities. Her wide-ranging interests also encompass the politics of inclusion and interpretation that frame our understandings of Asian diaspora histories, and transnational dimensions of Asian Australasian diaspora experiences. She is also a committed delegate for E tū union.

Keith Ng is a Hong Kong New Zealander based in Pōneke. He has been a freelance writer, journalist and data-visualisation specialist for most of his career, and a data journalist for the NZ Herald until 2022. His work has ranged from reporting on politics, public finances and cybersecurity to investigations of companies and hidden assets. He currently works as a data scientist in the public sector, and occasionally as a freelance digital investigator. He was in Hong Kong during the summer of 2019, and he still misses the city’s Museum of History.

Dr Sapna Samant. is a writer, filmmaker, radio producer, activist, GP and single mum. A migrant herself, Sapna tells migrant and refugee stories through her company Holy Cow Media. She has made award-winning content for Radio New Zealand and produced The Asian Radio Show, which played on Radio Live from 2008 to 2012. While her initial filmmaking mahi was through a pan- Asian lens, her activism has led her to focus on making visible the many Indian and other South Asian stories in Aotearoa.

Serena Lal is a liberation led innovator and Fijian Indian girmitya descendant, raised as a 1.5 generation migrant in Tāmaki Makaurau and now living in Pōneke. A long serving member of Asians Supporting Tino Rangatiratanga, she works across cross cultural partnerships, mental health, governance, and community led innovation, and leads Kites Trust, a peer led Tāngata Whaiora organisation grounded in lived experience.

events.id: Jewellery-making in 8 weeks for Beginners-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Jewellery-making in 8 weeks for Beginners
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
This class is beginner level only, with each student following the class project.

It starts Tue 23 June and runs for 8 weeks ill Tue 11 August, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Our popular weeknight classes are the best way for beginners to get into jewellery-making in a lively, warm and friendly environment.

The stone-setting process teaches you many fundamental techniques in one project!

We start with basic ring-making and stone-setting in copper or brass. Students will learn measuring, texturing, shaping, cutting and soldering.

Then we move on to making a practice ring set with a Cabochon stone (a cabochon has a flat bottom and a smooth, domed top) in a Bezel Setting.

As you work through your practice ring and setting, you can move on to working in silver and produce another ring with a cabochon stone that you really love. This way, you will learn the basics as you go on your practice ring, before taking the next step in costly silver.

This class has all materials included in the class fee!

Each student receives a carefully curated materials pack including copper or brass, sterling and fine silver for your ring-making projects, as well as two stones from our supply so you get a good stone for your level of experience.

We have loads of gorgeous stones of a range of colours, and they are all appropriate for beginner settings.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, Afterpay or PayPal on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)

Who are your real friends—and who’s just there to fill space? We’re constantly surrounded—yet still feel alone. That’s not random. Not every connection is real, and not everyone around you actually cares.

events.venue: Te Raukura ki Kapiti, Coastlands Theatre, 34a Raumati Rd, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Kapiti College is excited to present Hadestown: Teen Edition, giving local audiences the opportunity to experience this internationally acclaimed musical live on stage.

Hadestown: Teen Edition blends modern folk and jazz-inspired music with ancient Greek mythology. It follows Orpheus and Eurydice, a young couple trying to make things work in a tough world, alongside Hades and Persephone, who rule over a dark, industrial underworld. When Eurydice is pulled into that world, Orpheus risks everything to bring her back, relying on nothing but his music and his belief in her. It’s a story about love, hope, and the choices we make.

The show is a huge team effort, with around 100 students involved. While many take the stage, others are working behind the scenes on lighting, sound, set design, and stage management. This helps to bring the entire production to life and gives students valuable experience both on and off stage.

events.long_description:
A MUST-SEE new Aotearoa play written by Jack McGee and directed by Campbell Wright!
Adria’s transmission is shot, and she can’t afford to fix it. Her girlfriend, Mel, offers to pay. Mel doesn’t have the money. She asks her Aunt Jennifer. Jennifer is squeezed with the mortgage. Her son Steven owes her a few grand. Maybe she can get that back?
Loosely inspired by La Ronde, Arthur Schnitzler’s 19th century satire about interlinking lovers, Owe follows twelve individuals down a chain of debt and difficult conversations. With crackling dialogue, a sense of humour, and one hell of an ensemble, Squash Co’s newest work casts a wide lens on the cost of living crisis.
The play weaves a sincere tapestry of human interdependence in a world of shrinking wallets, narrowing worldviews, and closing borders. With twelve, short, eclectic scenes, Owe moves fast and keeps you wanting more.
️"Pōneke's brightest young theatre-makers - and honestly, thank god they're here" - Theatreview (on previous work)

The panic is over! Anglo-French avant-pop group Stereolab are indeed returning to Aotearoa in June, hot on the mechanical heels of last year’s brilliant album Instant Holograms on Metal Film. This was the band’s first studio album in fifteen years, and followed their celebrated reunion in 2019. events.venue: Buddle Findlay Wellington & on Zoom,1 Willis Street, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
LEANZ AGM + Keynote by Hon Judith Collins KC
Join us for the 2026 LEANZ AGM, featuring a keynote address by The Hon Judith Collins KC.

About this Event



The Law and Economics Association of New Zealand (LEANZ) and Buddle Findlay invite you to the LEANZ AGM and a seminar (in-person and online) where the Hon Judith Collins KC will present on the challenges and opportunities for local and central governments with technological advances.

Wednesday 24 June 2026
Buddle Findlay, AON Building, Level 17, 1 Willis Street, Wellington CentralOnline attendance also available
Attendees are welcome to arrive from 5:00 pm, with refreshments available from then until the AGM commences at 5:30 pm until 6:00pm followed by the seminar from Hon Judith Collins KC.

Speaker: Hon Judith Collins KC
Topic: Reflections on challenges and opportunities for local and central governments with technological advances
Hon Judith Collins KC – bio
Prior to being elected as a Member of Parliament, Judith Collins practised law in Auckland for 21 years, primarily in the areas of commercial, property, tax and employment law. She undertook governance positions with both private and public entities.
Judith was elected as a Member of Parliament for 24 years and held 18 portfolios as a Minister of the Crown, including Justice, Police, Corrections, Defence, Energy and Resources, Space, Science, Innovation and Technology, Digitising Government, the Public Service, Revenue, and New Zealand's intelligence and security agencies. Judith is a former Attorney-General of New Zealand and has a strong record in advocating for the Rule of Law and comity.
Judith is a past President of the Auckland District Law Society (now The Law Association of New Zealand), and a Vice-President of the New Zealand Law Society. She is an honorary life member of The Law Association of New Zealand.
She is a Vice-Patron of the Vietnam Veterans Association Children’s & Grandchildren’s Trust, an honorary life member of the Long-Range Desert Group, and an honorary member of the Sappers’ Association (NZ).
With an interest in AI, Judith was pleased to have been an Advisory Road Member of the NAOInstitute (Natural, Artificial, and Organisation Intelligence Institute) of the University of Auckland.
Judith holds a Bachelor of Laws, a Master of Laws (Honours) and a Master of Taxation Studies from the University of Auckland, and a Graduate Diploma in Occupational Health & Safety from Massey University.
Judith is a barrister and was appointed a King’s Counsel in 2023. Judith is also an Adjunct Professor of Law at Western Sydney University.

CPD Hours
Lawyers may note that if this seminar is part of your learning objectives in your CPDPR, then attendance at this event can count for one hour of your 10 CPD hours. Please contact a LEANZ representative at the event to confirm your attendance.

Online attendance (Zoom): from 5:30pm onwards

Meeting ID: 590 504 0726
Passcode: leanz2026

events.name: Lost Wax Casting - 6 Weeks Course
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
A fantastic course that's full of fun and inspiration!

It starts on Wed 25 March and runs for 6 weeks till Wed 29 April, 5.30pm - 8pm.

Create interesting designs in wax, then send them off to be professionally cast in metal. Once your pieces are back, you will be taught how to cut, file and shape them into wearable pieces.

Level 1 students: Learn to work in both soft and hard jewellers' wax and send your waxes away to be cast. When they return, you will learn how to clean them up into finished jewellery and/or incorporate them into jewellery in multiple ways. We start with rings, but encourage students to think outside the box!

Level 2 students: Advance your carving skills and learn to set stones in your waxes. This can be done either by creating claws and other settings or trying the cast-in-place technique - an organic, exciting process.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Not included are the casting and metal costs, which vary from student to student depending on what they want to make. Small castings can cost around $7 - $10, and metals are between $0.35 per gram for bronze - $4 per gram for silver. Please see details on our Regular Classes page.

Our booking system asks for payment to be made via credit card, PayPal or Afterpay on booking. If you do not have access to these payment methods or need to pay your course fee over time, please email us to arrange this ;)

events.name: Wānaga Matariki
events.venue: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, 55 Cable St, Wellington
events.long_description:
Wānanga Matariki: Matariki Herenga Waka is a special Matariki evening kōrero exploring the traditions, knowledge and future of waka voyaging in Aotearoa and across the Pacific.

Presented by the crew of Ngahiraka-Mai-Tawhiti and Te Kura Waka, this free public wānanga brings together experienced navigators, cultural leaders and storytellers to share insights into traditional celestial navigation, ocean knowledge, waka hourua traditions, and the intergenerational revival of indigenous voyaging practices.

Through personal stories, cultural perspectives and discussion, speakers will reflect on the past, present and future of waka navigation, and the role of mātauranga Māori in reconnecting communities with whakapapa, te ao Māori and the moana.

The evening features respected speakers and facilitators including Tainui Stephens, Manihera Forbes, Hinerapa Rupuha and Tamahau Tangitu, each bringing extensive experience in Māori storytelling, cultural leadership, traditional navigation and Pacific voyaging.

Suitable for adults, educators, cultural practitioners and anyone interested in Māori knowledge systems, navigation traditions and contemporary indigenous storytelling.

Booking is recommended.

This event is wheelchair accessible. Please note that variable lighting may be used during the event.

events.venue: Wellington
events.long_description:
Everyone is warmly invited to the Thorndon Society’s AGM, featuring special guest speaker Gábor Tóth - you don’t need to be a member or a Thorndon resident to attend!
So please come along, sit through our brief AGM business, enjoy Gábor’s excellent illustrated talk, and stay awhile for a convivial chat. We look forward to seeing you there!

The Butcher, the Baker and the Beauchamps
Katherine Mansfield convincingly evoked the very particular setting of her childhood home, at 75 Tinakori Road, to examine late Victorian class interactions, in her 1922 work of short fiction ‘The Garden Party’.
Local and NZ History Specialist Gábor Tóth has twitched the historical lace curtain to give us the facts about her Beauchamp family’s neighbours and neighbourhood - who really was just over the palings or the pickets? And what was that terrible stench?
Gábor’s entertaining talk, outlining his detailed investigations into the Tinakori Road area’s residents and their occupations in 1900, will not only give you fascinating insights into demography and social history but possibly a newfound appreciation of your neighbours!

events.venue: Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library, 65 Victoria St, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011,Public Library Building, 65 Victoria St, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand, Wellington
events.long_description:
Understanding women’s health across the lifespan: A talk by Lynda Lovatt
In this presentation Wellington-based Menopause specialist nurse, personal trainer, clinician and author Lynda Lovatt asks "What if the conditions we associate with 'old age' actually begin decades earlier?" Through one woman’s story — from age 20 to 80 — this talk explores how hormones, muscle, bone health, pelvic floor changes, stress, lifestyle, pregnancy, menopause, and chronic disease risk shape a woman’s future health outcomes. This is not a talk about fear or perfection. It’s about understanding the female body earlier, recognising the warning signs sooner, and learning what women can do at every age to stay stronger, healthier, independent, and well for longer. This will be a powerful and practical conversation for women of all ages — and for anyone who cares for them.

Location: Ngā Pou Ruahine space (Level 2)

About the presenter/author:

Lynda Lovatt is a New Zealand Registered Nurse, Exercise and Pelvic Health Professional, and Lifestyle Medicine Practitioner. She is a successful businesswoman with a gift for creating outstanding exercise programmes for women to promote safe exercise during pregnancy, prepare them for birth and recover them afterwards. Her Postnatal Recovery Programme won Programme Excellence in 2017, and her Postnatal Recovery Programme for Personal Trainers was awarded finalist for the Innovation award in 2020. Both awards were received at the NZ Exercise Industry Awards. Lynda’s earlier nursing career was rich and diverse, and saw her looking after burn victims and disfigurement, cancer and chronic disease. After Lynda sold her fitness business, she had a strong desire to return to nursing to focus on women’s health aging from Menopause onwards. Driven to prevent the disease she had seen in New Zealand and British hospitals, Lynda started up her own Wellington Clinic. Her mission is to help women navigate menopause, keep healthy as they age and to provide assessment and treatment for incontinence and the genitourinary changes in Menopause.

Lynda’s superpower is her empathy for her patients and her drive to ease the conversation in taboo topics in women’s health to improve health outcomes. Increasingly, Lynda is being invited to speak at corporate events, webinars and women’s business groups on topics such as menopause, healthy aging and pelvic floor dysfunction from fifty years onwards.

Lynda is the author of: 'Lady Talk, A personal pursuit with practice pearls'. Copies of the book will be available for purchase and signing after the event.

events.venue: Ngā Pou Ruahine, Level 2, Te Matapihi, 65 Victoria Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This event will take place in Ngā Pou Ruahine on Level 2 of Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, Wellington Central Library.

The theme of our June musical book club is private lives.

Between the Lines is a monthly early-evening chamber music series and book club that brings music and literature into conversation. Presented in the beautiful setting of Ngā Pou Ruahine in Te Matapihi, the series invites audiences to listen, think, and talk. No prior knowledge of music or literature is required, just a curious mind.

Taking place monthly from April to October on the final Thursday of each month, Between the Lines has been co-created by New Zealand String Quartet, Orchestra Wellington, and New Zealand School of Music. Each month these organisations will take turns presenting a talented group of musicians to perform music and host discussion on a different literary theme. From devil’s bargains to language games, the obsessive tortured artist to the intimate private lives of writers and composers, this book club will delve deep into themes that span across artforms.

Each session will feature carefully selected music and a reading list highlighting the theme of the month. So, arrive solo or bring your book club to Te Matapihi for a new kind of conversation.


The theme of our June musical book club is private lives.

Music to be performed:
Amadeus Mozart | String quartet Kv. 465 “Dissonance”, 1st movement
Leoš Janáček | Intimate Letters, 3rd movement
Dmitri Shostakovich | String Quartet No. 8, 1st & 2nd movement
Felix Mendelssohn | String Quartet No.6, Op.80, 1st movement
Pyotr Tchaikovsky | String Quartet No. 1, Op. 11, 2nd movement
Florence Price | "Adoration"

Optional reading list is available on the New Zealand String Quartet website.

Music and literature both have the power to transport an audience deep into the interior private lives of the composer and author. For our June musical book club, Between the Lines, which will take place on the anniversary of the publication of Anne Frank’s diaries in 1947, the New Zealand String Quartet have devised a programme of music that explores the ‘Private Lives’, secret thoughts, and hidden desires of four composers. Mozart, Janáček, Shostakovich, Mendelssohn, Tchaikovsky and Price each encoded their music with secrets, imbuing their music with a personal significance often at odds with their public personas. Now, by reading their letters, alongside performing their music, we can learn more about these composers’ personalities and appreciate their thoughts, fears, and hopes.

The reading list for ‘Private Lives’ brings together a variety of primary sources – the letters and diaries of artists, writers, composers and people living through extraordinary and difficult times – alongside fiction that utilises diary and letter forms.


Explore the rest of the series:

Thursday 30 April, 5:30pm - Orchestra Wellington - The Art of Conversation (first & second sessions to take place on Ngā Paiaka/ Bleachers on Te Papa Whenua/ Ground Floor)
Thursday 28 May, 5:30pm - New Zealand String Quartet - Obsession (first & second sessions to take place on Ngā Paiaka/ Bleachers on Te Papa Whenua/ Ground Floor)
Thursday 25 June, 5:30pm - New Zealand String Quartet - Private Lives
Thursday 30 July, 5:30pm - Orchestra Wellington - The Devil's Bargain
Thursday 27 August, 5:30pm - New Zealand String Quartet - Outsider
Thursday 24 September, 5:30pm - NZSM - Te Kōkī - Theme to be announced
Thursday 29 October, 5:30pm - Orchestra Wellington - Language Games

events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Our popular weeknight block classes are the best way for keen makers to get into jewellery making in a lively, warm and friendly environment. This class will be held at our new waterfront location, Market Lane!

The course starts on Thursday 25 June and runs for 8 weeks till Thursday 13 August, 5.30pm-8pm.

This class is designed for students who already have some skills and are ready to develop their craftsmanship in a lively, warm, and supportive environment. Guided by our highly skilled tutors, you’ll build confidence, refine your techniques, and gain the satisfaction of making jewellery that reflects your personal style.

If you’re brand new to jewellery making, we recommend beginning with our Tuesday Evening 8-Week Beginners’ Block, which gives a solid foundation in essential techniques before moving on to this class.

At Level 2, the focus is on precision and technique. Students explore the art of chain making, a classic jewellery making project that develops fine soldering skills and accuracy in construction. This project is an excellent way to build confidence with the torch and create a piece of jewellery that is both functional and beautiful. The finished chain can become a pendant, bracelet, or necklace, or you may choose to adapt it into a design of your own.

At Level 3 and above, the emphasis shifts toward creativity and design development. Students at this stage are encouraged to take on more complex projects, experiment with new and challenging techniques, and bring their own design ideas to life. With the guidance of our skilled and supportive tutors, you’ll learn how to push your skills further, problem-solve during the making process, and refine your eye for detail and design.

Evening classes are not just about the technical side of jewellery making - they are also a chance to slow down, enjoy the process, and be part of a creative community. Many students return term after term, finding the rhythm of regular making both mindful and rewarding.

Please note: this class does not include a materials allowance, giving you the flexibility to choose your own metals, stones, or other materials. You only pay for what you use, making it easier to customise your projects and work at your own pace.

Our booking system asks for full payment at the time of registration (via credit card, PayPal, or AfterPay). If you don’t have access to these options or would like to pay in instalments, please email us and we’ll happily arrange an alternative.

Yoga Nidra: Winter Solstice
Yoga Nidra: Winter Solstice

On this threshold moment, as nature gently calls us inward, we join together to honour the longest night of the year.

In this special Yoga Nidra, we respect the beauty of the pause. You’ll be guided into a deeply restful state between waking and sleeping, where the body can fully release, the nervous system can unwind, and the mind can settle into spacious awareness.

Through breath, body sensing, and subtle imagery, we’ll rest in the richness of the dark - not as something to move through,
but as something to be held by.

This is a practice of deep nourishment, quiet reflection, and inner listening

Come wrapped in warmth, bring anything that helps you feel held, and allow yourself to be guided into profound rest.

There will be an amazing plant-based dinner & dessert afterwards - all included in your ticket!

events.long_description:
Cultivating Calm: Positive Psychology & Mindfulness
Cultivating Calm: Positive Psychology & Mindfulness

Develop the tools you need for navigating stress, anxiety, and overwhelm.

Mary Rose Dias - Positive Psychology Practitioner (MSc), Yoga Therapist, and Certified iRest®️ Meditation Teacher - will be leading a nourishing and practical evening exploring how mindfulness and positive psychology can help us cultivate greater calm, resilience, and inner steadiness.

Life can be demanding, and when stress builds in our system, it can become difficult to access clarity, ease, and perspective. While we can’t always remove life’s challenges, we can learn to shift our relationship with stress and develop tools that help us meet it with greater awareness and self-compassion.

Through guided meditation, reflection, and experiential practices, you’ll be introduced to accessible tools to help you:
•⁠ ⁠Regulate stress and settle anxiety
•⁠ ⁠Connect with a deeper sense of inner safety and steadiness
•⁠ ⁠Clarify intentions and reconnect with what matters most
•⁠ ⁠Access practical resources for greater calm and wellbeing in everyday life

Together, we’ll explore grounding practices drawn from mindfulness, meditation, and positive psychology, beginning and ending with guided meditation to support integration and deep rest.

This is more than just developing a mindset, you’ll be leaving with something practical to draw upon long after the evening ends.

Open to all - no prior meditation experience needed.

Plus - there is an amazing plant-based dinner & dessert included in your ticket! Stay back for the good food & great company.

Meet Mary Rose
Mary is a Wellington-based holistic therapist, meditation teacher and yoga practitioner whose work gently weaves together evidence-based psychology, ancient yogic wisdom, meditation practices and a whole lot of unconditional love and respect for each person’s unique journey. With over 15 years of experience in wellbeing, counselling, coaching, yoga and meditation, she is deeply passionate about creating nurturing spaces that support healing, self-discovery and inner calm.

Her heart-felt calling is to support others in accessing greater health, healing and happiness. While based in her birthplace of Aotearoa New Zealand, Mary’s dedication to wellness has taken her around the world, including Hawaii, Australia, Ireland, the Czech Republic and the UK, where she has trained with internationally recognised teachers in yoga, meditation and positive psychology. Through private sessions, workshops, courses and retreats, she offers a grounded, compassionate and holistic approach that honours both modern psychology and timeless wisdom traditions.

events.name: Workshop: A Different Type of Wessex
events.venue: 7 Beauchamp St, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Saturday 27 June 2026
10:00am – 4:00pm (Full Day)
Karori Arts & Crafts Centre, 7 Beauchamp Street, Karori
Cost: $55 for members
$80 for non-members
Taught by: Maria Champion-Forster
Register here: https://weg.org.nz/registration-form/
This is an advanced level colour exercise class. Using Wessex work as your tool, you will learn how the placement of different colours and types of thread impacts your final product. To start the class you will be given a traditional Wessex pattern to stitch. From there you will build up to designing your own stitch pattern on grid paper, which you can then use to experiment with thread colour and position. You’ll come away with a good foundation and confidence to use Wessex in your future stitched pieces.
This class has 12 spaces available.
This workshop includes a catered afternoon tea from 1-2pm.

Materials to bring:
• Fabric – 1 or 2 reasonably substantial fabrics, big enough to fit in your hoop.
• Threads – bring a selection of your favourite threads, 8 to 10 different ones. Look for different textures, types.
• Hoops – either the Nurge No2 or a 22cm circular one. Two hoops will allow you to move between samples, but it’s not mandatory.
• Needles – embroidery/crewel needles sizes 1-5 would be good, otherwise a selection of sharp needles.
• Pliers – may be required to pull the needle through the fabric at the end of the stitching.
• Tweezers/stitch unpick.
• Your usual sewing kit; including sharp scissors (fabric and thread), thimble if used, pins, magnifying glass if used, additional lighting if desired, etc.
• Paper and pen for making notes.
• Felt pens or coloured pencils in a similar colour to your threads. This is to help with your stitch designing (only if you have them; some will be available to use).
• Gay Eaton’s ‘Wessex Stitchery’ book – but only if you have one.

events.venue: Hutt Art Society Inc,11 Myrtle Street, Lower Hutt, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Kintsugi Workshop in Wellington // Hutt Art Society Inc
Re-use, Re-Purpose, Beautify with Gold!! Come along and learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop.

About this Event

After several SOLD OUT workshops in Wellington here is the next one... June 2026
Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)
Saturday 27th June - 10:30am - 12:30pm or 2 - 4pm

Ema Frost is a very clever Kiwi Artist, who has been teaching Kintsugi for 5+ years and regularly travels to Japan to study and learn new techniques. Ema's illustrations and ceramic works sit in many of our countries best galleries, and whose products and merchandise sell in the most stylish design stores and gallery shops. Her style is enchanting - quirky, feminine and colourful, and clearly influenced by her travels throughout the world, usually off the beaten track.
Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.
KintsugiIt's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your knew skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.
What you will take away:A finished artwork pieceA understanding of KintsugiKnowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

events.venue: St. Ninian's Church, 206 Karori Rd, Karori, Wellington 6012, New Zealand
events.long_description:
We are excited to bring you Phenomenal Women. The title of this concert is inspired by Maya Angelou's poem Phenomenal Woman (See extract below):

Pretty women wonder where my secret lies.
I’m not cute or built to suit a fashion model’s size
But when I start to tell them,
They think I’m telling lies.
I say,
It’s in the reach of my arms,
The span of my hips,
The stride of my step,
The curl of my lips.
I’m a woman
Phenomenally.
Phenomenal woman,
That’s me.

This concert is our take on honouring and celebrating womanhood and being proudly and unashamedly ourselves, whatever that may mean. There will be songs in various languages form different parts of the world including Georgia, Madagascar and Hawaii.
You are invited to join us for afternoon tea after the concert.
We are a community choir made of women from different walks of life, different levels of singing abilities and beliefs. We are joined together by our love of singing. We learn and perform modern and traditional folk songs from different cultures around the world as well as original community songs that are inspirational, empowering and connects us to the world.

events.id: Lost Wax in 3 - Soft Wax - Friday Nights-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Lost Wax in 3 - Soft Wax - Friday Nights
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Over three sessions, two weeks apart, create stunning jewellery using the age-old lost wax technique. This is an excellent opportunity for a best friends' outing or a self-care date with yourself!

In the first and second session, you'll learn how to work with jeweller's soft wax to create impressions of natural textures and creatures like seashells, leaves and feathers. We can also use moulds created using Fimo, and press soft wax into them, which will result in amazing pieces!

Then there’s a week's break before the third session, to allow time for everyone's waxes to be cast. The third session covers how to trim, clean and finish your casts, turning them into original jewellery ready to wear!

More advanced students can use these sessions to complete projects in a class setting.

Included in the class fee are all your different types of waxes, sandpaper and courier costs.

Not included are the casting and metal costs which vary from student to student depending on what sized piece they want to make and the type of metal they choose. Small castings typically cost around $6.65–$12, with metal costs ranging from approximately $7 to $30, depending on whether you use brass, bronze, or silver.

events.long_description:
Discover the magic of Mitsuro Hikime — the beautiful Japanese technique that uses a special stretchy wax to create flowing, organic textures unlike anything else in jewellery-making.

Over three inspiring sessions, you’ll learn how to transform this fascinating material into stunning wearable pieces using the traditional lost wax casting process.

Mitsuro Hikime wax behaves very differently from standard jeweller’s wax. Warm and pliable, it can be stretched, twisted and pulled into delicate ribbons and natural textures that resemble flowing water, bark, roots or molten metal. The results are beautifully organic and wonderfully unpredictable, making every piece completely unique.

During the first two sessions, you’ll learn how to handle and shape this traditional Japanese wax, exploring different techniques to create rings, pendants or small sculptural objects full of movement and texture. Once your designs are complete, your waxes will be professionally cast in the metal of your choice.

There is then a one-week break before the final session to allow time for casting. In the third class, you’ll learn how to cut, file, sand and finish your cast pieces, transforming them into polished jewellery ready to wear, gift or treasure.

This course is suitable for complete beginners as well as more experienced makers wanting to experiment with this exciting and expressive technique. More advanced students are also welcome to use the sessions to develop independent projects in a supportive studio environment.

Included in the class fee are all Mitsuro Hikime waxes, consumables, sandpaper and courier costs.

Please note that casting and metal costs are not included, as these vary depending on the size of your piece and the metal selected. Small castings generally cost around $6.65–$12, with metal costs ranging approximately from $8–$30 depending on whether you choose red bronze, white bronze or silver.

This class is great for young folks aged around 12 and up. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
Sip & Kintsugi Workshop in Wellington // The Bond Store Distillery
Come and experience this unique Sip & Kintsugi workshop at the lovely Bond Store Distillery. You will get a gin tasting tray on arrival with three different gins with tonic. And why not come a little earlier and grab a bite to eat beforehand. (Must be 18years +)

Learn the magical art of Kintsugi with Artist Ema Frost in this new Workshop. You can bring along a piece of your own pottery to restore in this beautiful style. (I'll also have a few as back up if you don't have your own piece) (All Levels)

Friday 26th June - 5:30pm - 7:30pm


Ema has been teaching Kintsugi for 5+ years and regularly travels to Japan to study and learn new techniques. Ema's illustrations and ceramic works sit in many of our countries best galleries, and whose products and merchandise sell in the most stylish design stores and gallery shops. Her style is enchanting - quirky, feminine and colourful, and clearly influenced by her travels throughout the world, usually off the beaten track.

Have you ever wanted to try Kintsugi.... It's an ancient Japanese art form where you fix broken pottery with gold - making its imperfections its beauty. - A truly wonderful philosophy to live by. Nothing is ever really broken but new life and meaning is brought back making your piece a work of art and truly something special. You can also apply this technique on various materials like glass, wood, greenstone and shells.

Kintsugi
It's called kintsugi (金継ぎ), or kintsukuroi (金繕い), literally golden (“kin”) and repair (“tsugi”). This traditional Japanese art uses a precious metal – liquid gold, liquid silver or lacquer dusted with powdered gold – to bring together the pieces of a broken pottery item and at the same time enhance the breaks.

You will take away your wonderful finished work, plus your new skills which will enable you to further your own Kintsugi in your own time.

What you will take away:
A finished artwork piece
A understanding of Kintsugi
Knowledge and History of this beautiful art form.

Join artist Sarah Rose for an immersive listening experience set in relation to her sound installation, Redolence.
Drawing on ideas of deep listening as well as the work of sound artist Mark Peter Wright, Rose invites audiences into a shifting sonic terrain, foregrounding a shared act of correspondence through sound. Deep listening, as developed by pioneering musician and composer Pauline Oliveros, is an ethical and perceptual practice, a way of expanding attention beyond the human.

Voices New Zealand with
Conductor: Ana Erčulj

Under internationally renowned Slovenian conductor Ana Erčulj, Voices New Zealand — the country’s premier national choir — presents two unforgettable nights of choral brilliance in a programme infused with warmth and radiance everlasting.
At the heart of Eternal Light is Fauré’s Requiem – music of restraint and consolation, with gentle harmonies that hold grief and hope in balance.
Erčulj also brings music from her native Slovenia, introducing New Zealand audiences to works by celebrated composers, Andrej Makor and Aldo Kumar, Damijan Močnik, and Lojze Lebič. This is paired with a newly commissioned work; ‘Awatea’ by acclaimed New Zealand composer Rosa Elliott.
Set within the soaring acoustics of two of New Zealand’s most iconic cathedral spaces, this concert invites you to experience the unifying power of the country’s finest voices, resonating in gleaming harmony.
Get ready for an evening of timeless peace and resplendence – a celebration of light unending.

Following their Machine Listening [Offsite performance ](https://www.pyramidclub.org.nz/offsite-machine-listening...) at Circuit on Monday 29th June , visiting artists from Naarm/Melbourne, Joel Stern, Sean Dockray and James Parker, will perform an improvised set for self built software and buchla synth at Pyramid Club.
Opening the gig, Joel Stern will collaborate in an improvised, found sound/found object set with locals Chrissie Butler (DSLB), Gerard Crewdson and Daniel Beban.
___________________________________
Joel Stern is an artist, curator, and researcher. His work explores sound and listening as cultural, political, and technical practices shaping contemporary life. He is a Research Fellow at RMIT’s School of Media and Communication, an Associate Investigator at ADM+S, and was Artistic Director of Liquid Architecture from 2013 to 2022.
James Parker is an Associate Professor at Melbourne Law School, who works across legal scholarship, art criticism, curation, and production. He is an Associate Investigator with ADM+S, a former ARC DECRA fellow, former visiting fellow at the Program for Science, Technology and Society at the Harvard Kennedy School for Government, and sits on the advisory board of Earshot, an NGO specialising in audio forensics.
Sean Dockray is an artist and writer whose work explores the politics of technology, with a particular emphasis on artificial intelligences and the algorithmic web. He is a Senior Lecturer in Fine Art at Monash University, a founding director of the Los Angeles non-profit Telic Arts Exchange, and initiator of knowledge-sharing platforms, The Public School and AAAARG.ORG.

events.long_description:
Aotearoa's bluegrass explorers, You, Me, Everybody, bring their new album, Midnight to Wellington.
Rooted in tradition but unafraid to innovate, the band blends virtuosic musicianship with gracious arrangements to create a progressive acoustic sound that reaches well beyond classic Americana. Their live shows offer plenty of toe-tapping energy, yet it’s their creative fearlessness, soaring dynamics and heartfelt storytelling that truly set them apart.
The band’s new album, Midnight—recorded in Wellington with Nashville-based producer Rachel Baiman and mixed by Grammy-winning engineer Sean Sullivan—marks a bold evolution in their sound. Exploring the space between endings and beginnings, the record pairs emotional depth with dynamic, contemporary acoustic textures. With singles arriving throughout 2025, You, Me, Everybody now support the release of the album with a national tour of Aotearoa.
"This album moves & breathes in all the right places" - Jenny Mitchell
"Bluegrass can be exhilarating. It can also be rigidly predictable. On ‘Midnight,’ the Everybody’s go for the former with a lively mix of finely-tuned, unpredictable arrangements" - Cameron Bennett

events.id: New Zealand School of Dance - Choreographic Season 2026-Te Whaea: National Dance and Drama Centre, 11 Hutchison Road, Newtown, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: New Zealand School of Dance - Choreographic Season 2026
events.venue: Te Whaea: National Dance and Drama Centre, 11 Hutchison Road, Newtown, Wellington
events.long_description:
The season lives in the space between who we are, who we think we are, and who we become when witnessed.

NOTE TO SELF is a full-length choreographed performance, created from original short works, devised by NZSD 3rd-year contemporary dance students. Each work has been independently created, then thoughtfully woven together to form one shared performance experience.

Together, these works sit inside the tender and uneasy space of being seen. They ask what it means to be viewed, to be perceived, and how that gaze can shape, distort, reveal, or challenge our sense of self. The season explores the body not simply as something to look at, but as something that knows, remembers, senses, absorbs, and reveals.

Running through the work is a deep humanness - vulnerability, discomfort, identity, observation and the quiet negotiation between who we are privately and who we become when witnessed.

events.name: Virtuosi
events.venue: 111 Wakefield St, Wellington
events.long_description:
In keeping with our season’s theme of COLLABORATIONS, this programme showcases many of the fabulous string-instrument performers in Wellington.
We invite the New Zealand String Quartet to lead our string sections in Edward Elgar’s "Introduction and Allegro," a piece which opens the concert with a big Romantic flourish and a touch of Baroque fugue playfulness.
The orchestra continues its Elgar theme with his cello concerto. Cellist Inbal Meggido, who frequently leads the Orchestra Wellington cello section, steps up to take the solo. This work of emotional virtuosity is a poignant response to the tragedies of the First World War. The music’s emotional intensity holds nothing back, and the cello’s deep, autumnal tone is the perfect vehicle for conveying a sense of both beauty and loss.
The orchestra’s collective virtuosity is on display in Bartok’s "Concerto for Orchestra," a work that gives the audience a peek under the bonnet of how orchestral players collaborate. It breaks the ensemble into solos and pairs and unusual groupings so one can truly appreciate how an orchestra creates the incredible palette of sounds of which it is capable. There are haunting fragments from different solo instruments or groups, soft brass chorales, and elements of Bartók’s mysterious “night music” style. This is one of Bartók’s most accessible works yet it demonstrates his genius, progressing from darkness to light and ending with a formidably complex fugue.
This programme is proudly supported by concert partner The Adam Foundation.
Read more at https://orchestrawellington.co.nz/event/virtuosi/

events.venue: Abandoned Taproom Petone, 38 Fitzherbert St, Petone, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
In a professional musical career of nearly three decades, Charlotte Yates has worn a number of hats, both literally and figuratively. She was part of the comic-musical trio When The Cat’s Been Spayed, with their fruit-festooned headgear and high-camp renditions of Kiwiana classics such as ‘Taumarunui On the Main Trunk Line’.

She conceived and directed the large-scale recording and stage projects Baxter, Tuwhare and Ihimaera, based around the works of three of this country’s major literary figures. She has managed festivals and worked in different roles as an arts professional.

Yet looking back, writing and performing original material has been the thread that runs through her work. “I never thought, ‘I’m going to be a singer-songwriter for the rest of my life’,” says Yates. “I didn’t have the grand master plan.” In 2017 she released her seventh solo album, Then the Stars Start Singing.

events.name: Virtuosi
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre,111 Wakefield St, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Virtuosi
In keeping with our season’s theme of COLLABORATIONS, this programme showcases many of the fabulous string-instrument performers in Wellington.

We invite the New Zealand String Quartet to lead our string sections in Edward Elgar’s "Introduction and Allegro," a piece which opens the concert with a big Romantic flourish and a touch of Baroque fugue playfulness.

The orchestra continues its Elgar theme with his cello concerto. Cellist Inbal Meggido, who frequently leads the Orchestra Wellington cello section, steps up to take the solo. This work of emotional virtuosity is a poignant response to the tragedies of the First World War. The music’s emotional intensity holds nothing back, and the cello’s deep, autumnal tone is the perfect vehicle for conveying a sense of both beauty and loss.

The orchestra’s collective virtuosity is on display in Bartok’s "Concerto for Orchestra," a work that gives the audience a peek under the bonnet of how orchestral players collaborate. It breaks the ensemble into solos and pairs and unusual groupings so one can truly appreciate how an orchestra creates the incredible palette of sounds of which it is capable. There are haunting fragments from different solo instruments or groups, soft brass chorales, and elements of Bartók’s mysterious “night music” style. This is one of Bartók’s most accessible works yet it demonstrates his genius, progressing from darkness to light and ending with a formidably complex fugue.

This programme is proudly supported by concert partner The Adam Foundation.

Read more at https://orchestrawellington.co.nz/event/virtuosi/

Own the Room: Master the art of negotiation strategy, use space to your advantage, and know the unspoken rules.

events.long_description:
Bring your whānau and spend the day exploring creativity, discovering the world of dance, and celebrating the joy of being uniquely you at St James.

Join us for a vibrant and inspiring Whānau Day at St. James, a special event designed to bring families together through dance, storytelling, and creativity. For the first time, this much-loved day will take over Theatre’s multiple spaces across Levels 1 and 2, the stage, and the Hospitality Suite, offering a wide range of interactive experiences for all ages.

This year’s event is inspired by the beautiful children’s ballet The Bomb, creating a day full of imagination, movement, and self-expression.

About The Bomb

Based on the award-winning book by Sacha Cotter, illustrated by Josh Morgan, The Bomb tells a powerful and uplifting story about finding your own voice. It follows a young boy determined to master the perfect “bomb” dive. With the help of his Nan, a former champion, and through learning to trust himself, he discovers that true success comes from embracing what makes him unique.

This meaningful story has captured the hearts of readers across New Zealand and has received multiple prestigious awards in 2019, including the Margaret Mahy Book of the Year.

https://www.facebook.com/watch/?v=389888618397391

A Day for the Whole Whānau

With most activities completely free and something to engage every age group, Whānau Day is a welcoming and inclusive event for the whole community. Whether your child is trying dance for the first time, getting creative with crafts, or watching live rehearsals, there is something to inspire everyone.

events.long_description:
The winter truffle season runs from June through August, making it the ideal time to join and watch skilled dogs in action and savour the rich, earthy flavours of freshly unearthed truffles.

This Truffle hunting experience has you enjoying a relaxed mid-morning hunt through Fiona and John’s truffle orchard of Oak and Hazel trees - Akura Truffles. Accompanied by their trained truffle dogs, they want to share this short but wonderful season and experience with you.

When you've found some of these treasured delicacies, pop around the corner to Le Gra Vineyard and Winery for a fun and interactive lunch inspired by these little black beauties.

You'll learn how best to infuse the truffle flavour into your food, taste some of the Opaki's finest and freshly hunted in delectable dishes, and, if you so choose pair them with local wines.

There are only 10 spots per hunt, ensuring a truly intimate and real hunting and tasting experience. Don't miss out; choose the date to suit your diary now.

events.name: Ōtari Raranga 2026 - Pihinga (Beginners)
events.venue: Ōtari-Wilton’s Bush, 160 Wilton Road, Wilton, Wellington
events.long_description:
Kua raranga tahi tātou he whariki mō āpōpō
Together we weave the mat for future generations

Nau mai haere mai, all are welcome to attend Ōtari Raranga wānanga (classes).

These classes run approximately fortnightly.

No experience required and all materials provided. You will walk away with woven taonga at the end of every class.

During the first 2 classes, beginner students will complete a variety of putiputi (flowers).

We provide harakeke for you if it is your FIRST class and we will teach you how to harvest for yourself during this time and what to harvest for your next class.

After that, if you would like us to harvest for you, purchase the add-on - "Please harvest for me" for an additional fee.

Moving forward, you will start making kōnae (2 corner kete - basket), kono (4-sided kete), tapawhāroa and more.
You will need to harvest 8-10 rau for yourself and start building your own tool kit.

After completing 6 or more beginner classes (close together), you may be ready to move up to our intermediate classes. Please talk with our kaiako and kaiāwhina if you are interested.

With regular attendance, you will:
- Learn tikanga (protocols) and karakia for hauhake (harvesting) and preparing harakeke
- Build your mātauranga (knowledge)
- Use kupu Māori appropriate to raranga practice
- Develop your pūkenga (practical skills)
- Create taonga (treasures) for your whānau
- Build hononga (connections) within our raranga rōpū (group)
- Have the skills to practice at home.

What’s included in your beginner's ticket?
- Three-hour weaving class with experienced kaiako
- Harakeke is provided for your first class, and then you should hauhake (harvest) for yourself or click the "please harvest for me" option in addition to your ticket at least two days before class.
- Light refreshments are provided, and we encourage you to bring kai to share

Led by Irihāpeti Te Aho (Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Kahungunu, Ngāti Pauhawera) , Linda Lee (Ngāti Huia, Ngāti Raukawa, Ngāti Kurī, Te Rarawa, Te Aupōuri), and/or Anna Lees (Te Āti Awa, Kāi Tahu).
On occasion our raranga rangatira, Frank Topia (Ngā Puhi, Ngāti Porou, Ngāti Haua), will teach and we often have support from our kaiāwhina.


Important information
- It is important that everyone turns up on time for karakia
- For tikanga purposes, beginner ticket sales close two days before wānanga, giving us time to hauhake (harvest) for you
- If class numbers are too low, we may have to cancel (and will offer a refund or transfer), so please check your emails before class
- We offer concession tickets for students, unwaged, seniors, and those with disabilities.
- It is important to us that our classes are accessible to all. If ticket costs are a barrier for you, please visit our website to enquire about our reduced-cost or free tickets
- We welcome children aged 10-14, but they should be accompanied by an adult with a ticket

Follow us on Facebook or Instagram: Otari Raranga Weavers
For more information about what to expect and what to bring, visit our website: www.otariraranga.co.nz

We mihi to our funders and sponsors, Wellington City Council, Wellington Gardens and the Ōtari-Wilton Bush Kaitiaki, Maverick Creative, Good Fortune Coffee and Wellington Apothecary.

Donations, Tax Credits and Corporate Gifting
- We accept koha to support Ōtari Raranga Weavers via Shared Lines Trust. This enables us to continue to offer subsidised and free events to the community
- Shared Lines Trust is registered with the Charities Service; Shared Lines Trust (CC61762)
- For corporate gifting or individuals requesting tax credits, please email SharedLinesTrust@gmail.com or visit www.sharedlines.org.nz for more information

events.long_description:
Kua raranga tahi tātou he whariki mō āpōpō
Together we weave the mat for future generations

Nau mai haere mai, all are welcome to attend Ōtari Raranga wānanga (classes). You will walk away with woven taonga at the end of every class.

No experience is required and all materials are provided for your beginner classes.

In your first class you will learn a variety of woven putiputi (flowers). If you choose to continue your learning, your next classes will teach you kōnae (2 corner basket) and kono (4 sided basket) in. On completion of those classes and with practice you will have the skills to move on to other raranga taonga.

Location
Leonard Cockayne Centre, Otari-Wilton's Bush, 150 Wilton Road, Te Whanganui-a-Tara

Upcoming Dates
Sat 30 May 2026, 10:30am–1:30pm
Sat 13 Jun 2026, 10:30am–1:30pm
Sat 27 Jun 2026, 10:30am–1:30pm

For more information and to book your ticket please visit our eventfinder page.

We offer a flexible pricing structure to ensure cost is not a barrier to participation. If you would like to discuss your situation further please get in touch.

We thank Wellington City council for their continued support of our raranga programme.

Mauriora
