events.name: WELLINGTON BREATHWORK EVENT
events.venue: Courtenay Creative,49 Courtenay Place, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
WELLINGTON BREATHWORK EVENT
On Saturday June 27, three of New Zealand’s OWAKEN-trained facilitators are coming together to lead a powerful breathwork experience.

About this Event


WELLINGTON BREATHWORK EXPERIENCE

On Saturday June 27, step into a rare breathwork portal with three of New Zealand's OWAKEN trained facilitators - Jacqui, Hayley and Brigette.

This experience is designed to bring you HOME to yourself. Within this immersive afternoon, the girls will guide you through a breathwork journey that will help you to release stored stress and emotion, regulate your nervous system, reconnect to your body, and access deeper clarity, power, peace and aliveness.
If you’ve been overwhelmed, stuck in your head, emotionally shut down, or constantly running on pressure, this experience is an invitation to move what’s been trapped beneath the surface and come back into contact with your full self.

This is a powerful inner experience designed to help you break through emotional holding patterns, shift stagnant energy, and reconnect to the part of you that is clear, grounded, alive and deeply powerful.

So many people are living with years of suppressed emotion, unresolved stress, internal pressure and nervous system overload in their bodies. We get used to coping. Used to pushing through. Used to overthinking, overriding ourselves, staying busy, staying strong, and disconnecting from what we actually feel.
But there is a cost to living that way. It drains your energy. It clouds your clarity. It dulls your aliveness. It disconnects you from your power.
Breathwork changes that.



Breathwork is a powerful active practice that works directly with the body and nervous system to create emotional, physical, mental and energetic shifts. Your breath is one of the fastest ways to influence your internal state. It can unlock held emotion, shift stress patterns, restore regulation, increase presence, and open access to deeper clarity, truth and vitality.
Because insight alone is not always enough.
You can understand your patterns intellectually and still feel blocked in your body.
You can know what needs to change and still feel unable to move it.
That’s because the body holds what the mind cannot think its way through.
Breathwork offers a direct pathway into that deeper layer. It creates space to release what has been suppressed, process what has been stored, and move energy that has been keeping you stuck. What opens on the other side is often relief, freedom, clarity, self-trust, emotional power and reconnection to life force.
During this experience, people may move through emotional release, physical sensation, energetic activation, nervous system recalibration, grief release, insight, breakthrough, clarity, peace and profound reconnection to self. Every experience is unique, but many people leave feeling lighter, clearer, stronger, more open, more grounded and more fully alive.



This experience is intentionally guided in a grounded, supportive and trauma-aware way.

We’ll begin by sharing cacao and coming together in community, creating space to arrive, connect, and gently open into the experience together.
Then, we move into grounding and nervous system preparation so your body feels supported and ready for the journey. From there, you’ll be guided through a powerful active breathwork experience held collectively by three trained facilitators through breath, music, emotional release and live support in the room. Afterwards, we move into integration, grounding and reflection so your system can land the experience and fully receive what has shifted.
This event may deeply support you if you’ve been:
carrying stress, emotion or pressure for too long
feeling stuck, flat, disconnected or shut down
trapped in overthinking and disconnected from your body
navigating change, grief, burnout or inner tension
craving clarity, release, reset or reconnection
doing inner work but still feeling blocked in your body or patterns
No prior breathwork experience is necessary. Beginners are absolutely welcome.



People often leave feeling lighter, clearer, emotionally released, physically grounded, more energised, more open-hearted and more deeply connected to themselves. Sometimes transformation is not about becoming someone new. Sometimes it’s about releasing what has been sitting on top of who you already are.

IMPORTANT:
Please bring a yoga mat, blanket, pillow or cushion, water bottle, journal, and comfortable clothing you can fully relax in. Creating physical comfort helps the nervous system feel safe enough to open and go deeper into the work.
This is your invitation to breathe, release, move what’s been stuck, & come fully home ot yourself with more clarity, more power and more life inside you.
We can’t wait to breathe with you.


Please note that breathwork may not be suitable for people who are pregnant or experiencing certain medical or psychiatric conditions including epilepsy, severe cardiovascular conditions, schizophrenia, psychosis or recent major surgery. If you have questions about whether this experience is suitable for you, please reach out privately. Your safety is deeply important to us.

events.name: Bike Repair Workshop for Beginners - No Experience Needed
events.venue: 58 Bay Rd, Kilbirnie, Wellington 6022, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Learn to fix common issues and keep your bike running smoothly!
Got a bike but not much experience with repairs?
Keen to learn how to look after it and fix common issues?
Bikespace’s friendly bike mechanics are coming to Karori to guide you through the basics in a relaxed, supportive environment.
• Perfect for beginners and those with a little knowledge
• Learn how to look after tyres, brakes, chains, gears, and more
• Friendly, experienced, patient community mechanics
• First part of the session: Step-by-step explanation of how things work and how to fix or adjust them
• Second part of the session: Hands-on time to work on your own bike with support available, or watch and learn from others
• No equipment or technical know-how needed – just bring yourself. Also bring your bike if you’d like to apply what you’ve learned during the second part of the evening
• Tea and biscuits provided
Recommended from 13 years and older. Younger participants may benefit from parent support – please note that the first 45mins are observing and learning and require a level of focus and patience.
Cost: Registration is $15. At the end of the workshop, you’ll receive a $15 voucher to spend at your local bike shop, Burkes Cycles in Kilbirnie. Perfect incentive to stock up on what you need to keep your bike running smoothly!
Find us on the ground floor of Kilbirnie Lyall Bay Community Centre.
We look forward to seeing you!
Questions? Email bikespace@wcc.govt.nz

events.id: Textured Bracelets-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
events.name: Textured Bracelets
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
This lively, hands-on workshop is designed for complete beginners, but it’s also a great opportunity for more experienced students to enjoy a creative session making their own unique bracelet.

Everyone will leave with a beautifully finished bracelet of their own preferred texture.

We’ll begin by experimenting on a sample strip of copper, where you’ll practice creating textures using hammers, punches and stamps. Once you’re confident you’ll move on to your main project: a 3mm wide flat strip bracelet in either sterling silver or copper, crafted entirely by you from start to finish. Along the way, you’ll learn essential jewellery making skills including measuring, texturing, soldering, shaping, and finishing.

Students are free to personalise their bangle with textures or stamped designs. This could be a simple hammered finish, decorative patterns, or meaningful words, names, dates, or poetry lines - making your bracelet truly one of a kind.

Beginners will work with the 3mm strip provided, ensuring a rewarding project that’s manageable to complete. Wider metal is much harder to form and solder, so we are learning to walk before we can run ;)

Copper is included in the course fee, if you wish to work in silver you can purchase it on the day.

This workshop is a taster class: perfect for anyone seeking a fun, creative experience with a beautiful result, or for those looking to dip their toes into jewellery making and build foundational skills.

Important Note for Young Makers: Kids aged 12 and over are welcome to attend, but anyone under the age of 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio if you wish to make more.

events.venue: Greytown Town Hall, 89 Main St, Greytown
events.long_description:
Kick off the festivities on Saturday 27 June with a spectacular rural celebration. Main Street turns into a Town and Country show of sorts, where you can cheer on your favourite backyard hero in our Ride on Lawnmower Grand Prix, play old school games, and once it gets dark, see the magical lights get switched on for the first time, and enjoy the much-loved Light Up Tractor Parade as it rolls through the village.

What to expect:
- Entertainers throughout the village
- Artisan Night Markets with arts, crafts, food, and festive treats
- Outdoor dining at Truckstop, The White Swan Garden Bar and Food Truck Central
- The first switch-on of magical Christmas lighting
- The beautiful Community Christmas Tree, featuring adorable Ruru Morepork's decorated by local children. Thanks to Greytown Lands Trust.
- Snowfall returns — by popular demand - thanks FreshChoice Greytown! Every 30 mins from 6pm - 8pm
- spin the wheel to win a meat pack

Browse the Night Markets and sample delicious food truck treats, grab a hot chocolate or mulled wine, enjoy the entertainment, the snowfall and festive music through the streets.

Main Street will be closed to traffic so you can roam freely and soak up the atmosphere. Throw on your winter coat or your Christmas jumper and join us for an opening night to remember, thanks to Greytown Lands Trust.

IMPORTANT INFORMATION
Some Festival of Christmas events involve flashing lights and light projections, which may affect people with light sensitivity. Please stay within designated safe zones and follow the directions of our traffic marshals.

events.venue: The Bond Store, 21 Birmingham Street, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Join us for a fun adults’ painting class at The Bond Store – a vibrant distillery in the heart of Paraparaumu, known for its award-winning New Zealand craft spirits. No painting experience is needed – your friendly artist will guide you step by step in a relaxed, judgement-free environment.

This event is all about creativity, conversation, and having a great time while unleashing your inner artist.

Your ticket includes a gin tasting tray, giving you the chance to sample some of The Bond Store’s specialty gins while you paint.

Whether you’re coming with friends, planning a date night, or flying solo, this is your chance to unwind, get creative, and experience the joy of painting with Paintvine.

What is Paintvine?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality canvas, acrylic paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit (or find some at the bottom of a glass). At the end of the night you will leave with your own painting ready to hang up on your wall.

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to the Paintvine website ⇒ paintvine.co.nz

Whether you're a long-time festival regular, a musician, a volunteer, or just folk-curious, come along to our Meet & Greet and share a drink with the crew behind the Wellington Folk Festival.
When: Saturday 27 June, 4pm–6pm (and onwards for those keen to stay)
Where: Welsh Dragon Bar, Wellington
It's a relaxed, no-pressure catch-up — a chance to put faces to names, hear what's brewing for the festival, and connect with others who love folk music as much as we do. We would also love to hear from you about what you want your 2026 WellyFest to look like.
Bring your instrument, bring your stories, and we'll bring the good company. Bar snacks will be provided. The Welsh Dragon is a dog friendly pub and children are welcome if accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.
We can't wait to see you there!
Ngā mihi nui,
The WellyFest Committee

events.venue: 46a Victoria St Alicetown,46 Victoria St, Alicetown, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
Condenser Plays The Cure and Wire
Last year they delivered Joy Division’s Unknown Pleasures to rave reviews.

This year they’re back to perform two more landmark post-punk albums - The Cure - Boys Don’t Cry and Pink Flag by Wire.

Condenser, Wellington’s punk rock stalwarts, have been unleashing sonic assaults and kicking against the pricks since 1980. This trio, composed of James on drums, PJ on bass, and Nigel on guitar, delivers a raw and energetic performance that harks back to the genre’s incendiary origins. But Condenser isn't just a band; it's a culmination of Wellington's rich punk history. James, Nigel, and PJ are all veterans of the scene, having cut their teeth in noted Wellington bands including Condemned Sector, Neoteric Tribesmen, Columbian Necktie and Compos Mentis. These groups, active in the early days of punk, were instrumental in shaping the Wellington sound and fostering a spirit of rebellion that continues to resonate.

Condenser's music isn't just a performance; it's a living history lesson, connecting the dots between Wellington's punk past and its present. The experience gained in their wild youth has coalesced in Condenser, creating a potent force that keeps the flame of punk rock burning bright in Aotearoa.

events.id: Sunday Morning Jewellery-making In 4 Weeks - Mixed Level-Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Sunday Morning Jewellery-making In 4 Weeks - Mixed Level
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
Spend your Sunday mornings immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

It runs from Sun 28 June for 4 weeks till Sun 19 July, 10am-1pm.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

These Sunday sessions are also perfect for returning students and more experienced makers who want dedicated studio time, guidance on more ambitious projects, and the chance to be part of a friendly, creative community.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up. Please note: anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.long_description:
Join us for this fabulous introduction to working with colourful molten glass!

This class is a great way for absolute beginners to get a taste of working with glass to produce beautiful beads that can be used in a myriad of ways, including making a unique gift for your loved one (or yourself!).

As one of the earliest forms of human adornment, beads have long functioned as a way to express individuality, and what better way to do that than to learn to make your own unique beads?

Students are shown correct lampworking techniques to produce several decorative beads in just 3 hours! How many beads you make is up to you; some students make up to 10 while others make fewer using trickier techniques.

Kids over 12 (or so) are welcome to take the class, but anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.name: Silver Clay Taster
events.venue: Toi Pōneke Arts Centre, 3-6 Market Lane, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join us to try out this amazing technique and make a gift for yourself or your loved ones :-)

Precious Metal Clay is an incredible product made from metal particles mixed with an organic binder. When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.

Beginners start with simple pendants/earrings. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!

Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Precious Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!

Included in the course fee is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant or earrings, or a collection of charms - it's up to you.

Extra findings such as earring hooks and chains will be available to purchase (you can also make your earring hooks if you are feeling adventurous).

This class is great for kids also but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany any person under the age of 16.

When your pieces are shaped - just like a modelling clay - they are then dried and fused in the kiln. That process takes only a few minutes so there is plenty of time in this 3-hour class to complete your projects.
Beginners start with simple pendants, earrings or charms. It is much easier to start with flat projects so we leave the rings for the advanced class!
Jewellery pieces can be textured and shaped however you like, and if you don't like your piece simply squish it and start again - Precious Metal Clay is the ultimate recyclable material!
Included in the course fee of $185 ($167 Early Bird Price, ends 1 June) is 5 grams of fine silver clay, enough to make a pendant, earrings, or a couple of charms.
Extra findings such as earring hooks and chains will be available to purchase (you can also make your earring hooks if you are feeling adventurous).
This class is great for kids also but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany any person under the age of 16.

events.long_description:
AUDITIONS for Lettice and Lovage
Lettice and Lovage by Peter Shaffer is a hilarious, satirical comedy about Lettice Douffet, an eccentric, history-obsessed tour guide who embellishes facts for tourists. When a strict preservationist, Lotte Schoen, fires her for lying, the two clash—only to form an unlikely bond over a shared disdain for the modern world.

· Lettice Douffet
An extravagant, imaginative, and highly theatrical former tour guide whose mother travelled France acting in Shakespearean plays. An expert on Elizabethan cuisine and medieval weaponry.

Requires extremely strong comedic acting. Maggie Smith won a Tony for this role!

Stage age 30-60.

· Lotte Schoen
A stern, strait-laced, and unbending inspector from the Preservation Trust. Underneath her brisk, bureaucratic exterior lies a deeply disappointed idealist and secret champion of radical architecture preservation.

Stage age 30-60.

· Mr. Bardolph/Visitor to Fustian House
Stiff-upper-lip, buttoned-down British attorney who is reluctantly dragged into one of Lettice’s extreme historical reenactments.

Requires excellent comedic acting.

Stage age 25+.

· Miss Framer/ Visitor to Fustian House
Lotte’s timid, and obedient secretary.

Stage age 30+.

· Surly man/ Visitor to Fustian House
Hostile history buff and visitor to Faustian House.

Stage age 25+.

· Visitors to Fustian House

Email for the audition sides.

Show run 2-12 September
Rehearsals will be 3 times a week in July and August.

events.name: Environmentality
events.venue: 27 Dixon St, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
"Our devices are listening to us". A lecture-performance by Naarm Melbourne collective Machine Listening in which critical texts about AI are processed in real time.
Admission Free: 30 seats only - Register Here - https://events.humanitix.com/environmentality
What kind of planet would the planetisation of machine listening make? Microphones and loudspeakers are being laced through the biosphere. AI systems monitor forests, oceans, reefs and skies, all in the name of a cybernetic ecology. But who governs this listening infrastructure? Who is heard, and what does it even mean to be heard? What is unheard?
Presented by CIRCUIT in partnership with The Pyramid Club, this lecture-performance by Naarm Melbourne collective Machine Listening — James Parker, Joel Stern and Sean Dockray — bring together ideas from Parker's text The Planetization of Machine Listening (2025) and the collective's audiovisual instrument Konvolute, a tool for composing with cut-up video and environmental datasets in real time. The three artists will critically feed the essay’s argument back through performance and media improvisation to complicate it, testing the lecture’s claims against the grain of the material, letting the software push back, introduce noise, and open questions the words alone cannot quite hold.
Machine Listening is a platform for collaborative research and artistic experimentation, founded in 2020 by Sean Dockray, James Parker, and Joel Stern to subject automated systems to political and aesthetic scrutiny. The collective works across writing, installation, performance, music, software, curation, pedagogy, and radio.
Their work has been presented at major institutions including the Australian Centre for Contemporary Art, Cricoteka Tadeusz Kantor Museum (Kraków), Warsaw Museum of Modern Art, Galerie Nord (Berlin), the National Communication Museum, RMIT Design Hub, and MUMA. They have performed at Unsound Festival, Soft Centre, and Melbourne Recital Centre, among others.

events.name: Founder Lecture: A thousand words: Photographic archives in Aotearoa
events.venue: National Library of New Zealand, 70 Molesworth Street, Thorndon, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join us for the annual Friends of the Turnbull Library Founder Lecture with Auckland Museum’s Catherine Hammond, who will share insights from her work with major photographic archives across Aotearoa.

Catherine's Founder Lecture will discuss the role and impact of photographic archives as complex repositories of memory and research.

Currently Director of Collections and Research at Auckland War Memorial Museum Tāmaki Paenga Hira, Catherine has more than 20-years’ experience working with artists’ archives in major cultural institutions in Aotearoa.

She will discuss the recent book and touring exhibition, 'A Different Light: First Photographs of Aotearoa', and reflect on archives and meaning-making in examples ranging from Marti Friedlander to Frances Hodgkins, feminist photographic practice and whānau portraiture.

Light refreshments will follow the lecture.

Seats are limited, book your spot here: https://events.humanitix.com/catherine-hammond-founder-lecture-2026-a-thousand-words-photographic-archives-in-aotearoa

events.long_description:
Treasury Guest Lecture with Vangelis Vitalis (MFAT): IN-PERSON attendance
The international context for New Zealand trade policy – where we were and where we are – and how do we respond?

About this Event

Join us for the next lecture in our new seminar series
The golden weather for New Zealand trade policy - from 1995 to roughly 2017 - is well and truly over. The world trading system is more turbulent, uncertain and challenging, but New Zealand is well placed to navigate this new world trade disorder.
We will, however, need to double-down on three inter-connected ‘pillars’ of trade policy: rules; resilience and innovation.
This presentation - by MFAT’s Deputy Secretary Vangelis Vitalis - will explain what this means and how it can help us prevent the jungle from growing back.
About this event
This will be a hybrid event. Please use this site to register if you plan to attend it in person.
If you would like to attend it virtually, please use THIS LINK to register.
About the presenter
Vangelis Vitalis is Deputy Secretary, Trade and Economic at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. He is New Zealand’s Chief Negotiator for the New Zealand-India Free Trade Agreement and has led or helped conclude several major trade agreements, including those with the European Union, CPTPP, ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand, China, and Malaysia.
He previously served as New Zealand’s Ambassador and Permanent Representative to the World Trade Organisation in Geneva, and has also been Ambassador to the European Union and NATO. He has held key international leadership roles through APEC and CPTPP host years, bringing deep experience in trade policy and global economic diplomacy.
About this seminar series
New ideas, robust evidence, and insights from leading thinkers are crucial to strengthening the Treasury’s economic analysis and policy advice. Our new guest lecture theme — Navigating Global Shifts: Resilience, Challenges and Opportunities for New Zealand — invites us to reflect on how Aotearoa New Zealand can navigate an increasingly complex and interconnected global environment.
This series explores the major global forces that shape our economic landscape, including evolving trade relationships, geopolitical developments, and the global movement of people, capital, and ideas. Through these discussions, we aim to deepen our understanding of how New Zealand can build economic resilience, respond effectively to uncertainty, and harness our regional and international partnerships to support economic performance, productivity, and our living standards.
Our speakers explore strategies for mitigating the impacts of global disruptions — from pandemics and climate‑related events to geopolitical tensions and supply‑chain shocks – while also examining potential opportunities presented by rapid technological shifts, digital economy, and global innovations, to name a few. The series considers the role of government in supporting economic transitions, strengthening national resilience, and ensuring that New Zealand remains well‑positioned to meet emerging global opportunities. By bringing together diverse perspectives, this series seeks to inspire new ways of thinking about New Zealand’s economic future and to support informed, forward‑looking policymaking.
Please note that the views, opinions, findings, and conclusions expressed in the Treasury Guest Lecture Series are those of the individual presenters. They do not necessarily reflect the views of the New Zealand Treasury or the New Zealand Government.
For updates and our latest research visit: www.treasury.govt.nz

events.long_description:
*TICKETS TO THIS EVENT ARE CURRENTLY ON HOLD*

Gates to Memory is a contemporary dance work that premiered at the Kia Mau Festival 2025. The work explores the connection with entities and embodies the messages, wants, and connection with our physical world.

Gates to Memory invites audiences to witness the intimate act of remembering—of reclaiming lost stories and forging new ones through embodied performance. It is a call to honour those who came before, to hold space for those yet to come, and to respect the ones who will always be.

The strength of this work lies in the unspoken but strongly felt spiritual presence that comes from openness to access messages that are not ours but from ancestors from spirit worlds. To the creators, these messages come in the form of music, movement, and intuition.

Gates to Memory is performed and directed by Caribbean and Brazilian afro-descendant artists Ella Williams and Stela Dara, lighting designer Elekis Poblete and CreaTech sound designers Kevin Licorish and Jeanelle Frontin . All who wish to connect with their spirituality and the cultural intertwining of traditions and entities.

Presented as part of the Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance 2026.

events.id: Weds Eve Jewellery Making - Mixed Level-Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki-Event Finder
events.name: Weds Eve Jewellery Making - Mixed Level
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Spend your Wednesday evenings immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

These sessions are also perfect for returning students and more experienced makers who want dedicated studio time, guidance on more ambitious projects, and the chance to be part of a friendly, creative community.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up.
Please note: anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

events.name: Musical Improv for Performace | A PopRox Course
events.venue: 3 Market Ln, Wellington Central, Wellington 6011, New Zealand
events.long_description:
In this seven week course, upskill your musical improv skills for the stage. Learn simple song structures and refine your approach to rhythm and melody to create banging tunes and heartfelt harmony on the spot.
This course runs 7-9pm on Wednesday nights for seven weeks from July 1st to August 12th with a performance opportunity on the weekend of the final workshop (Details TBC).
Workshops take place at the new Toi Aro community space at 3 Market Lane.
ABOUT THE TEACHER
LIA KELLY is a theatre-maker and musician based in Pōneke. She is an established director, actor, improviser and musician with over a decade of professional work under her belt. She created and directed One Night Band which won 'Most Original Production' at the Wellington Theatre Awards 2023, and her Musical Comedy show Bug Songs not Love Songs won the "Momentous Music" award at NZ Fringe 2026.
THE STAND-BY LIST
PopRox firmly believes that improv is for everyone, especially when it comes to sharing skills and knowledge. So we're offering "the stand-by list" for all our workshops in 2026. We'll giveaway any spots remaining one week before this course, on a first-come-first-serve basis. No need to provide a reason, no questions asked. If the entry fee is a barrier for you to come along, then simply email poproximprov@gmail.com and we'll pop you on the SBL. Everyone on the list will be notified whether there was a place available for them at least 5 days before the course begins.

events.long_description:
Come along for an evening of creativity, community, politics, irreverence and, most of all, singing! Join local Wellington artists Ru Mundy and For Future's Sake Singers, and visiting Palmerston North group the Brazen Hussies in a journey through protest singing together. Sing some well-known protest songs, some new adaptations of old classics, and some original songs, all with a political message. Come ready to sing with us!

Ticket sales cover artists' and event costs, and additional proceeds go to https://triplethevote.nz - supporting 'getting out the vote' for the upcoming election in November.

A reminder: You need to be enrolled to vote (and have up to date details!) before October 25th this year. Remind your friends, family, colleagues, neighbours, acquaintances and everyone you can to enrol and update their details early at www.vote.nz

events.id: You, Me, Everybody - Midnight Album Tour-Whisky & Wood, 60 Cambridge Terrace, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: You, Me, Everybody - Midnight Album Tour
events.venue: Whisky & Wood, 60 Cambridge Terrace, Wellington
events.long_description:
You, Me, Everybody hit the road in 2026 for a national tour celebrating Midnight, their new album exploring the moment where one day ends and the next begins. Recognised as finalists for Best NZ Folk Artist at the 2021 Aotearoa Music Awards, the group has earned widespread acclaim, including a global audience after their song “Stranger” featured in Netflix’s Sweet Tooth.

Founded by brothers Laurence (vocals and guitar) and Sam Frangos-Rhodes (mandolin, fiddle and vocals) and featuring Nat Torkington on Banjo, Rob Henderson on double bass and Kim Bonnington on vocals and guitar, You, Me, Everybody has built a reputation for pushing bluegrass beyond its borders, blending virtuosic musicianship with contemporary folk and modern string-band innovation. Midnight captures the tension and possibility of life’s turning points, brought to life onstage through rich harmonies, bold instrumental interplay, and great storytelling.

“Acoustic, drumless, genius” - Roger Bowie

The Midnight Tour sees the band bring their new album to Whāngarei as part of a 12-date run across Aotearoa.

events.name: MATA MATA - Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance
events.venue: Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
AWAKENING THE TANIWHA, HONOURING THE RECLAMATION. MATA MATA is an offering through the act of solo dance. A summoning of the ancestral spirits that reside deep within the awa. As the taniwha stirs just beneath the surface, memory begins to flow from skin into whenua. Awakening the blood memory that is present here. Becoming a sacred ancestral ritual, allow yourself to slip into this journey of returning. Acknowledging the physical body as a vessel to conjure spirit, mana, and memory. MATA MATA is the honouring of Whakapapa and identity and the holder of space to witness the sacred act of awakening this reclamation.

Presented as part of the Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance 2026.

About the artist:
Harrison Cook is a contemporary dancer, choreographer, and writer of Māori (Kāi Tahu) and Pākehā descent, born and raised on Ngāti Hauā Whenua in the Waikato region of Aotearoa. He is currently based on the lands of the Whadjuk Noongar people in Boorloo (Perth). Harrison is a graduate of the Western Australian Academy of Performing Arts, completing his Bachelor of Arts Dance (2023) and Bachelor of Performing Arts Honours (Awarded a First Class Honours) (2024). During his honours research year, working under the mentorship of Jo Pollitt, he developed and produced his thesis work ’Te Wakahuia: Coming to Know Lineage through Dance Improvisation and Archival Poetics’ which included a body of movement and film work under the name ‘HōtokeWynter ~ ComingToKnow.’ This experience of producing this written and movement practice left Harrison feeling pulled to continue this ongoing artistic enquiry into whakapapa, ancestral memory, and the uncovering of the body as a living archive. His developing choreographic practice centres on research-based improvisation, exploring relationships between land and water, ancestral voice, and embodied lineage. Harrison’s solo work MATA MATA has become a sacred part of his practice and artistic offerings and has been developed and supported through the PILOT Choreographic Program with Enneagon Movement and will premiere as part of The Blue Room Theatre’s 2026 Annual Season through the EVOLVE Program with STRUT Dance. His artistic development has been supported through residencies with The Blue Room Theatre and PICA (Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts), where Harrison was given time and space to continue developing his ongoing practice and project 'THE RETURN'. Through his evolving practice, Harrison continues to explore and understand the connecting to dance becoming a sacred site for remembering, reconnecting, and embodying the stories of our past.

events.name: No One Rides Alone - Film Screening with Q and A
events.venue: Penthouse Cinema, 205 Ohiro Rd, Brooklyn, Wellington
events.long_description:
Special screening of No One Rides Alone the latest documentary from Silvereye Films.

Can someone with Multifocal Motor Neuropathy (MMN) ride the route of the Tour de France? That’s what Clive Phillips and four fellow veterans set out to discover during the Tour de MMN 2025. Following the 1955 Tour de France route, the team set out to see if they could ride in the wheel tracks of the first British Tour de France team

Would they overcome the challenges of the Alps, Mont Ventoux and the Pyrenees? Or would the impacts of this rare disease on Clive’s motor function and strength bring him and the team to a halt?

From Making the Most of Now and the team at Silvereye films behind the award winning “One Day Ahead”. No One Rides Alone, follows the team as they ride around France, connect with the rare disease community and learn more about MMN and the impacts it and conditions like it have.

Featuring double Paralympic gold medalist Ben Watson and Italian para-triathlete Ilaria Brugnoli, No One Rides Alone is a journey of discovery and an intimate portrait of how with team work, positivity and a willingness to be vulnerable we can achieve the seemingly impossible.

Set against the majesty of the French landscape and a remarkable historical achievement. No One Rides Alone tells an inspiring story that has lessons for us all whatever challenges we face. The film aims to raise awareness of MMN, inspire the rare disease community and raise funds for MMN Research.

events.long_description:
‘Set Me Up By The Bar’, the long-awaited new album from Andrew London and an army of collaborators loosely dubbed the Swing Voters, will be officially launched at the Kapiti Playhouse on 2nd July. The band will play all twelve tracks from the new album which includes several of Andrew’s signature satirical offerings about supermarket etiquette, unintentionally falling out with neighbours and the pitfalls of playing in restaurants; some poignant country/folk tunes, and a handful of rollicking western swing-inspired songs that give opportunity for jazz-style improvisation to pianist Wayne Mason, saxophone/clarinet player Oscar Laven and Andrew of course on his trademark 1959 Hofner guitar.

With his ever-reliable partner Kirsten on bass, and the metronomic Ryan Watson on drums, the band will also play a selection of jazz, blues and swing standards from their 2019 album ’Standard Deviations’. There will be joyous swing, satirical mirth, foot-tapping country and even a little beard-stroking jazz.

events.id: A Person Shaped Thing - Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance-Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: A Person Shaped Thing - Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance
events.venue: Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
A Person Shaped Thing is a new solo contemporary dance work by Trinity Maydon, exploring the fragile architecture of Self Perception/Presentation - the process of strategically concealing or revealing information in order to influence others' and our own perceptions on ourselves. Even the person you believe yourself to be only exists for you.

We consciously select different versions of ourselves in different rooms. Each version is carefully calibrated. Each gesture considered. A quiet choreography of revealing and concealing.

Drawing on sociologist Erving Goffman’s dramaturgical theories of human interaction, the work examines life as a performance: frontstage and backstage, audience and actor and the constant maintenance of expression control where we learn to play roles before we even realise we are performing them.

The attentive pupil performs attentiveness
until the performance consumes the listening.

In A Person Shaped Thing, identity is not something created, but selected — assembled from external influences, expectations, and the environments we move through. We shapeshift to fit the spaces we enter, adjusting the mask, refining the image, editing the self.

But the performance is exhausting.

What happens when the masks begin to slip?
What remains when the roles fall away?

As the work unfolds, the body becomes a site of tension — caught between authenticity and artifice, between who we are, who we think we are, and who we believe we should be. In the search to “fit into one’s own skin,” we risk becoming estranged from it entirely.

There is no singular, stable self.
At the crux, we are something harder to name —
An unidentifiable, faceless creature.

Blurring the boundaries between performer and performed

Does the performance ever really end?

Presented as part of the Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance.

About the artist:
Trinity Maydon is a contemporary dance artist originally from Ōtepoti and a graduate of the New Zealand School of Dance. Since graduating in 2024, she has been taking her first steps as a freelance artist, exploring and shaping her unique voice within the art form of dance.

Trinity has always been drawn to the ways in which we use our bodies to tell stories, how we can shape ourselves to physicalize our ideas and express them to the world. She is deeply interested in the lived experience of movement and the connection between mind and body, constantly exploring how embodiment can be a tool for both personal expression and collective storytelling.

Since graduating, Trinity has had the privilege of collaborating on two rave installations with Untitled Warehouse Project— 'Entry' and 'Omnia' (2025). She has also worked alongside Jeremy Beck, teaching throughout Dunedin and performing in Company Beck’s 'Commentary of Dreaming' as part of the 2025 Dunedin Arts Festival.
In 2026, Trinity was immersed in the Fringe Festival, performing in Lyndon Foley’s 'Our Dreaming Bodies' and and was a choreographer in Wellington Community Ballet Theatre's 'Four Questions' in her piece 'Is Santa Claus Real'. She also performed as a guest artist at the Performance Arcade in 'Four Strings – Four Limbs' with Alex Cooper.

A Person Shaped Thing is Trinity’s first full-length work and she is excited to be debuting it as part of this year’s festival.

events.id: Deafheaven & Nothing-San Fran, Wellington-Ticket Master
events.name: Deafheaven & Nothing
events.venue: San Fran, Wellington
events.long_description:
Deafhaven return to NZ with special guests Nothing
American black-metal trailblazers Deafhaven announce their return to New Zealand this July, presented by Banished Music. The band will perform two exclusive headline shows in Auckland and Wellington, joined by special guests Nothing.
Formed in the San Francisco Bay Area in 2010, Deafhaven have spent the past decade and a half pushing at the emotional and sonic boundaries of modern metal. From their debut Roads to Judah, to the genre-defining breakthrough Sunbather, and subsequent records like New Bermuda, Ordinary Corrupt Human Love, and Infinite Granite, Deafhaven have continually redefined the limits of heavy music while confronting themes of alienation, addiction, family history, and self-perseverance.
The tour follows the release of their 2025 album Lonely People With Power. Their sixth album and first for Roadrunner Records arrives as both a culmination and a reckoning , an album that embraces the band’s full identity after years of evolution. Produced by Justin Meldal-Johnsen (Beck collaborator and producer of Infinite Granite), the record captures Deafhaven’s innate ability to merge melody with brutality, and pain with poetry. Through reflections on masculinity, inherited trauma, family, and self-perception, the album grapples with the idea that while we can’t fully escape our past or our nature, we can choose how we move forward. Ultimately, Lonely People With Power stands as one of Deafhaven’s most expansive and human statements.
The album has drawn praise from Pitchfork, Rolling Stone, The Line Of Best Fit, Kerrang and more, and features collaborations with Interpol’s Paul Banks and Boy Harsher’s Jae Matthews.
Revered for their transcendental live shows, Deafhaven have toured the world over, performing at festivals such as Coachella and Primavera Sound, and sharing stages with artists ranging from Slipknot and Knocked Loose to Chelsea Wolfe and Mono. They’ve received a Grammy Award nomination for Best Metal Performance and continue to command a reputation as one of the most compelling live acts in heavy music.
Joining them are American shoegaze outfit Nothing, whose latest release A Short History of Decay has been described by Pitchfork as “fresh and exciting.” Their fifth album and first for Run For Cover Records further expands the band’s sonic scope, delivering the most refined and immersive iteration of Nothing to date.

San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

events.id: Not a Figure of Speech (Side B) - a Screening By Grace Samboh-CIRCUIT, Level 2, 27 Dixon Street, Wellington, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Not a Figure of Speech (Side B) - a Screening By Grace Samboh
events.venue: CIRCUIT, Level 2, 27 Dixon Street, Wellington, Wellington
events.long_description:
Grace Samboh is a curator, writer and researcher based in Yogyakarta. She is visiting Aotearoa as CIRCUIT’s 2027/28 Curator-at-large. Not a figure of speech is a screening of recent artist works from her trans-national practice, some of which feature Grace as collaborator. The screening is followed by a conversation between Grace Samboh and Mark Williams (CIRCUIT).

Presented as a two different but connected screenings in Auckland and Wellington, Grace describes Not a figure of speech as follows; 
 
“Comprising seven works made between 2015 to 2026, this programme takes the form of a mixtape. Not because the works gathered here arrive at the same conclusions, nor because they can be reduced to a single theme, but because I have come to know them through time, repetition, and return. Some of these works emerged from collaborations, commissions, research projects, and long conversations. Others I have encountered repeatedly through exhibitions, screenings, and ongoing exchanges with artists whose practices continue to accompany my own thinking. In some instances, I also appear within the works themselves. This is therefore not a survey assembled from a distance, but a temporary arrangement of works and relations that have remained useful to think with.
 
Over the years, I have found myself returning to artistic practices that do more than represent a question or a social condition. They try things out. They construct situations, however modestly, through which concerns become shareable, structures become visible, and positions become palpable. Rather than asking what a work means, I am often drawn to what a work allows us to experience, inhabit, rehearse, or recognise together. Across the two sides of this mixtape, a number of questions recur in different forms. How does a concern become shared? How does discrimination become visible? What does it mean to remain in relation across differences of experience, authority, generation, or history? At what point does observation become participation? What remains to be done with what one now knows?
 
The mixtape does not propose answers to these questions. Nor does it suggest that the works agree with one another. Instead, it follows a series of echoes and returns. One work leaves something unresolved for another to pick up. Certain questions disappear only to re-emerge later in a different form. Even the pauses between works are part of this choreography, allowing an encounter to linger before the next one begins. A mixtape assumes that sequence matters. One thing follows another, changing how both are experienced. What emerges from that sequence, however, remains open.

I have also found myself returning to works that remain attentive to relation: between people, generations, institutions, and histories. Not because they resolve these relations, but because they stay with the labour of negotiating them. Communication, authority, memory, and care appear differently in each work, yet all of them ask what it means to remain in relation to something larger than oneself. The works gathered here move through a conversation, a choreography, and an act of collective historical care. Across this side of the mixtape, questions return in altered forms, shifting between intimacy and collective life, lived experience and inherited history. A short pause separates the final work from those that precede it, allowing certain questions to linger before they return again through memory, disagreement, and the ongoing work of understanding.

Presented by CIRCUIT with support from Asia New Zealand

events.name: FEVER|DREAM - Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance
events.venue: Hannah Playhouse, 12 Cambridge Terrace, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
BCA presents FEVER|DREAM, a fresh programme of dance and music featuring four newly created works. This mixed bill takes audiences on a journey from intense, feverish moments to dreamlike states, reflecting on today's fast-paced life and the subconscious ways we process ourselves and our experiences within it.

FEVER
FEVER is a high-energy dance work exploring burnout, competitiveness, and the relentless pressure to keep going. Driven by fast-paced, dynamic movement, this piece captures the sensation of being trapped in cycles of productivity and competition — where stopping feels impossible.
PATHS CROSS
In the unpredictability of life, paths cross and intersect, but a singular focus may result in missed opportunities towards an intended destiny.
Through a singular focus, what might we overlook in the periphery? What alternative encounters might have veered us onto a different path and altered our course.
Chance encounters shape our lives, yet unrealised paths might have led to an entirely different existence.
We again introduce a work created by emerging student artists who will explore a ladder of words from FEVER to DREAM. Exploring ways to portray simple concepts from unrelated words through film and performance, graduate and graduating students from the New Zealand School of Dance will bring their individuality to the programme through exploring innovative ways to approach the composition of new movement patterns.
D)rea(m)lity (Dream Reality)
D)rea(m)lity (Dream Reality) is a reflection on our inner worlds, drawing on the interrelationship between a subconscious and conscious state of being. 
The audience is collectively absorbed into a sort of dreamscape, a dance with elusive ideals in the presence of pervasive shadows. Traversing the textures of the imagined and the real, this piece explores tensions between the fears that create voids in our lives, and the illusions that fill them.
Working closely with Jefferson Chen (Goodspace), this is an exchange of bites of movement that Zoe creates with her dancers and Jefferson’s musical response. Pōneke Contemporary Dance Festival will see the premiere of this work, one that will stay in our repertoire for future Festival Programmes, with the aim to present this in Auckland – Zoe’s home base.

Presented as part of the Pōneke Festival of Contemporary Dance.

About the artist:
BalletCollective Aotearoa is a project based dance collective based in Pōneke, Wellington. We are dedicated to exploring new ways to tell the stories of Aotearoa, pushing the boundaries of ballet technique within the contemporary dance space. Collaboration across the arts sector is central to our vision, ensuring that kiwi-trained dancers have the opportunity to develop their artistry at home. Under the BalletCollective Aotearoa banner, we provide a platform for dancers and choreographers to experiment, collaborate, and create new works in contemporary ballet. We aim to bring ballet to new audiences and foster a supportive, innovative environment for artistic growth within the genre.
This year we continue to build a repertoire of homegrown, locally developed contemporary ballet. We aim to present newly created choreography that is both abstract and virtuosic, to highlight the individual strengths of each dancer and their authenticity as contemporary artist’s trained in a ballet technique. We celebrate kiwi ingenuity and collaborate with other kiwi artists to bring you works that reflect the environment we inhabit at this time.

events.long_description:
“Delightful energy, alertness and vulnerability . . . fresh and invigorating” – Theatreview

Improvised scenes are inspired by the anecdotes friends share while sitting on a couch. Stories are told from a place that is truthful; the improvisors take the ideas places that are sometimes serious, sometimes whimsical, always playful. WIT's Improv Lounge structure originates with "The Living Room" developed in Chicago nearly forty years ago by Charna Halpern at the iO Theatre.

The Wellington Improvisation Troupe, aka WIT, is a member-based community theatre group and registered charity, teaching and performing in Wellington since 2003. Our theatre is made up on the spot, usually inspired by suggestions from the audience and each other. WIT players share a love of storytelling and work together as a team to inspire the audience, we’re sometimes serious, often hilarious and always totally unpredictable.

Pay-what-you-can tickets from $5, and door sales. Entrance to the Upstairs Hall is in Arthur St, or through the exhibition space entrance in Cuba Street.

Today The Veils alongside Banished Music announce a 10-date New Zealand tour including 6 band shows featuring the closing show of Strange Universe: Winter in Auckland, and 4 solo performances.

“It feels right to start our Fragile World tour back home in dear Aotearoa. These are some of our favorite towns to play in on earth and we can’t think of a better way to dust off this moth-bitten black suit and hat and get the show on the road. Come along, be merry, and as always come up and say hi” says Finn Andrews.

Arriving just over a year after their last release, ‘Fragile World’ marks a striking shift in tone and energy for the band. Recorded live to tape in New Zealand by Paddy Hill, with production by Tom Healy (Tiny Ruins, The Chills, Folk Bitch Trio), ‘Fragile World’, captures The Veils in an urgent and instinctive mode.

The album’s title is both a reflection of the present moment - a time in which many institutions appear to be crumbling before our eyes - and a metaphor for the act of creation itself. The process of making music, Andrews notes, is a delicate and fragile undertaking where thousands of small decisions gradually coalesce into a finished whole.

“We went into the studio with a lot of songs, but very little idea of the arrangements or instrumentation. It was truly exciting having no idea what this record would sound like and only a few weeks to figure it out. It’s mostly Tom and I playing everything, with Joseph McCallum coming in at times. It was all very instinctual, quite full-on, and scary at times - but a good kind of scary, not scary like the real world out there.”
‍
With its immediacy, intensity, and emotional clarity, ‘Fragile World’ stands as one of The Veils’ most compelling releases to date.

events.long_description:
‘Set Me Up By The Bar’, the long-awaited new album from Andrew London and an army of collaborators loosely dubbed the Swing Voters, will be officially launched at the Wellington Bluegrass Society on 3rd July. The band will play all twelve tracks from the new album which includes several of Andrew’s signature satirical offerings about supermarket etiquette, unintentionally falling out with neighbours and the pitfalls of playing in restaurants; some poignant country/folk tunes, and a handful of rollicking western swing-inspired songs that give opportunity for jazz-style improvisation to pianist Wayne Mason, saxophone/clarinet player Oscar Laven and Andrew of course on his trademark 1959 Hofner guitar.

The Swing Voters are a high energy group who allow themselves licence to extend a song as the mood takes them. This is more than obvious on the ‘Set Me Up By The Bar’ album which features no fewer than four saxophonists, namely Nils Olsen, James Tait Jamieson, Brian Omundsen and Oscar Laven. Oscar doubles on clarinet, James on Irish whistle. Kirsten and Ryan hold down the rhythm section, Mason plays keys on several tracks although Andrew contributes piano to the title track. Pedal steel guitarist Bill Bassett contributes some colour to a western swing song, and the ever-ready Neil Billington provides raunchy harmonica to the rocky ‘Shamrock Hotel’. The album will be available on CD, or to stream or download digitally from bandcamp.com.

With his ever-reliable partner Kirsten on bass, and the metronomic Ryan Watson on drums, the band will also play a selection of jazz, blues and swing standards from their 2019 album ’Standard Deviations’. There will be foot-tapping at the very least.

Andrew and Kirsten are delighted to be launching this album at the Wellington Bluegrass Society.

Welcomer are embarking on their first nationwide headline tour to celebrate the release of their debut album Calendars, out June 12 via trusted DIY stalwarts, Papaiti Records.
Calendars follows a string of European shows in 2025 and a self titled EP which was described by Under the Radar as ‘melancholic splendour.. in swirls of harmonious goodness, each packed with presence and perfectly placed’. Single Nothing of You Remaining was described by Rolling Stone AU as “blending folk influences with strings for a warm, layered pop sound”.
https://welcomer.bandcamp.com/album/calendars
Joined in Pōneke by Belladonna and King Hit
Belladonna is the musical project of Bella Cook, a songwriter with a well-honed knack for musical storytelling, capturing the quirk and romance of everyday life. The debut Belladonna album, Arcus Way, was released in 2025 - a stunning collection of sharp and affecting songs with paired back arrangements.
https://belladonnamusicnz.bandcamp.com/album/arcus-way
King Hit is a Pōneke-based four piece melding the abrasiveness of shoe-gaze and punch of hardcore with the melancholy of Midwest-emo. Originally conceived as a three-piece by principal songwriter, guitarist and frontman Stefan Jenkins, King Hit cut their teeth in the Wellington underground scene for the first half of 2025 before adding Caitlin Gabb on guitar and vocals, joining bassist Felix Bird and drummer Sebastian Bell as architects of the band’s formidable wall of noise.
https://kinghit.bandcamp.com/track/sap
Tickets via UTR

events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Create your own ring stack from copper, brass, and sterling silver in this fun and rewarding jewellery workshop.

Guided by experienced and supportive tutors, you’ll be introduced to the fundamental skills of jewellery making while creating a small collection of rings to take home.

During this 3-hour class, you’ll learn how to measure your finger, cut metal to size, and add textures and patterns using hammers and punches. You’ll also be shown how to solder your rings with a jeweller’s torch, before finishing them with filing, sanding, and polishing techniques.

By the end of the session, you’ll have crafted a thick sterling silver ring and a stack of copper or brass rings, including two plain round wires to texture as you like, and a choice of decorative brass pearl wire or square wire.

This class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends, or visitors wanting a memorable creative experience. Many students find jewellery making a mindful activity, offering a chance to slow down, work with their hands, and enjoy the rhythm of making.

The class fee includes all materials and consumables, such as solder, sandpaper, and polishing materials. Extra silver and other metals will be available for purchase in the studio for those who would like to expand their collection or upgrade one of their brass or copper wires to a second silver one.

Children aged 12 and over are welcome. Anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

Ruapehu Mountaineer
After a sold-out run in February, the Ruapehu Mountaineer is back. If you’ve been thinking about it, now’s the time to lock in a seat.

This is a full-day steam-hauled rail journey through the Central North Island to Mt Ruapehu. You’ll travel in comfortable heritage carriages with large viewing windows, an open-air viewing platform, and a café carriage onboard. It’s an easy, relaxed way to take in some of the best scenery on the network, from the Kapiti Coast through the Manawatū and across the Mangaweka viaducts.

At Ohakune, you’ll transfer by coach up to Whakapapa Village, where you’ve got a few hours to do your own thing. Grab lunch, take in the alpine views, or add on the Sky Waka gondola for a trip up the mountain.

It’s a long but rewarding day, and a pretty unique way to experience Mt Ruapehu. Ideal for families, groups, or anyone keen on a proper steam day out.

events.long_description:
Art Therapy for Well-Being: A Canvas for Self-Discovery
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
Sometimes, our minds get stuck in habitual thought loops—endlessly cycling through the same worries, fears, and anxieties without ever finding a breakthrough. When words fall short, art therapy offers a different language. By shifting from thinking to creating, we bypass the noise of everyday stress and tap into an intuitive visual language that can surprise us with fresh insights, new perspectives, and profound meaning.
This workshop is a gentle, immersive introduction to a pathway of self-restoration, self-compassion, and self-worth—the vital foundations for true self-healing.
What you will experience:
A Shift in Perspective: Break free from repetitive thinking by engaging the creative, intuitive side of your brain.
Tools for Daily Coping: Learn how the simple act of making art can become a sanctuary for processing stress and finding grounding.
A Pathway to Wholeness: Explore how visual expression can reveal hidden strengths and foster a deeper sense of self-care.
Important Note: You do absolutely not need to be an artist or have any artistic experience to attend. This day is about the process of expression, not the final product. While this workshop is not a substitute for clinical individual or group therapy, it is a powerful, supportive introduction to the healing power of the arts.
What to Bring:
A journal and a pen or pencil. All other creative materials will be provided.  Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks and  photo ID.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Mental Health First Aid is an evidence-based workshop which gives people the skills and confidence to have supportive conversations with their whānau, co-workers and community and help guide them to professional help if needed.
You will learn to recognise common mental health challenges, how to provide initial help to someone experiencing a mental health challenge using a practical, evidence-based action plan, and how to respond in a crisis situation. During the workshop you will have the opportunity to practice new skills in a safe environment.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
Mental health challenges covered in the course include:
Depression
Anxiety
Psychosis
Substance use problems
Mental Health Crisis Covered:
Suicidal thoughts and behaviours
Non- Suicidal self-injury
Panic attack
Traumatic events
Severe effects from Alcohol or other substance use
Aggressive behaviours
People who attend Mental Health First Aid training can complete a short online assessment to be accredited as a Mental Health First Aider. You must attend the full two days to be able to do the online assessment for accreditation. The accreditation is valid for three years.
If you choose not to be accredited, you will receive a certificate of participation if you attend the full course. You will also receive a workbook as part of your course fee.
A condition of enrolment is that you must provide photo ID when you attend.

How will an apprentice MatheMagician and a Fire Chief from Kindle save the village from the Flabberfamish? With some MatheMagics of course. A Riotous comedy, with a transforming set and audience participation.

events.id: Refugees (Japan) + Erika Grant & Winterwood-Futuna Chapel, Futuna Close, Friend Street, Karori, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Refugees (Japan) + Erika Grant & Winterwood
events.venue: Futuna Chapel, Futuna Close, Friend Street, Karori, Wellington
events.long_description:
Refugees is the duo of Mary Meacha Goldfish with her partner, Kawol SamarQandi. The project became a platform for expansive, contemplative soundscapes that blend analog electronics, acoustic instrumentation, and poetic minimalism.⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣Mary Meacha Goldfish is a multidisciplinary musician and sound artist known for her atmospheric compositions and her philosophy of “tinnitus music,” an approach that designs organic acoustics while listening attentively to the sound of silence.⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
⁣Central to Goldfish’s artistic philosophy is what she calls “tinnitus music.” Rather than treating silence as absence, she approaches it as a living field of subtle vibration. By designing organic acoustics and listening carefully to internal and environmental sound, she creates works that hover between presence and disappearance. ⁣⁣⁣
Her compositions invite listeners to attune themselves to micro-sounds, resonances, and the fragile boundary between noise and quiet.⁣⁣⁣
⁣⁣⁣
Through a life shaped by kitchens, harbors, choirs, ateliers, and analog synthesizers, Mary Meacha Goldfish continues to craft immersive sonic spaces— music that listens as much as it speaks.⁣⁣⁣

Kawol Samarqandi crafts non-national, “poor” music—stripped-down improvisations built only from his faltering guitar and trembling voice. In this sparse terrain of sound, silence becomes structural, and fragility becomes strength.⁣⁣⁣

For this special event local musicians Erika Grant, and Winterwood will join Refugees for a collaborative improvisational performance.

Saturday 4th July⁣⁣⁣
Futuna Chapel
67 Futuna Close, Karori
2:00pm⁣⁣.
$20.00 waged. $10.00 unwaged

events.name: The Veils - Fragile World w/ Jazmine Mary
events.venue: Meow Nui, 92 Vivian Street, Te Aro, Wellington, 6011, Wellington
events.long_description:
Following the critically acclaimed release of ‘Asphodels’ in 2025, The Veils quickly return with a bold and invigorated new album titled ‘Fragile World’, out June 19 on V2 Records. Today, The Veils alongside Banished Music announce a 10-date New Zealand tour including 6 band shows featuring the closing show of Strange Universe: Winter in Auckland, and 4 solo performances.

“It feels right to start our Fragile World tour back home in dear Aotearoa. These are some of our favourite towns to play in on earth, and we can’t think of a better way to dust off this moth-bitten black suit and hat and get the show on the road. Come along, be merry, and as always, come up and say hi,” says Finn Andrews.

Arriving just over a year after their last release, ‘Fragile World’ marks a striking shift in tone and energy for the band. Recorded live to tape in New Zealand by Paddy Hill, with production by Tom Healy (Tiny Ruins, The Chills, Folk Bitch Trio), ‘Fragile World’ captures The Veils in an urgent and instinctive mode.

The album’s title is both a reflection of the present moment - a time in which many institutions appear to be crumbling before our eyes - and a metaphor for the act of creation itself. The process of making music, Andrews notes, is a delicate and fragile undertaking where thousands of small decisions gradually coalesce into a finished whole.

“We went into the studio with a lot of songs, but very little idea of the arrangements or instrumentation. It was truly exciting, having no idea what this record would sound like and only a few weeks to figure it out. It’s mostly Tom and me playing everything, with Joseph McCallum coming in at times. It was all very instinctual, quite full-on, and scary at times - but a good kind of scary, not scary like the real world out there.”
‍
With its immediacy, intensity, and emotional clarity, ‘Fragile World’ stands as one of The Veils’ most compelling releases to date.

events.id: A Change Is Coming: Journey to Homosexual Law Reform presentation-Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, 65 Victoria St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: A Change Is Coming: Journey to Homosexual Law Reform presentation
events.venue: Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui, 65 Victoria St, Wellington
events.long_description:
In July 2026, New Zealand marks 40 years since the passing of the Homosexual Law Reform Act 1986, a landmark change that decriminalised sex between consenting adult men and helped reshape the lives of rainbow communities across the country.

Join Walk Tours NZ and Wellington City Libraries for A Change Is Coming: Journey to Homosexual Law Reform, a powerful one-hour presentation tracing the long and difficult road to reform, presented at Te Matapihi ki te Ao Nui Central Library.

Blending live storytelling, historic images, archival audio and personal memories, the presentation begins in 1967 with the first public meeting in New Zealand calling for homosexual law reform, held in what is now City Gallery Wellington. From there, it follows some of the social, political and personal struggles that led to the historic law change of 9 July 1986.
The presentation explores the realities many rainbow people faced before reform, including criminalisation, discrimination, police surveillance, medical stigma, religious condemnation and social exclusion.

At times confronting, but ultimately uplifting, A Change Is Coming is a celebration of resilience, protest, courage and community. It honours the activists, allies and rainbow communities whose determination helped transform New Zealand society, and whose legacy continues to shape our future.

Learn the basic technique first in copper or brass, and then craft your final piece in silver!

Over this taster class, you’ll be guided through the process of heating and texturing metal, cutting and shaping with traditional jewellery tools. Use feathers, leaves, or fabrics to create a unique texture for a beautiful ring!

Learn to measure your finger, cut metal to length and texture it without rolling mill, hammers and punches. Then use a jewellers torch, sandpaper and polishing, and your beautiful new ring will be ready to wear.

This 3-hour class is ideal for beginners, groups of friends and visitors to the city.

Included in the class fee are copper and brass for practising on, a sterling silver ring strip and all consumables such as sandpaper, solder and chemicals. Extra metals are available for purchase in the studio.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but any person under the age of 16 must be accompanied by adults.

events.name: Titanium Earrings
events.venue: Workspace Studios Wellington Market Lane, 3 Market Lane, Wellington Cenral, Wellington
events.long_description:
In this super-fast 3-hour class, you will make a pair of earrings fit for a superhero!

Titanium is an amazingly light metal that can transform from a subtle grey to a whole range of super vibrant, or sleek and pale colours, from gold, pink, purple or deep blue, to light blue, palest green and subtle grey.

You’ll begin by practising fundamental metalworking techniques on copper, then experiment with flame-colouring titanium to understand how heat transforms its surface. With these skills, you’ll craft your own earrings, exploring texture and colour.

We’ll use a rolling mill to imprint natural or abstract patterns into the titanium sheet, shaping pieces into clean geometric forms—rectangles, diamonds, triangles, or squares. You can also experiment with layering elements for added depth and variation.

Finish your design with a choice of comfortable hooks or hoops, and leave with a unique, wearable piece.

Titanium is hypoallergenic, and your findings options include surgical stainless steel and gold-plated stainless steel.

You should take this class:
- If you like large earrings that are bold and badass
- If you like earrings to be feather light
- If you like colourful earrings that will really make a statement
- If you like pastel blues and simple shapes
- If you love earrings and want to try something new
- If you’re curious to learn more about using Titanium in your jewellery making - this is an ideal way to dip your toes.

Kids aged 12 (or so) are welcome to attend the class, but an enrolled parent or caregiver must accompany anyone under the age of 16

events.long_description:
The Rogue's regular Sunday afternoon jazz. Funky, jazzy, soulful jazz. Beer, hangs, and jazz, on a Sunday, perfect!

This week featuring Australian saxophonist Andy Sugg with his quartet

Leading Australian sax player, Andy Sugg, is touring NZ in July and he’s assembled a stellar line-up of NZ jazzers—Roger Mannins (tenor sax), Umar Zakaria (bass) and Mark Lockett (drums)—to play with. This will be the first time this formation has played together.



Also premiering are a collection of Andy’s original tunes, which together with some choice standards, make great vehicles for improvisation in the best tradition of contemporary jazz.



Andy and Roger’s collaboration goes back a long way, starting with the powerhouse three-sax group TTTenor (which also included John Mackey) and continuing more recently with the band led by American bass heavyweight, Gene Perla. Andy and Roger share great respect and admiration for each other’s playing. On stage they challenge and spur each other on. It makes for fiery music-making.”

Music from 5pm, FREE ENTRY

events.id: Fundamentals of Drawing - Creative Arts Holiday Programme-Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Fundamentals of Drawing - Creative Arts Holiday Programme
events.venue: Inverlochy Art School, 3 Inverlochy Place, Wellington
events.long_description:
In this two day course you will learn the basics of structure and perspective so you can draw anything you like. Returning students are assigned additional challenges in order to promote continuous development of their drawing journey.

We'll be drawing on paper with pencils and pens. There's a strong emphasis on learning structure and perspective drawing, with the aim to feel more confident in drawing anything - real or imagined. We will be drawing things from real life, from photos and from our imagination.

What you will learn in the class.

- Perspective - learning the basics to help draw forms and spaces convincingly.
- Using perspective to draw organic forms.
- The structure of human faces - Constructing the face to understand it.
- The structure of human figures - Drawing the body from the skeleton out.
- The structure of animal and creature bodies - Seeing the similarities to humans.
- Shading and shadows - Understanding light as it hits objects.
- Composition - Arranging elements in your picture.
- Using different B&W mediums like pencils, pens, inks.

This course is catered to ages 10 years or older. Basic materials provided.

Mon & Tues, 6 & 7 July, 10-1pm

Our artist guides you step-by-step, so absolutely no art experience is needed. It’s the perfect excuse to switch off, get creative, and try something a little different.

Whether you’re coming along solo, planning a date night, or organising a catch-up with friends, Paintvine is all about good vibes, creativity, and having fun while you paint – you might even surprise yourself with what you can create!

events.long_description:
Wellington Community Ballet Theatre is hosting a movie night to raise funds for our next production. Join us for a movie about art to support the arts! Our next show, "Winter's Saga", is contemporary dance based on Norse mythology. The show is on 18-23 August at the Hannah Playhouse and tickets are available through Eventfinda.

The latest film from one of cinema’s most prolific directors, Steven Soderbergh (Black Bag, Ocean’s Eleven), The Christophers is a richly comedic exploration of art and legacy led by a magnetic paring of Ian McKellen and Michaela Coel (Mother Mary).

Close to completely giving up on her artistic career, Lori (Coel) works out of a food truck whenever she’s not doing freelance restoration. But when she gets approached by the estranged children of renowned painter Julian Sklar (McKellen) with an offer to forge his abandoned paintings so they can collect the inheritance once he passes, she accepts. Ingratiating herself into Julian’s life under the guise of being an assistant, Lori’s ruse makes way for a constant battle of wits, twists, and shifting allegiances as they delve into deviousness to reveal thorny truths about artistic integrity.

"The double act of McKellen and Coel has the onscreen chemistry of the year"
★★★★★ - THE GUARDIAN

Content warning: rated M for offensive language
