events.name: Book Group: The Odyssey by Homer
events.venue: The Library, 1/53 Courtenay Place, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
The Odyssey is one of the foundational works of literature, an enduring narrative that has been told and retold. The work is one of two major epics of ancient Greek literature attributed to Homer. (The other, of course, is The Illiad.)

After ten years fighting in the Trojan War, Odysseus, the cunning king of Ithaca, can finally set sail for home, where his wife, Penelope, and son, Telemachus - only a baby when Odysseus left for Troy - are waiting for him. However, further perils await as our hero battles gods, monsters and himself during his ten-year struggle to return home.

Beyond literature, The Odyssey has been adapted for the stage, for symphonies, ballets and operas, as well as many film and TV adaptations. In fact, in mid-July Christopher Nolan's major feature film of The Odyssey will hit the screens - we'll have to arrange an outing.

Do you keep meaning to read more of the great classics? At Wellington Classic Literature Club, we read works that have stood the test of time, whether they were written in 1780, 1880 or even 1980. We meet on the first Tuesday of the month.

RSVP
Bookings essential. Get your free ticket by clicking 'Register' above. Limited places.

If you've signed up, but things change and you're not going to be able to make it along, please email classiclitwgtn@gmail.com as we may be able to make more spaces available for others.

VENUE
We meet in the ‘Games Room’, The Library bar's private area overlooking Courtenay Place. After you enter the bar, head to your right (up the step) and through a smaller space with booths to the large carpeted space beyond (behind the big wooden sliding door).

ABOUT US
Wellington Classic Literature Club has been running for more than a decade - since the start of 2013 - and we have a great bunch of regulars as well as readers who join us for particular books or simply when it suits.

events.id: InBetween Nowhere and Everything-BATS Theatre, 1 Kent Tce, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: InBetween Nowhere and Everything
events.venue: BATS Theatre, 1 Kent Tce, Wellington
events.long_description:
Inbetween Nowhere and Everything is a play about cowboys... in space. It plays upon the traditional tropes of the old west; identity, survival, and camaraderie - but through the lens of an expansive science fiction world.

Set in a distant future where stardust is fuel and war is a commonplace, we follow three strangers, a Lover (Alex Quinn), a Killer (Zoe Harris) and a Nobody (Simon Ulm) as they find shelter within an escape pod and are flung into the deepest recesses of empty space, far from any soul or star.

As these strangers float through a haunting and isolating cosmos, they start to find solace in each other, sharing their cowboy songs and stories around the proverbial campfire. Throughout these stories, their pasts and true selves become unveiled with the help of a fourth character, the enigmatic and shadowy THEM (Míren Welsh Ahipene Duffin).

Throughout these stories however, these three strangers find that their lives may not be as distant as they first thought, and that soon, they may have to decide who they'll choose to be when the chips are down...

“AN OTHERWORDLY MEDITATION ON THE LUCK OF THE DRAW...”
GARY HENDERSON

This ambitious, thought-provoking, charming, and poignant play is the debut independent work of emerging Wellington theatre maker Nathaniel Smith. Featuring elements of live music and dance alongside the traditional structure of a one-room play, it is packed full of moments that will stay with the audience long after they've left the theatre.

In the Mo' Theatre Co. is a brand new company of emerging, local practictioners. Many of the cast and crew are graduates of theatre programmes at Te Herenga Waka and Te Auaha. This project showcases dynamic, exciting new talent in a bold, orginal new work.

Follow @inthemo_theatreco

events.long_description:
Created by Hariata & Tamati Moriarty and directed by Jim Moriarty, 'Waenga' centres on a young wahine Māori who is arrested and finds herself in a police holding cell. Alongside her journey is Peyton, who is coming to understand what a Tangata Tiriti partnership is and Grayson, a young Māori lawyer navigating his role in the system.

Performed by an ensemble cast, including well known rangatahi Hariata and Tamati Moriarty, the play is presented in Te Rākau’s unique Theatre Marae framework, creating space for collective reflection and shared experience.

Te Rākau is the longest running Māori theatre company in Aotearoa founded in 1989.

Recommended age 12+ contains swearing and depicts some violence. Children under 12 can accompany for free with a paying adult.

events.venue: Nōku te Ao Capital E, 65 Victoria Street, Wellington Central, Wellington., Wellington
events.long_description:
Join local artist Tayla Hartemink for a hands-on screenprinting workshop exploring the importance of protecting our moana and waterways.

Te moana is an important source of life; it sustains ecosystems, provides habitat for native species, and supports our communities through recreation, kai gathering, and drinking water. However, many of our waterways are at risk from human activity.

In this hands-on workshop, tamariki aged 8-10 learn to screenprint as they express their ideas around the importance of our waterways and our collective responsibility in protecting them.

The workshop begins at Ngā Paiaka Bleachers with Wellington City Libraries to spark inspiration. Participants then head to the Kia Mākūkū! Makerspace Wet to bring their ideas to life using ink and fabric, screenprinting their own designs onto recycled tees or tote bags using stencils created by Tayla.

Tote bags and t-shirts are provided.

events.long_description:
Ever wanted to sound like a robot, a monster, a space explorer, or something completely out of this world? Introducing The Voice Changer — a hands-on electronics project that lets you record your voice, save your sound files, and then play them back with weird and wonderful effects.

The unit has its own handheld microphone, built-in speaker, headphone output, screen, buttons and menu controls. You can save up to 6 recordings of around 20 seconds each, then experiment with effects like echo, pitch shifting, distortion, tremolo and reverb to completely transform the sound. You can control everything from the unit itself, or connect to it from a phone or computer to adjust settings using a simple web interface.

On the day you will get to solder the electronics, assemble the laser-cut case, fit the speaker, screen, buttons and microphone, and load the code onto the onboard microcontroller. The unit is powered by a USB cable so no batteries required. At the end of the day you’ll walk away with a fully working voice-changing gadget that you built yourself, ready to prank your family, invent strange characters, or create your own sci-fi sound effects.

No previous experience is required and you’re welcome to bring a grown up if you want to.

events.venue: Nōku te Ao Capital E, 65 Victoria Street, Wellington Central, Wellington., Wellington
events.long_description:
Join local artist Tayla Hartemink for a hands-on screenprinting workshop exploring the importance of protecting our moana and waterways.
Te moana is an important source of life; it sustains ecosystems, provides habitat for native species, and supports our communities through recreation, kai gathering, and drinking water. However, many of our waterways are at risk from human activity.

In this hands-on workshop, rangatahi aged 11–14 learn to screenprint as they express their ideas around the importance of our waterways and our collective responsibility in protecting them.

The workshop begins at Ngā Paiaka Bleachers with Wellington City Libraries to spark inspiration. Participants then head to the Kia Mākūkū! Makerspace Wet to bring their ideas to life using ink and fabric, screenprinting their own designs onto recycled tees or tote bags using stencils created by Tayla.

Tote bags and t-shirts are provided.

events.long_description:
National Celebration - 40 Years of Homosexual Law Reform
40 Years of Homosexual Law Reform – Community Celebration at Parliament

Join us in the historic Banquet Hall at Parliament as we come together to celebrate 40 years since the passing of the Homosexual Law Reform Act — a landmark moment that helped transform Aotearoa New Zealand into a more inclusive and just society.

This special evening will honour the courage, determination, and advocacy of those who fought for equality, while celebrating the vibrant and diverse rainbow communities who continue that legacy today.

The programme will feature speeches from past and present activists, sharing reflections on the movement, the challenges faced, and the progress achieved over four decades. Guests will also enjoy performances from talented members of the community, bringing music, storytelling, and creative expression to the celebration.

More than a commemoration, this event is also an opportunity to connect across generations of the rainbow community and allies. Join activists, community leaders, supporters, and friends for an evening of reflection, celebration, and whakawhanaungatanga in one of the country’s most significant civic spaces.

Together, we honour the past, celebrate the present, and look toward a future where equality and inclusion continue to grow.

Join us in the historic Banquet Hall at Parliament as we come together to celebrate 40 years since the passing of the Homosexual Law Reform Act — a landmark moment that helped transform Aotearoa New Zealand into a more inclusive and just society.
This special evening will honour the courage, determination, and advocacy of those who fought for equality, while celebrating the vibrant and diverse rainbow communities who continue that legacy today.
The programme will feature speeches from past and present activists, sharing reflections on the movement, the challenges faced, and the progress achieved over four decades. Guests will also enjoy performances from talented members of the community, bringing music, storytelling, and creative expression to the celebration.
More than a commemoration, this event is also an opportunity to connect across generations of the rainbow community and allies. Join activists, community leaders, supporters, and friends for an evening of reflection, celebration, and whakawhanaungatanga in one of the country’s most significant civic spaces.
Together, we honour the past, celebrate the present, and look toward a future where equality and inclusion continue to grow.
This event features: Fran Wilde, Tīwhanawhana, The Glamaphones, Vinyl&Proud
MC: Lynda Topp

Canapés are provided. There will be a cash bar available.

events.long_description:
Pub Sing - where the audience turns into the choir at the pub, with a live rock band,

No sheet music, no experience needed, and absolutely no solos.

Katy reveals three songs on the night (usually a crowd-pleaser, a ballad, and a banger), and even if you don’t know them, you’ll pick them up fast with colour-coded lyrics on screen.

You learn different harmony options, sing along with the band, and blend into a room of up to 80 voices, so no one’s listening to you; they’re singing with you.

There’s banter, laughs, a bit of silliness, and a whole lot of feel-good energy. It’s not karaoke (shudder), it’s everyone singing together just for the fun of it, and it’s the perfect end-of-week lift you needed.

*All ticket sales goes directly to the band*

events.name: Krafty Kuts 'Turbulence' Album Tour
events.venue: Meow, 9 Edward St, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
KRAFTY KUTS 'Turbulence' ALBUM TOUR | Matariki Weekend. Get a sneak peek of Krafty's new album 'Turbulence' releasing 10 July on Against The Grain. Drawing from UKG, breaks, bassline and jazz, it's his most significant record in over a decade.

A pioneer in the most literal sense. Krafty's Slam The Breaks series and his Mixmag Instant Party covermount didn't just define an era, they set the blueprint for the bass movement that soundtracked the 21st century. Two Breakspoll award-winning albums, a FabricLive 34 mix, and a back catalogue spanning Ministry of Sound, OWSLA, Fabric, Skint and Finger Lickin' tell you everything about where he sits in the canon.

On the road his CV reads like a who's who: Big Day Out alongside Rage Against The Machine and Bjork, Summadayze straight after Groove Armada, Glastonbury, Bestival, sell-out nights at Fabric, Brixton Electric and Matter. He's shared stages with Grand Master Flash, Z Trip, Thievery Corporation and Kurtis Blow and played everything from the Chinese Grand Prix to Spotify's launch party.

Local support from BRYCE | WADE | MASON | STU

events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Bassist Peter Hook has intimate knowledge of the music of bands Joy Division and New Order. He’s one of the founding members of both British new wave bands. In July 2026, he is bringing his band The Light to The Opera House in Wellington. Together they will perform New Order’s album ‘Get Ready’ in full to celebrate its 25th anniversary. To make the concert even better, they will also perform a selection of greatest hits from Joy Division’s and New Order’s back catalogue. Get ready to enjoy songs like Disorder, Shadowplay, Transmission, Love Will Tear Us Apart, Blue Monday, and True Faith. 
The dark and ethereal sound of Joy Division and New Order ushered in the post-punk era and continue to be influential in the rock music scene. Peter Hook and The Light are careful to meticulously recreate their music in a live setting. Audiences are in for a show where treasured songs are played with the passion and energy they deserve.

events.venue: 5710,Kahutara, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Matariki Festival Paetūmōkai
Matariki herenga waka – for all of us.

Kia ora Paetūmōkai whānau, Wairarapa Moana communities. and manuhiri, it's time for us to start planning our Matariki celebrations again.

Soon we will put the call out; for those of you who are storytellers, pumpkin choppers, kawakawa gatherers, kaumatua and kuia chauffeurs, chair putter-outers, table decorators, steam pudding makers, sweepers, child wranglers, photographers, leftover hangi dispersers, fairy light arrangers; our small town makes wonderful things happen when we gather together. If you have helped before, thank you, and if you can help again- thank you- but if you need to rest, we understand. If you haven't helped before- nau mai, haere mai, welcome- and in advance, thank you!

This year’s theme of "Matariki herenga waka" is all about inclusion, and encouraging ALL people to celebrate Matariki together. The theme has strong connections to multi-culturalism and the sharing of cultural practices; we can ALL connect to the core values of Matariki and embrace the celebration of the holiday.

The Māori New Year is a time of reflection, celebration, and preparation. It is a time to remember loved ones, come together with whānau to give thanks to what we have and look forward to the promise of a new year.

In the meantime; here's a new Matariki waiata to get your heart singing. Don't worry, there'll still be the Matariki Macarena!

events.id: Matariki Whānau Day-Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, 55 Cable St, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Matariki Whānau Day
events.venue: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa, 55 Cable St, Wellington
events.long_description:
A family-friendly Matariki celebration filled with free cultural activities, workshops and interactive experiences inspired by waka voyaging, Pacific traditions and celestial navigation.

This special Matariki Whānau Day invites tamariki and whānau to explore the stories, mātauranga and cultural connections carried across Te Moana-nui-a-Kiwa through hands-on activities, creative workshops and live demonstrations.

Families can take part in a design workshop with artist and carver Selwyn Palmer exploring the remote Polynesian islands of Rennell and Bellona, discover the Fijian environmental calendar and seasonal food knowledge with Emele Ugavule, and learn about Pacific navigation through star compass demonstrations from the navigators of Ngahiraka Mai Tawhiti.

Visitors can also explore Kiribati culture with St Joseph's Kiribati Community, complete a Te Papa Taonga Trail inspired by the tohu of Matariki, and enjoy Matariki-themed face painting throughout the day.

Suitable for all ages.

This event includes NZSL interpretation and wheelchair access.
events.description:
A family-friendly Matariki celebration filled with free cultural activities, workshops and interactive experiences inspired by waka voyaging, Pacific traditions and celestial navigation.
This special Matariki Whānau Day invites tamariki and whānau to explore the stories, mātauranga and cultural connections carried across Te Moana-nui-a-Kiwa through hands-on activities, creative workshops and live demonstrations.
Families can take part in a design workshop with artist and carver Selwyn Palmer exploring the remote Polynesian islands of Rennell and Bellona, discover the Fijian environmental calendar and seasonal food knowledge with Emele Ugavule, and learn about Pacific navigation through star compass demonstrations from the navigators of Ngahiraka Mai Tawhiti.
Visitors can also explore Kiribati culture with St Joseph's Kiribati Community, complete a Te Papa Taonga Trail inspired by the tohu of Matariki, and enjoy Matariki-themed face painting throughout the day.
Suitable for all ages.

events.long_description:
Join Ōtaki Pottery Club for the 2026 Star Glaze Mid Winter Ceramics Festival, an exciting celebration of art and the traditions of Matariki, set against the picturesque backdrop of the Ōtaki Māori Racing Club.

The festival kicks off with a captivating opening ceremony, marking the beginning of a vibrant weekend filled with diverse hands on activities, inspiring exhibits, delicious food, lively music, and much more. Immerse yourself in the rich heritage of Matariki and discover the magic of pottery in a festival like no other.

Friday also features race day at the venue, adding to the atmosphere and making for a lively start to the weekend. On Saturday, don’t miss the public raku firing, a hands on and visually striking experience that is always a highlight for visitors.

Ruku atu ki te hōhonutanga o ngā tikanga o Matariki, ā, kitea te mākutu o te mahi uku i roto i tētahi hui kāore he rite.

Gate entry is $10 on Friday, no entry fee on Saturday.

events.long_description:
Matariki comes alive in Greytown with an afternoon and evening of culture, creativity, storytelling and community celebration in and around Stella Bull Park.

Families can take part in hands-on activities throughout the day, including glow-in-the-dark star painting at Greytown Art Gallery, located in Stella Bull Park. Inspired by the Matariki cluster, you can paint and hang stars. Wander through the park at your leisure to see artworks created by children from Greytown School.

Warm up with delicious kai, including a traditional hāngī prepared by the Kuranui College Netball Team, alongside fry bread, sweet treats and festive winter fare. Find them at Stella Bull Park from 3pm. Limited Hangi available, so get in quick!

As darkness falls, enjoy a special projected retelling of the Matariki story, created by Stun and illuminated across the Blackwell & Son’s building just up the road at 110 Main St, creating a striking visual centrepiece for the celebrations.

With music, light, art and shared kai, Greytown’s Matariki celebration is a beautiful opportunity to come together, reflect, remember and look forward to the year ahead

events.long_description:
Shooting the Stars- Wainuiomata Regional Park
Calling all aspiring astro-photographers!

Join us to get close-up and personal with our galaxy and learn the basics of dark sky shooting from a professional.

Are you a photographer interested in learning the tips and tricks of dark sky photography? We are thrilled to be offering this exclusive astrophotography workshop and stargazing session guided by Glen Butler (Night & Light Photography) and Wellington Astronomical Society as part of Greater Wellington’s Dark Sky Series.

This event is strictly limited to 30 people, register now via this link:


Please only register if you have the equipment requirements outlined below. What to bring (minimum requirements):
• Camera – with the ability to change manual settings of aperture, shutter speed and ISO
• A wide-angle lens or zoom (e.g. 14mm, 24mm, 35mm)
• A stable tripod
• A remote shutter release or the ability to put your camera onto (2-second) self-timer mode
• Empty memory card(s)
• Spare/fully charged camera batteries
• Head torch (ideally with red light setting)
• Warm clothing and sturdy footwear

During this introductory session to astrophotography, you will learn the fundamentals and some creative ideas to begin taking captivating images in a unique dark sky environment. Wellington Astronomical Society will also have their telescopes on hand for you to have a closer look at our sparkling Southern Skies.

Why Wainuiomata? Wainuiomata Regional Park is close to achieving dark sky place accreditation and offers some of the region's best stargazing just 30 minutes from Wellington's CBD. The location of the park provides a sanctuary from city light pollution, allowing budding astro-photographers a stunning night sky to shoot.

This event is not suitable for children under 18.

events.long_description:
We’ve spent the last 5 years living together, how hard could it be writing an event description together?

This show is about anything and everything, but mostly about us. How we met, where we’re going, which coalition member we hate more than the other two dickheads, et cetera.

We have lots in common... we both studied at Otago, we both do stand-up comedy, and we both love each other ♥️ It did take ages to choose a name for this show. Our first idea, "Flight of the Conchords", was sadly already taken. But, we figured Date Night was perfect, as we always talk about finding more time to spend together; forgetting time has already arrived, we only need to decide who else to share it with.

Regardless, it'll be an unforgettable night, and we’d love to share the joy with you.

events.name: Delaney Davidson Baby Heavyweight Tour
events.venue: St Peters Village Hall, Cnr Beach Rd and Ames St, Paekākāriki
events.long_description:
Delaney Davidson is a New Zealand Singer Songwriter, Musician, and Visual Artist.

A wry sense of humour, some theatre of unease, and a voice classed as not conventionally beautiful all combine to breathe life and space into the niche he has carved out for himself, winning him critical acclaim across the world for his original take on things.

His seminal influence and work with Marlon Williams on their Sad But True series as well as his visionary production on Tami Neilson’s acclaimed album’s Dynamite, Don’t Be Afraid and Chickaboom!, have also earned him great praise from the media and huge respect amongst his peers. Sync placements in The Expanse, Nashville TV Series, Bad Sisters, and Brokenwood Mysteries have taken Delaney’s music globally.

Baby Heavyweight, born in a kitchen in Switzerland, is Delaney Davidson’s 11th solo album. Somewhat more groovy than his previous releases, this is the second album he has made with Merk (Mark Perkins). Building on the smooth depth of the previous album Out Of My Head, and taking it into a new realm of story telling and emotive music.

Hitting the road with a stacked band featuring Heather Webb, Cass Basil, Alex Freer and Ryan Fisherman, Delaney sets his sights on a show that will deliver the album in all its complexity and nuance. Truly something to be witnessed. Do Not Miss Out.

Incontestably one of Aotearoas most influential and lauded contemporary songwriters - Under The Radar

…..beautifully haunting Rolling Stone

events.name: Kiri Te Kanawa Song Quest 2026
events.venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Widely regarded as the launchpad for New Zealand’s leading operatic talent, this competition has championed emerging singers since 1956. In the Kiri Te Kanawa Song Quest 2026, elite singers vie for a share of $95,500 in prizes. Watch as six finalists perform with the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra conducted by Brad Cohen, at the Grand Final Gala. International judge Frederica von Stade will announce the winner live at the end of the night. 
For the first time in its 70-year history, the competition bears the name of its most famous winner, Dame Kiri Te Kanawa. The Gisborne-born singer won the competition in 1965 and went on to an illustrious operatic career across the globe. 
The 2026 judge, Frederica von Stade, is one of the most beloved mezzo-sopranos of her generation, celebrated for her expressive artistry and enduring contribution to classical music. Affectionately known as “Flicka,” she made her Metropolitan Opera debut in 1970 and went on to perform more than 300 times with the company. In concert, she has collaborated with eminent conductors and orchestras across the globe.

events.long_description:
Christian Benson is known professionally as Luude. The Australian drum and bass producer is best known for his 2021 cover of the 1980s iconic anthem Down Under. The D&B rework gave it a whole new dynamic and sold millions of copies. Five years and many successful mixes later, Luude is riding a wave of success. He’s toured relentlessly across some of the biggest stages in dance music and now comes to Wellington’s Shed 6. Along with Down Under, you’ll hear big hits like Big City Life, TMO, and Oh My. 
Luude’s recording achievements also include an ARIA Award for Best Dance Release and a nomination for the Michael Gudinski Breakthrough Artist Award. He also won Best International Artist at the 2022 Drum and Bass Awards, three BBC Radio 1 Hottest Records, and platinum, gold, and silver Certifications. He is also half of Australian electronic duo Choomba.

The world’s foremost purveyors of time-twisting hits, Postmodern Jukebox, return to Wellington for one highly anticipated show at The Opera House. 
Founded in New York, the trailblazing troupe made up of singers, dancers, and instrumentalists brings their brand new ‘The Future is Vintage’ tour to New Zealand shores. Concertgoers can expect to enter a parallel musical universe where modern-day earworms and iconic pop tracks are reimagined. Come and be swept away by the romance and swagger of the past while enjoying your favourite tunes from now.

events.id: Matariki Movie Matinee: War Stories Our Mother's Never Told Us (1995)-Regent 3 Cinemas, 230 Queen Street, Masterton-Event Finder
events.name: Matariki Movie Matinee: War Stories Our Mother's Never Told Us (1995)
events.venue: Regent 3 Cinemas, 230 Queen Street, Masterton
events.long_description:
Matariki Movie Matinee: War Stories Our Mothers Never Told Us (1995)

Join us for a special Matariki screening of the acclaimed Aotearoa documentary War Stories Our Mothers Never Told Us by Dame Gaylene Preston.

Seven New Zealand women share their personal stories of love, loss, marriage, and service during the Second World War. Told in their own voices and woven with archival footage, the film offers an intimate and powerful portrait of a generation whose experiences were often left unspoken.

Rather than narration, the film allows the women to speak directly, creating a simple and deeply moving record of memory, resilience, and everyday life during wartime Aotearoa.

As part of Matariki, this screening reflects the star Pōhutukawa, associated with remembrance and those who have passed. The event creates a space for reflection, storytelling, and intergenerational connection through shared experience.

Event schedule
11.30am | Optional shared kai (seasonal soup and bread) at Café Strada, Masterton
12.15pm | Film screening at Regent 3 Cinemas, Queen Street, Masterton

Following the film | Post-screening kōrero and audience Q&A with Dame Gaylene Preston

Tickets
$15 | Film only
$25 | Film + shared Matariki lunch
Cash sales available on the day, subject to availability.

Ticket proceeds
In accordance with the wishes of Dame Gaylene Preston, all $15 cinema ticket sales will be donated to Te Waiwhaakata Wairarapa Film Festival, supporting its kaupapa of celebrating, preserving, sharing, and creating films that connect people with place.

Acknowledgements
This screening is proudly supported by the Masterton District Council Matariki Fund, which contributed $500 toward cinema hire and film screening rights.

Film Duration: 95 minutes
Presented by The Story Studio as part of the 'Follow the Stars' Matariki Grant administered by Masterton District Council.

events.venue: Blackwell & Sons, 110 Main Street, Greytown
events.long_description:
Join zinester, artist, and academic Bryce Galloway for a hands-on zine-making workshop. Whether you're new to zines or already immersed in DIY publishing, this workshop is a space to explore how personal writing can shift from private reflection into a creative, shareable form.

Many zines begin the same way journals do, as fragments of daily life, observations, sketches, and unfiltered thoughts. In this hands-on workshop, you will receive prompts from Bryce, and each participant will contribute a page to a collective zine that you can take home at the end. Use the skills you learn to continue working on your own individual zine in the future.

All materials are provided, and your ticket includes a copy of Bryce’s brand new book, 'Zines NZ: Punk to Present'. This richly illustrated exploration of Aotearoa’s zine culture traces the scene from its 1980s punk origins through to today’s vibrant communities, preserving voices that are often fleeting, personal, and hard to archive.

What is a zine?
A zine (pronounced “zeen”) is a noncommercial, often homemade or digital publication typically focused on niche or unconventional topics. Lo-fi and personal, zines are usually produced in small batches by passionate creators. They exist in a unique space between private diary and public storytelling - a way to give shape to perspectives that might otherwise remain unseen.

About the tutor:
Bryce Galloway is a long-time zinester whose publication Incredibly Hot Sex with Hideous People is Aotearoa’s longest-running zine. Known for its diaristic writing and playful, hand-drawn style, his work exemplifies how journal-like material can become compelling, shareable art. Bryce is also a founding member of the Kirikiriroa Hamilton Zinefest, part of the Wellington Zinefest team, and a Fine Arts lecturer at Massey University’s School of Art.

Details:
Saturday July 11th
1:30 - 4pm

Price: $65 - includes the workshop and a copy of Bryce's book 'Zines NZ: Punk to Present'
All materials provided

Please note: our venue is up one flight of stairs and there is not an elevator.

events.long_description:
Go behind the bubbles at Alexia Urban Winery as winemaker Jane Cooper reveals the craft behind New Zealand’s “Champagne” — known as Méthode Traditionnelle.

As one of the country’s few 100% in-house producers, Alexia completes every step of the process on site. Enjoy a rare insider’s preview of what’s still ageing and developing, from base wine to finished sparkling, and discover how time, patience, and precision transform them in the bottle. Hear behind-the-scenes stories from the winery and have the language of fizz demystified so you’ll leave knowing exactly what’s in your glass and how it got there.

This is a fun, informative event - regardless of whether you’re a devoted wine enthusiast or just curious about the magic behind the mousse, you’ll enjoy an afternoon that offers a true insider’s perspective on crafting exceptional NZ fizz.

The event includes a glass of Méthode Traditionnelle on arrival, all tasting pours and light snacks. Vegetarian and GF options available. Due to the nature of this event, other dietary requests cannot be offered.

$45 per person, please purchase your tickets through https://www.alexia.co.nz/buy-alexia-wine

events.venue: St Peters Village Hall, Cnr Beach Rd and Ames St, Paekākāriki
events.long_description:
Barry Barclay's Ngati is of historical and cultural significance in Aotearoa New Zealand as it is the first feature film written and directed by Māori.

The film is set in 1948 in a small town on the east coast of New Zealand during the impending closure of a freezing works and the threat of unemployment for the local community.

The 4pm screening of "Ngati" will be followed by a short kai break before a 6.15pm screening of "The Camera on the Shore" (2009), a documentary about the late Barry Barclay that will be introduced by director Graeme Tuckett.

events.name: Sat Afternoon Jewellery Making - Beginners
events.venue: Workspace Studios Ōtaki, 2 Arthur Street, Ōtaki, Ōtaki
events.long_description:
Spend your Saturday afternoons immersed in creativity, learning the timeless craft of jewellery-making in our warm, welcoming studio.

This short course is the perfect introduction for complete beginners, guiding you step-by-step through the essential techniques used by jewellers. You’ll start by working in copper or brass, building confidence as you learn to cut, heat, shape and texture metal. From there, you can choose to move into silver and bring your ideas to life in more refined pieces.

A beautiful textured ring band is an ideal first project, but once you’ve mastered the basics, the possibilities really open up—create earrings, pendants, or small bespoke pieces that reflect your personal style. You’ll learn how to solder using a jeweller’s torch, refine your finishing techniques, and polish your work to a professional shine. It’s a hands-on, deeply satisfying process, and there’s nothing quite like wearing something you’ve made yourself.

Materials are purchased as you go, so you can tailor your projects to your budget and ideas. Beginners typically spend around $50–$70 on metals over the course.

This block is ideal for teens and young creatives aged 12 and up.
Please note: anyone under 16 must be accompanied by an enrolled parent or caregiver.

The Wellington Comedy Club in conjunction with Wellington Community Revitalisation Society present Matariki Laughs

With Ben Hurley
As seen on The Project, Seven Sharp, and more
With a massive but hugely likeable stage presence, Hurley can win over even the toughest room. A sharp improvisational mind and well honed original material make Hurley a popular act with audiences and critics alike.

Opeti Vaka - 2026 Billy T Award nominee
If you ask him how why he started performing comedy, he'll tell you "Well I actually started running out of options.."
Born in Wellington, with a dollop of South Auckland style, add in a sprinkle of life in the fast lane with his very large whanau and their antics, take a pinch of "what the f**k?", and wrap it all up in a person of multiple colours, those colours being 2 shades of brown (Tongan & Maori), well you get a very comedic perspective of his world.

Mamaeroa Munn
A multi-award-winning stand-up comedian, improviser and writer based in Wellington, New Zealand. A regular on the professional stand-up circuit in Pōneke, Mo has taken shows to the NZ International Comedy Festival, Melbourne Comedy Festival, TAHI solo festival of the arts, and Chicago iO Festival. In 2025, Mo debuted their first solo hour in the NZ International Comedy Fest, taking home the award for Best Newcomer.

Jak Darling
2025 Billy T Nominee and Pōneke Powerhouse Jak Darling has been charming audiences all over Aotearoa and across the ditch. Their Matariki resolution is to make you laugh so get ready for some tongue, cheek, and a whole... lot more!

events.name: Waenga
events.venue: Avalon Intermediate - Te Kura Waenga o Motutawa, 1041 High St, Lower Hutt
events.long_description:
A special Matariki event of Māori theatre in Lower Hutt.

Created by Hariata & Tamati Moriarty and directed by Jim Moriarty, 'Waenga' centres on a young wahine Māori who is arrested and finds herself in a police holding cell. Alongside her journey is Peyton, who is coming to understand what a Tangata Tiriti partnership is and Grayson, a young Māori lawyer navigating his role in the system.

Performed by an ensemble cast, including well known rangatahi Hariata and Tamati Moriarty, the play is presented in Te Rākau’s unique Theatre Marae framework, creating space for collective reflection and shared experience.

Te Rākau is the longest running Māori theatre company in Aotearoa founded in 1989.

Recommended age 12+ contains swearing and depicts some violence.

events.long_description:
Postmodern Jukebox [WELLINGTON]
The world’s foremost purveyors of time-twisting hits, Postmodern Jukebox, have announced their highly-anticipated return to Australia and New Zealand in June and July 2026!

Having previously performed multiple sold-out tours across Oceania, the trailblazing troupe of singers, dancers and instrumentalists will hit our shores with their brand new The Future is Vintage tour.

“In the midst of the AI hype all around us, some folks have gone so far as to proclaim that in the not-so-distant future, all of the music that we listen to will be AI generated – we’ll gladly take the other side of that wager,” says PMJ founder and arranger, Scott Bradlee. “We’re humbly presenting our own unique vision of a spectacular future; one that is built upon the timeless musical genres of the past and the authentically human spirit of creativity that inspired them.”

Concertgoers can expect to enter a parallel musical universe where modern-day earworms and iconic pop tracks alike are reimagined. Expect everything from ’70s rock classics and ’80s Britpop hits, to current chart-toppers, movie and video game soundtracks. Dress in your vintage best, for the full time-travel experience!

A TEG Dainty presale begins on Thursday November 20 at 11am (local). Sign up for access:

https://www.tegdainty.com/tour/postmodernjukebox2026/

Tickets to general public go on sale on Friday November 21 at 11am (local).

events.id: Mark de Clive-Lowe │Remixes & Reimaginations │Remix Set-Meow, 9 Edward St, Te Aro, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Mark de Clive-Lowe │Remixes & Reimaginations │Remix Set
events.venue: Meow, 9 Edward St, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
New Zealand-born, Tokyo-based pianist, composer and producer Mark de Clive-Lowe returns with Remixes & Reimaginations, a new collection celebrating decades of boundary-pushing work across jazz, broken beat, house and electronic music. Known internationally for his ability to seamlessly fuse live instrumentation, improvisation and technology, MdCL has collaborated with artists including Moodymann, Kamasi Washington, DJ Spinna, Sheila E, Kenny Dope and Kyoto Jazz Massive.

More than a traditional remix album, Remixes & Reimaginations explores the art of transformation - taking existing works and uncovering entirely new dimensions within them. Spanning soulful broken beat, deep house, jazz and experimental club sounds, the collection features reworks of artists including Close Counters, We Are KING, Omar and Anthony Joseph, each crafted with deep respect for the original while pushing the music somewhere unexpected.

Renowned for his dynamic live remix performances, Mark de Clive-Lowe creates sets that blur the line between concert, club and spontaneous composition. Every performance is built in real time, reshaping familiar sounds into something immediate, immersive and completely unique.

Support from Pōneke's own Benny Salvador, DJ, multi-instrumentalist, producer and radio show host. Benny has won over audiences throughout New Zealand with his eclectic, dancefloor-friendly selections that find the common threads between house, techno, electro, disco-funk, dub, boogie and beyond.

events.long_description:
Back due to popular demand! Scott Bradlee’s Postmodern Jukebox to return to New Zealand with ‘The Future Is Vintage’ 2026 Tour!

NEW ZEALAND

AUCKLAND - Kiri Te Kanawa – Friday July 10
WELLINGTON - Wellington Opera House – Saturday July 11
CHRISTCHURCH - Isaac Theatre Royal – Sunday July 12

Tickets on sale Friday November 21 at 11am local time. For ticketing and tour details go to www.tegdainty.com

POSTMODERN JUKEBOX has announced their brand-new show, which will take them to cities across UK, Europe, Australia and New Zealand, to kick off their 2026 THE FUTURE IS VINTAGE World Tour.

The highly acclaimed troupe of singers, dancers and instrumentalists will be performing their new show in the group’s signature time-twisting style – putting a retro spin on everything from 70’s rock classics and 80’s Britpop hits, to current chart toppers, movie and video game soundtracks. With a heavy dose of danceable numbers alongside jaw-dropping showstoppers THE FUTURE IS VINTAGE works equally well as the perfect date night or family outing.

“In the midst of the AI hype all around us, some folks have gone so far as to proclaim that in the no-to-distant future, all of the music that we listen to will be AI generated…we’ll gladly take the other side of that wager,” say PMK founder and arranger, Scott Bradlee. “On the 2026 Postmodern Jukebox UK/Europe/Australia/New Zealand tour, we’re humbly presenting our own unique vision of a spectacular future; one that is built upon the timeless musical genres of the past and the authentically human spirit of creativity that inspired them”.

When Bradlee started making YouTube videos that remade the hits of today in the classic styles of yesterday, a “viral” success story was born —one that quickly led to sold out shows across North America and Europe in the Summer of 2014.

The touring act received rave reviews from industry publications and world-renowned artists alike. In the years that followed, “PMJ” built a reputation as the “Saturday Night Live of singers” by introducing audiences to dozens of exceptional musical artists and turning them into Bonafide stars.

Twelve years and two billion views on their YouTube channel later, a Postmodern Jukebox show has become something of an annual musical tradition for hundreds of thousands of dedicated fans, all over the world. The rare concert act that appeals across generations, older audience members will fall in love with the timeless sounds and nostalgic sensibilities, while younger fans will be thrilled by the fresh take on current pop culture and the sheer virtuosity of the performers on stage.

Dress in your vintage best for the full time-travel experience and remember: The Future Is Vintage!

Steam Trains between Paekakariki & Porirua | 12th July 2026

Break the School Holiday Boredom!
Join Steam Incorporated this School Holidays, as we invite you onboard our heritage train for a brilliant steam train ride for the whole family!

Trains are operating all Sunday between Paekakariki and Porirua, a beautiful scenic run along the Paekakariki Escarpment on the Kapiti Coast. In our run between Pukerua Bay and Paekakariki, we pass through 6 short tunnels! A section of railway line with origins dating back to 1886. A scenic train journey for the whole family, steam along the coast onboard our heritage train with our friendly team!

These trains are topped & tailed by one of our coal-fired steam locomotives, and our Da class diesel electric.

events.id: Elouan Quartet with Bridget Douglas (Flute)-St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington-Event Finder
events.name: Elouan Quartet with Bridget Douglas (Flute)
events.venue: St Andrews on the Terrace, 30 The Terrace, Wellington
events.long_description:
A diverse, intimate and engaging presentation of mixed ensemble chamber music for flute and string quartet. The performers are Jessica Oddie – violin, Anna van der Zee – violin, Alexander McFarlane – viola, Ken Ichinose – cello, and Bridget Douglas - flute. All are NZSO players.

This programme moves between the rich Romantic lyricism of Amy Beach and Arthur Foote, the contemporary fluidity of Salina Fisher’s Mata-Au (inspired by the Clutha River), and the rhythmic energy of Alberto Ginastera’s folk-infused Impresiones de la Puna. Ludwig van Beethoven’s string quartet anchors the programme, offering a timeless contrast to the surrounding works. Audiences will be immersed in a journey through soundscapes that evoke flowing rivers, twilight atmospheres, and dynamic folk rhythms. With a strong connection to water and place, this programme resonates deeply in Aotearoa, where waterways are both culturally and environmentally significant.

Amy Beach, Theme and Variations for Flute and String Quartet, Op 80
Salina Fisher, Mata-Au (for string trio)
Arthur Foote, A Night Piece for Flute and String Quartet
Ludwig van Beethoven, String Quartet No 6 in B-flat major Op 18
Alberto Ginastera, Impresiones de la Puna (flute and string quartet)

This concert is presented in association with Chamber Music NZ

events.name: Holiday Programme - The Voice Changer
events.venue: Miramar Central School, 38 Park Rd, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Ever wanted to sound like a robot, a monster, a space explorer, or something completely out of this world? Introducing The Voice Changer — a hands-on electronics project that lets you record your voice, save your sound files, and then play them back with weird and wonderful effects.

The unit has its own handheld microphone, built-in speaker, headphone output, screen, buttons and menu controls. You can save up to 6 recordings of around 20 seconds each, then experiment with effects like echo, pitch shifting, distortion, tremolo and reverb to completely transform the sound. You can control everything from the unit itself, or connect to it from a phone or computer to adjust settings using a simple web interface.

On the day you will get to solder the electronics, assemble the laser-cut case, fit the speaker, screen, buttons and microphone, and load the code onto the onboard microcontroller. The unit is powered by a USB cable so no batteries required. At the end of the day you’ll walk away with a fully working voice-changing gadget that you built yourself, ready to prank your family, invent strange characters, or create your own sci-fi sound effects.

No previous experience is required and you’re welcome to bring a grown up if you want to.

MakeRoom holiday programmes run every term break as well as over the summer. They are made up of one day workshops focusing on a big build with lots of fun learning along the way. Everyone gets to take the project they have constructed home with them.

- One day sessions
- Only 8 Kids per instructor
- 9am to 3.30pm
- $140 (including GST) for the day
- Open to kids aged 10-15
- Parents and Guardians welcome

On the day:

- Students should bring their own food and water bottle (morning tea and lunch)
- Students should wear closed toed shoes for safety in the workshop
- Students with long hair should have it tied back for safety

This is a beginners course in 2D animation where tweens & teens will learn the time-honoured principles of hand-drawn animation and how to apply them to your own animation project. Over this two day workshop, students may choose to work on their own project and incorporate their own ideas with the help of our tutor, or if you'd rather, undertake an assigned project.

You can use any device, ipad or laptop you already own (except a mobile – it's really not big enough to do good animation on). The school does not provide any digital equipment. events.name: Revolution's Daughter
events.venue: Roxy Cinema, 5 Park Road, Miramar, Wellington
events.long_description:
Doc Edge Festival 2026 - Opening Night

His revolution. Her truth.
Alina Fernández grew up in Havana not knowing she was Fidel Castro’s daughter, an open secret kept from her alone. Years before escaping Cuba and rebuilding her life in Miami, she made a choice that would define her: to speak out, and to keep speaking out. She calls it the only thing she ever really did, the one act she refused to shrink from. The film weaves Alina’s defiance into the broader fabric of Miami’s Cuban exile community, where artists and storytellers across generations carry the inheritance of revolution in their own ways, exploring identity, belonging, and what it costs to use your voice when silence would be easier.

events.name: Public Lecture - Prof Heidi Hornik
events.venue: St John's in the City Presbyterian Church, 170 Willis Street., Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Discover how art brings meaning to life.

Looking at Select Western Paintings: Art Historical and Theological Insights.

An analysis of visual examples will show how Western painters have interpreted biblical stories in ways that shape and reflect faith, ethics, and everyday
action.

Throughout the centuries, painters trained in the Western tradition have used their formal skills and talents to interpret biblical stories using their mind’s eyes. In Christian communities, the biblical narrative served as a thematic source of reflection on a contemporary issue of that society (e.g., Chrisitan habits and virtues, moral issues facing Christians, formative and liturgical practices). Several of these themes will be discussed through an analysis of the visual examples using theological insights and art historical methods.

Join Wellington trip-hop trio Tragedies in celebrating the release of their upcoming single 'Taupiri'. Coming from the reo Maori word for 'a loving embrace', Taupiri is a queer love song for the end of the world that celebrates the small moments of bliss carved out of dark times. Spies, lies and a box of video tapes.
Didrik thought his Norwegian father was a journalist. In reality, he was a CIA spy who fired AK-47s in the Kuwaiti desert and infiltrated cocaine laboratories in Colombia. When Didrik finds a box of old tapes and documents in his father’s attic, he uncovers a story almost too strange to be true. For the first time his father, Bjørn, begins to speak openly about his past. As Didrik digs deeper, the life and lies of a man who blurred the lines between journalism, propaganda, and international espionage begins to emerge. But can any of it be trusted?

Breaking barriers doesn’t have an expiration date.
Three trailblazing women broke barriers in their time: Kathrine Switzer, the first woman to officially run the Boston Marathon; Siila Watt-Cloutier, the first woman to connect climate change to human rights; and Sharon Farmer, the first woman to act as Chief White House Photographer. With determination and grit, these ladies shed light on what it takes to make it in a man’s world, and what old age looks like when you’re a self-described “tough old broad”.

After years of chasing a music dream, Emma Rutherford faces the question everyone with a creative degree eventually hears: “have you thought about going teaching?”

Originally from a rural North Canterbury town where everyone knows everyone, Emma Rutherford packed up her life, her microphone and a truckload of unsolicited advice to chase the impossible dream of making it in the music industry.

The winter brings a programme of three works celebrating the heritage of the Royal New Zealand Ballet and the contributions of outstanding artists from our past, present and future.

At its heart is the New Zealand premiere of Sir Frederick Ashton’s Birthday Offering, performed as a centenary tribute to Southland-born ballerina Rowena Jackson and as part of Ashton Worldwide 2024–8. Completing the programme are two works created for the RNZB: Sarah Foster-Sproull’s exuberant Ultra Folly, inspired by the rhythmic energy of La Folia, and Andrea Schermoly’s Stand to Reason, a powerful tribute to the women of Aotearoa and the enduring fight for equality. Together, these three works honour legacy, connection and the timeless spirit of dance.

events.name: Come Together - Radiohead, OK Computer
events.venue: The Opera House, 111 - 113 Manners Street, Wellington
events.long_description:
New Zealand’s most successful rock series ever, COME TOGETHER, returns in 2026 with an electrifying trio of landmark albums: Bruce Springsteen’s Born to Run, Radiohead’s OK Computer and Talking Heads’ Stop Making Sense.

Each album will be performed live, in full, by a rotating supergroup of Aotearoa’s most acclaimed rock artists and musicians — followed by a second set of classics and deep cuts that span each artist’s extraordinary catalogue.

From the wall of sound production of Born to Run, to the haunting dystopian brilliance of OK Computer, to the joyful and immersive perfection of Stop Making Sense, the 2026 series celebrates three albums that have cemented their place in music history. Performed in some of the country’s most beautiful venues, Come Together once again promises epic musicianship, emotional punch and the kind of once-in-a-lifetime collaborations that have made the series a cultural phenomenon.

Released in 1997, OK Computer shattered rock conventions and captured the anxious spirit of a changing world. Hailed as a masterpiece on release — and consistently ranked among the greatest albums of all time — it remains as haunting, expansive and relevant today as ever.

Performed front to back, the album’s intricate soundscapes and emotional weight will be brought to life before a second set celebrating Radiohead’s rich and restless back catalogue.


Performed by: Ed Knowles, Milan Borich, Seamus Johnson and the Come Together band — with more artists to be announced.

*Booking fees apply

events.long_description:
PopRox Presents: An Improvised Nativity at The New Zealand Festival of Christmas
PopRox is bringing their beloved improvised Christmas comedy show to the New Zealand festival of Christmas! PopRox is a professional improv theatre company from Wellington, specialising in slick, hilarious (and a little bit naughty) comedy shows, and for one night only their fully improvised retelling of the greatest story of them all is lighting up the stage at The Offering in Greytown.

A heavily pregnant Mary and a doting Joseph embark on a road-trip where they'll escape an evil king, come across three wise guys and just try to deliver this holy baby. Think "Life of Brian" with a heavy dose of kiwi humour! It's a night of laughs, heartfelt moments and great food with a dinner and a show at the gorgeous The Offering cafe. Enjoy an adults-only night out filled with laughter where these expert performers craft a story with a little help from you! Will Mary give birth in the back seat of Mazda Demio? Will the evil King Herod outlaw casual Friday? Will the three wise guys give the audience any helpful advice at all? There's only one way to find out. Book your tickets now and be sure to arrive early to enjoy drinks and a delicious dinner at The Offering.

“PopRox delivers on so many levels in its improvisation and comedic skill, with an ensemble of gifted and affecting actors... a performance that dazzles in its brilliance." Mitchell Manuel. Theatreview.

“All of the mahi these performers put in results in a show that is hilarious, engaging and leaves you wanting so much more.”
“What PopRox is doing here is nailing the tone and absurdity that the Nativity surely must have been filled with” Elliott Lam. Wellyott.

“it’s very clever...a rollicking good laugh to ease the pre-Christmas stress.” Sarah Catterall. The Post.

Show Running Information:

6:00pm- The Offering opens for dinner service
7:00pm- Main meal last orders taken
7:30pm- Show Begins
8:30pm (Approx.)- Show Finishes

PopRox is an ensemble of Wellington's top improv comedians, fresh off a two year residency at Circa Theatre and hit original shows at Wellington's "The Hannah" Theatre. Entering their 5th year as a company, PopRox's signature blend of compelling storytelling, hilarious one-liners, dazzling improvised music and slick production is sure to bring the warmth to Greytown this winter. Featuring decades of performing experience with award-winning comedians PopRox is an up and coming collective you don't want to miss.

events.long_description:
KING PARROT : Wellington NZ @ Valhalla w/- Slave Cadaver + Postnatal Abortion + Maced
FRIDAY JULY 17!
Tickets on sale now! via UTR
King Parrot are pleased to announce their return to New Zealand to launch the blistering new album A Young Persons Guide to King Parrot. Described as a hostile and abrasive slab of sensory destroying anthems, the record features ten thoroughly crafted blasts through the psyche of this crazed Aussie quintet. Recorded at Melbourne’s Dangertone studios with engineer Luke Walton, it’s the first full-length album since 2017’s critically adored Ugly Produce offering and their first new music since 2020’s Holed Up In The Lair EP. Pulling the new songs together was a meticulously creative endeavour and the final product is the most complete, aggressive, and urgent the band has ever sounded.
The band have been in full throttle touring mode since the release in early 2025 and are currently out on a massive 39 date jaunt through the USA alongside Gwar and Soulfly. Much of the last year was spent touring the globe in support of Pantera all over Europe, the UK and the USA where King Parrot amassed performing exactly 100 shows for the year. New Zealand fans can expect a band that is firing on all cylinders and awaiting their first shows in NZ in many years, comments vocalist Matt Young "It's been a while between drinks but we were most certain that we must return to NZ this year and give you guys a dose of King Parrot! We cant wait to get back and see our kiwi mates and bring our brand of off the kilter grind, thrash and punk rock chaos, get your tickets now and well see you real soon!"

events.long_description:
For billy woods, literate rhymes and inventive flows are littered through all his works. So much so, it’s hard to pinpoint his exact genre. But for the New York-based rapper, his music career began in the early 2000s, however, he was largely unknown until 2012 after the release of his solo album History Will Absolve Me. Since then, woods has gone onto release music under Armand Hammer – a collaborative project with ELUCID – and an array of solo albums like Today, I Wrote Nothing (2015), Maps (2023) and more.

His latest solo release – the 2025 album GOLLIWOG – has been deemed his most experimental yet. So much so, Pitchforkdescribed it as “a twisty horrorcore masterpiece where history and nightmares are indistinguishable” and a “perfect showcase for his craft”. It mixes horror, humour, surrealism and Afropessimism into the one work: think African zombies, time traveling trap cars, malevolent ragdolls and a dying Frantz Fanon

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
In today’s high-pressure world, burnout is often worn as a badge of honour—until the physical and mental toll becomes impossible to ignore. True recovery requires more than just "taking a break"; it requires resetting the nervous system from the inside out.
Led by Simon, a former high-stakes litigation lawyer who successfully navigated his own severe burnout, this workshop bridges the gap between understanding stress and actively healing from it. This practical, evidence-based workshop is designed to take you on a journey from chronic depletion to sustainable balance. You will explore what burnout actually is, identify your personal triggers, and master powerful physiological techniques to pause the stress response, recover your vitality, and return to life and work with renewed resilience.
What We Will Cover
Part 1: Understanding the Burnout Cycle (The Setup)
Before we can fix the problem, we must understand it. We begin by unpacking the foundations of chronic stress to help you map your own journey.
What is Burnout? Defining the psychological and physical parameters of exhaustion.
The Root Causes: Identifying the systemic, professional, and personal drivers of chronic stress.
The Nervous System Hijack: How prolonged pressure traps the body in a constant "fight-or-flight" state, impacting sleep, digestion, and cognitive function.
Part 2: The Science of Physiological Recovery (The Solution)
While mindset matters, burnout lives in the body. We will introduce the fastest, most effective tool for resetting a hijacked nervous system: Functional Breathing Training.
The Three Dimensions of Health: How biochemical, biomechanical, and psychophysiological breathing patterns dictate your stress levels.
Measuring Your Stress Tolerance: Learn how to assess your current breathing efficiency and physiological stress baseline.
Immediate Relief vs. Long-Term Resilience: Practices that offer instant calm during acute anxiety, paired with lifelong training to rebuild your nervous system.
What You Will Walk Away With
By the end of this one-day workshop, you will:
Recognise the Warning Signs: Deeply understand your own burnout triggers and early warning indicators.
Interrupt the Stress Response: Master proven, discreet techniques to pause the "fight-or-flight" response in real-time.
Improve Everyday Well-being: Know how to optimise your breathing patterns to combat poor sleep, fatigue, and brain fog.
A Personalised Recovery Plan: Walk away with a practical toolkit to integrate self-regulation and physical recovery into a busy professional life.
What to Bring: Please bring a notepad and pen to track your personal pacing metrics, record your breathing patterns, and map out your recovery strategy.
Participant Self-Management & Safety
This workshop is designed for adult learners. It is a supportive, respectful space where you are encouraged to engage at your own comfort level and self-manage your energy throughout the day (including taking breaks to decompress as needed).
Please note: The advanced physiological recovery techniques practiced in this workshop are highly effective for nervous system regulation. No prior experience with breathwork or yoga is required.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Mel die Storieverteller - LITTLE THEATRE, WELLINGTON - Internet Sensasie
Wellington! Mel is opgewonde om julle in te sluit in haar toer - dit gaan n onvergeetlike middag wees, moet dit nie misloop nie!

In 2023 het nuuskierige gehore opgedaag om te sien hoe internetsensasie, Mel die Storieverteller in lewende lywe op ‘n verhoog lyk. Nou stroom almal na haar vertonings want Mel is toe skreeusnaaks in die regte lewe ook (vir mans en vroue). In haar derde komiese een-vrou vertoning, Internet Sensasie, gaan gehore uitvind dat Mel nou kan sing ook.

Mel deel uit eerstehandse ervaring stories vanuit die elektroniese oerwoud vol aandagsoekers en liggelowiges: Oom Riekert se groot fout, ‘n beplande vuisgeveg in ‘n taai plek met die naam KuduKraal, hoe ‘Mel die Storieverteller’ ontstaan het en die siekte op haar voorkop.

Die stories is vars, onverwags en bleddie belaglik, maar blykbaar alles waar, wel, so sê Facebook, en ons almal weet wat op die internet staan is ‘n feit, maar kan betwyfel word, tensy jy dit wil glo!

Vertoning duur: 80 minute (Geen pouse)
Styl: Komiese Storievertelstyl
Ouderdomsbeperking: Geen onder 14’s
Venue: Little Theatre, Lower Hut (at the Dowse Art Museum)
Adres: 2 Queens Drive, Hutt Central, Lower Hutt 5010, New Zealand
Kaartjieprys: NZ$40
Vertoning begin: 16h00
Kaartjies: www.meldiestorieverteller.co.za

events.long_description:
Songs from the Shaky Isles: A Short History of Popular Music in New Zealand
Gareth Shute dives into his book Songs From the Shaky Isles to deliver a whirlwind overview of the past 100 years of popular music in Aotearoa.

Join us at the Library or online:

New Zealand Music: From pubs to playlists
From the era of ‘six-o'clock swill’ venue restrictions through to the grassroots 80s battle for radio airtime, then on to the seismic shift of the streaming age, Gareth Shute reveals how our music has always been intertwined with wider culture.

Gareth’s talk will be packed with fun, behind-the-scenes anecdotes about the wild characters who helped define the New Zealand music scene and will also be accompanied by some fascinating historic images from the Alexander Turnbull Library collection.

About the speaker
Gareth Shute writes regularly for the New Zealand music history website Audioculture | Iwi Waiata and is also the author of six books, including Hip Hop Music in Aotearoa, which won a national book award. He is also a musician who helps run Lil’ Chief Records and has toured overseas with two of their bands — The Brunettes, and The Ruby Suns. His current band is Thee Golden Geese.

Image: Gareth Shute. Book cover of Songs From The Shaky Isles: A Short History of Popular Music in New Zealand (Bateman Books, 2025).

events.long_description:
A Long Exhale: Winter Somatic Breathwork
Release built-up tension with The Long Exhale: 60-min somatic breathwork to calm your nervous system and find deeper rest.

About this Event


A Long Exhale: Winter Somatic Breathwork

The Long Exhale is a 60-minute somatic breathwork session designed for anyone feeling mentally full, emotionally stretched, or physically tense after months of constant movement and pressure.
You've been inhaling since January. It's time to breathe out.
This winter-focused session offers space for your nervous system to slow down, soften, and release, helping you reconnect with yourself in a gentle, grounded way.
This session may support you if you’re feeling:
Wired but exhausted
Emotionally or physically tense
Stuck in constant “go mode”
In need of deeper rest and nervous system support
Curious about breathwork in a safe, beginner-friendly space

What to expect
Guided breathwork and grounding practices
Gentle, body-led somatic breathing
Optional movement and nervous system release exercises
Rest, reflection, and integration time
A trauma-aware, consent-led environment with low-intensity options available

Benefits you may notice
Greater calm and clarity
Reduced tension in the body
Easier breathing and deeper rest
Emotional release and regulation
A stronger sense of inner steadiness

What to bring
Warm layers and socks
Water bottle
Optional blanket, eye mask, journal, and pen
Mats are provided for. You can bring your own for extra comfort

Pre-session guidance
Eat lightly 2 hours beforehand
Hydrate well throughout the day
Limit caffeine beforehand and avoid alcohol/substances for 24 hours
Arrive 10 minutes early

Important health information
Somatic breathwork may not be suitable for pregnancy, epilepsy, serious cardiovascular conditions, recent surgery/concussion, or severe psychiatric conditions. Please consult your healthcare provider if unsure.

Participant words
“After the session, I felt super light — like the weight of the world was no longer sitting on my shoulders. I felt a deep sense of peace and protection. An unforgettable healing experience.”
— Kaelah, New Zealand




Event followed by a plant-based dinner and dessert, all included in your ticket!



Meet Your Host: Lynn

Lynn Tiang is an Integrative Somatic Coach, breathwork facilitator, and Reiki practitioner based in Aotearoa, New Zealand. Her work combines somatic breathwork, Reiki, and life coaching to support nervous system regulation, emotional wellbeing, and grounded personal transformation in a practical, trauma-aware way.

🕑: 06:00 PM - 07:00 PM
A Long Exhale: Winter Somatic Breathwork
Host: Hosted by Lynn

events.long_description:
Let There Be Light - Wellington
From the depths of darkness, let there be light. Aotearoa New Zealand piano prodigy Shan Liu features in a concert about hope.

Programme:
Bohdana Frolyak Let There Be Light (NZ Premiere)
Prokofiev Piano Concerto No. 3
Tchaikovsky Symphony No. 4

From the depths of darkness, let there be light.

We are honoured to present Aotearoa New Zealand premiere of Let There Be Light by Ukrainian composer Bohdana Frolyak. Inspired by the war in Ukraine, this “brooding and luminous” work describes the return of the light (Opera Today).

Prokofiev’s Third Piano Concerto, begun in 1913, was similarly written at a time of war. Nevertheless, this music remains enticingly puckish, witty and brilliant — the perfect showcase for our astonishing young prodigy Shan Liu. Previously an NZSO Emerging Artist, in 2024 he performed with the NZSO National Youth Orchestra. Liu is a testament to the wonderful and important work our Education team achieve.

Finally, Tchaikovsky’s magisterial Fourth Symphony, from its foreboding opening fanfare to its galvanising finale, takes us on an epic journey, from fear of destiny to the glowing triumph of hope.

FOR THE FIRST TIME IN NEW ZEALAND — AUSTRALIAN THRASH LEGENDS MORTAL SIN

Having toured alongside thrash heavyweights Metallica and Testament in their early years, Mortal Sin forged their legacy in the global metal scene from the very beginning. Formed in 1985, they carved their name into the foundations of thrash with a ferocious, high-energy sound that stood shoulder to shoulder with the genre’s elite.

After years of silence, the band has reformed — returning to the stage with the same intensity and aggression that made them icons of the era.

events.long_description:
Girls Rock the Boys - Petone
Girls Rock the Boys began as a spark - a half‑joke, half‑challenge tossed around in a rehearsal room: What would happen if women took on the big, swaggering, stadium‑sized rock anthems that were never written with them in mind? Not only as a tribute, but as a full‑throttle, joyous celebration of the songs that shaped generations.

The idea stuck. Because everyone knows those songs - the ones you belt in the car, the ones that must be played too loud, the ones you recognise from the very first riff. Whitesnake. Boston. Foreigner. Deep Purple. Journey. Rainbow. Led Zeppelin. Uriah Heep. The giants.

But what no one expects is how they feel when powerhouse women take the mic.

Girls Rock the Boys brings together a lineup of women with range, grit, soul, and the kind of stage presence that pulls you straight into the mosh pit. Behind them is a kickass live band built for exactly this music. Together, they tear into the classics - honouring the songs, laughing a little at the very male lyrics now being belted by women.

These anthems were always big enough and wild enough to belong to anyone brave enough to claim them. The result is a show that’s nostalgic and fresh at the same time - and loud in all the right ways.

Girls Rock the Boys is a celebration of musicianship, of women in rock and of the timeless songs that still shake the walls decades later. It’s the classics you love, reimagined.

When women take the mic, the classics hit different. Experience it live with Ashley Hale-Durham, Georgie Sullivan, Jude Madill, and Julie Lamb leading the charge, backed by the stellar band: Andrew Richardson (drums), Matt Fitzpatrick (bass), Aslan Rowlands (guitar), and Duncan Haynes (keys).

🎟️ Early bird tickets $20. Door sales $30.

Hermitude | Wellington
Award-winning Australian electronic duo Hermitude bring their genre-bending live show to Aotearoa this July in support of their acclaimed new album EIGHT.

Australian electronic duo Hermitude have spent more than a decade shaping the future of electronic and hip hop music, earning acclaim for their boundary-pushing sound, global collaborations and explosive live performances. Consisting of Gusto and Dubs from the Blue Mountains west of Sydney, the pair have continually evolved their craft, blending hip hop roots with expansive electronic production that has resonated across headphones, dancefloors and festival stages worldwide. Their new record is inspired by all things uptempo, with a mix of techno, drum & bass and UK garage defining their new sound.

Award-winning multi-instrumentalists, Hermitude broke through internationally with their 2012 album HyperParadise, which won the Australian Music Prize, while the Flume remix of the title track amassed more than 200 million streams. Their follow-up album Dark Night Sweet Light debuted at #1 on the ARIA Charts and went Gold in New Zealand, with single The Buzz becoming a global hit and earning platinum success. Across releases including Pollyanarchy and latest album EIGHT, the duo have continued to push into new sonic territory while maintaining the experimental edge that has defined their career.

The collaborative spirit of Hermitude extends throughout their catalogue, having worked with artists including Kimbra, Flume, Bibi Bourelly and BJ The Chicago Kid, while also remixing tracks for acts such as ODESZA and Alison Wonderland.

With a globally celebrated catalogue and forward-thinking club sound, Hermitude’s return promises an electrifying live experience this July.

events.venue: Meow,9 Edward Street, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Vera Ellen - Heave Knows What Time
Aotearoa Music Award-winning and Taite Award-winning artist Vera Ellen releases her new album Heaven Knows What Time. on May 1 via Flying Nun Records. Alongside the album release, Vera Ellen returns to Aotearoa in July for a six-date national tour in celebration of Heaven Knows What Time.

The title Heaven Knows What Time. arrived while Vera was lying on the top bunk of a house truck in Buenos Aires, nearly two years after writing the record and almost a year after completing the mix. After multiple working titles, it surfaced with clarity and immediacy - less a decision than a moment of recognition. It reflects the album’s central tension: frustration and surrender to forces outside of control. As Vera describes it, creativity cannot be demanded - it can be nurtured, but ultimately arrives in its own time, “like a baby”.

The album was written during a two-week songwriting residency in Greytown, awarded through the NZ Pacific Studio Artist Residency Programme. The residency provided space and solitude away from touring and performance, culminating in a performance at Studio 73 for fellow residents and members of the local community.
‍

In her residency application, Vera wrote: “After the heaviness of Ideal Home Noise, I feel it is pressing that I now create an uplifting record that has a guiding message of hope, but from a matured perspective.” While that intention is present, Heaven Knows What Time. resists neat resolution, moving through themes of love, joy, self-assurance, humour, moodiness, and heartbreak - positioning Vera as an observer of both inner and outer worlds.

Alongside extensive touring in Aotearoa — including the 2025 Laneway Festival — Vera has performed internationally with her band, including a 14-date tour of China, a sold-out run in Australia supporting Crowded House, appearances at New Colossus Festival and SXSW (Austin and Sydney), and a full UK/EU support tour with Yumi Zouma. She is set to support Aldous Harding on her full UK/EU tour and perform at The Great Escape in Brighton. The Guardian described her performance as: “Arising New Zealand empress Vera Ellen and band were a revelation, a shimmering reminder that pop’n’roll can still nudge one’s soul.”

events.long_description:
Mastering Paella Workshop
Learn to authentically create Paella by Spanish Embassy Special guest chef, Edrick Corban-Banks, from Casa Paella.

About this Event

In collaboration with the Embassy of Spain in New Zealand and Casa Paella, we are proud to offer a one-day workshop taught by the award-winning chef, Edrick Corban-Banks.
Chef Edrick is the owner of Casa Paella, Casa Paella holds the official ICEX “Restaurants from Spain” quality seal, recognising its place within Spain’s international network of restaurants committed to authenticity, quality, and the promotion of Spanish gastronomy. This is rare opportunity to learn the culture and traditional Valencian techniques of Paella from a master artisan.



You will spend the day in Teams of 2 as Chef Edrick guides you through the creation of the award winning Arroz con Salmón.
Date: 25th July
Time: 9:30am – 3pm (light lunch is included with a glass of Albarino white wine)
Location: Level 2, 52 Cuba Street, Te Aro, Wellington
Allergies: Ingredients in this class contain the following allergens: Fish, Shellfish/Crustaceans, Molluscs, and Sulphates. This dish will be Gluten Free.
You Will Create:
Arroz con Salmón (Salmon Paella featuring Ōra King Salmon)
First developed in Tasmania using Petuna ocean-grown salmon and awarded the
Tetsuya Wakuda “Best Plate” prize at Taste of Tasmania, this paella is designed as a
technique-led masterclass in stock construction, rice absorption, and heat
management. A concentrated seafood fumet—prepared from shellfish and fish
frames—builds depth and structure, allowing the character of premium local salmon
to remain the centre of the dish.
Course Details: During the workshop, you will learn the following skills:
Prepare a fresh seafood stock using fish and shellfish frames
Build flavour through sofrito, saffron, paprika, and olive oil
Cook Valencian paella rice correctly so each grain remains separate
and full of flavour
Manage heat, evaporation, timing, and liquid levels
Understand the difference between cooking “rice with seafood”
and creating a true Mediterranean rice dish
Develop the prized socarrat — the golden crust at the base of the paella
Finish and serve your paella in the traditional shared style
Course Includes: All ingredients and equipment supplied, at the end of the class, participants will sit down together and enjoy the paella they have created with a glass of Albarino white wine.

What is a Le Cordon Bleu Workshop? A Le Cordon Bleu Workshop is a hands-on culinary training session delivered in our professional teaching kitchens. Be personally guided by world class chefs and taught key techniques step-by-step, with chef feedback throughout. This workshop includes a light lunch, and is designed to give you skills you can repeat confidently at home or in a professional setting.
Contact Details: +64 4 472 9800 |
