events.name: Kevin Fraser Live in Wellington NZ • Decadance 2026
events.venue: Harbourside Function Venue,4 Taranaki Street Wharf Cnr Cable & Taranaki St, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Kevin Fraser Live in Wellington NZ • Decadance 2026
Welcome to DECADANCE — a comedy celebration marking 10 years of Kevin Fraser on stage.

Born in 1990, Kevin’s story as an entertainer took an unlikely turn in 2016, when he began filming outrageous accents and characters from a humble container shed in Tasmania, Australia. Those viral videos sparked a journey that moved from small Aussie shows to stages across Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and beyond.

Each year added new chapters: Australia in 2016, more countries joining in 2017, a global explosion by 2018, and a steady climb through 2019, 2020, 2021… all the way to 2025 — with every tour, every city, and every character shaping the phenomenon Kevin is today.

Now, in 2026, Kevin rewinds the clock to bring fans the ultimate throwback party: a decade of chaos, culture, and comedy reimagined for the stage. Expect the nineties nostalgia that shaped him, the container-shed characters that started it all, and the world-travelled stories that turned everyday madness into global punchlines.

This isn’t just a comedy show — it’s a time capsule cracked open, a decade of laughs uncorked, and an invitation to dance through Kevin’s first ten years in comedy.

Event Details:

Date: Sat 25th July 2026

Location: Harbourside Centre (Cable Room)

4 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington 6011, New Zealand

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Pottery - Throwing: Beginners
This is an introduction to the wonderful, organic material that is clay. You'll receive a comprehensive overview to working with clay which will cover all steps from clay preparation and re-cycling through to glazing the finished work. You'll learn to throw basic forms with group demonstration and one-to-one instruction.
Pottery courses are held at Wellington Potters' Association, 130 Grant Road, Thorndon.  All our courses are scheduled up to a year in advance which means the at times we may need to make changes to the original schedule.  Please make sure you check your emails regularly in case of any changes.
All materials included in course fee. For more information about Wellington Potters, click on this link. 
By the end of the course, you'll be able to: 
•  Wedge and re-cycle clay 
•  Demonstrate the basics of working on a pottery wheel 
•  Centre clay on the wheel 
•  Open a centred piece of clay on wheel 
•  Pull clay up to form basic beaker/cylinder shape 
•  Demonstrate the correct use of prepared glazes 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Sewing - All Levels
All levels welcome! Beginning sewers will learn basic skills and techniques and those with some experience will improve their skills and learn tips and tricks.
Beginners - If you're a beginner, you'll start by making a lined bag, which teaches all the basic skills involved. After that you'll move on to a project of your choice, in consultation with the tutor.  Please bring: 1 metre of firm cotton fabric for your bag outer and 1 metre of a lighter cotton fabric for the lining. You'll also need to bring scissors, a Bernina bobbin (this can be purchased from the CEC office on the day of the course for $7), pins, thread to match your outer fabric, an 18 cm zip and tape measure to the first session.
 If you're a returning student, or have already mastered the basic skills, you'll work on your own project so please bring along whatever you're currently working on (or something new) and your sewing kit. 
Please note PDF patterns are not suitable for this course unless you are very experienced in using them;  we strongly recommend patterns from the following companies:  Simplicity, Butterick, New Look or Quicksew.
By the end of the course, you'll have been introduced to basic skills in dressmaking, if beginners, or further skills for the more experienced.
You'll be able to:
• Use all sewing machine equipment and demonstrate basic sewing techniques (basic seams and finishes)
• Begin to read a commercial pattern and select appropriate materials for task
• Cut out and construct a garment using techniques learned
• (In addition), use a variety of advanced sewing techniques e.g. rolled hems, various zip insertions (invisible and standard), make buttonholes or line garments. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. events.id: Understanding and Supporting Your Neurodivergent Child: A Practical Parent Course-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: Understanding and Supporting Your Neurodivergent Child: A Practical Parent Course
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
This course is designed for parents and caregivers of neurodivergent tamariki who want practical, evidence-informed strategies to better support their child’s wellbeing, behaviour, and participation at home and school.
Across three sessions, we will explore the foundations of neurodiversity, including different neurotypes, strengths-based perspectives, and neuroaffirming language. You will gain insight into sensory processing, regulation, and the critical role of connection and co-regulation in supporting your child.
The course also provides guidance on navigating Aotearoa New Zealand’s health, education, and disability systems, including how to access supports and advocate effectively for your child. We will explore common challenges such as school refusal, burnout, and meltdowns, with practical strategies for prevention, in-the-moment support, and recovery.
There will be opportunities for discussion, reflection, and shared learning, as well as a Q&A-style panel session incorporating both professional and lived experience perspectives.
This is a group-based learning environment (not individual therapy), with an emphasis on practical tools, connection, and empowerment.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

Watercolour Paint and Wine Night in Wellington - It's Wine Time
Looking for a unique night out in Wellington? Join us for a beginner-friendly watercolour painting event where you’ll explore fluid colour mixing, delicate brushwork, and create your own watercolour artwork … in a bar!

Our artist guides you step-by-step through the watercolour process, so absolutely no art experience is needed. You’ll be encouraged to add your own personal touch along the way, making each painting uniquely yours. It’s the perfect excuse to try something new, switch off, and enjoy a relaxed night of creativity and good vibes.

𝗗𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗸𝘀: No drinks are included in the ticket price, but drinks are available for purchase.

𝗙𝗼𝗼𝗱: A delicious menu will be available to purchase throughout the event.

𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗶𝘀 𝗣𝗮𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗲?
It’s a fun social painting class where our artists will run you through step-by-step instructions on how to create your very own masterpiece in a fun and relaxed bar setting. Perfect for dates, catching up with mates or for meeting new friends!

We provide all the materials you need (high-quality watercolour paper, watercolour paint, brushes). All you need to bring is your creative spirit. Our events are held in licensed venues, so you can purchase drinks to sip on while you paint. At the end of the night, you’ll leave with a watercolour painting you created yourself – you might even surprise yourself with what you can achieve!

For tickets, future events, FAQs and more info head to ➡️ [ https://paintvine.co.nz/]

This course gives you the opportunity to explore and sharpen both your technical and creative skills, so you have the ability and vision to capture the enchanting world that resides in the darkness.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Identify the equipment needed to take photographs at night
• Learn fundamentals of photography composition and editing of night images
• Identify how to use technical photographic tools in a night time context
• Explore techniques that allow you to develop a more creative approach to picture making including: light painting, intentional camera movement and light trails

Storytelling On Stage
Do you love storytelling shows like The Moth? Come join the growing art of live non-fiction storytelling. Learn how to find ideas from your life, craft a compelling narrative, and deliver your personal story in a confident and entertaining way.
 Website description:
Live storytelling is an artform unto itself, requiring different skills and techniques from standup comedy or prose writing. In this four-part workshop, you’ll learn:
- Creative writing exercises and daily practices to to find meaningful stories from your life
- Tools for crafting a compelling personal narrative
- Techniques to build suspense, drama, and humour into your stories
- Stagecraft and performance skills to heighten and polish your delivery
By the end of the class you'll have
- One or more polished 5-10 minute stories to showcase on stage
- Dozens of ideas to expand upon for future stories
- Writing practices to improve your life as a creative
- Less stage fright and more confidence as a speaker

events.venue: Parliament of New Zealand,1 Molesworth Street, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
Celebrate Being Queer AF - Rally at Parliament
40 Years of Love: Parliament Rally
Followed by a dance on the steps with music from Vinyl&Proud. 🏳️‍🌈🏳️‍⚧️

Join us on the steps of Parliament as we come together to celebrate 40 years since the passing of Homosexual Law Reform in Aotearoa New Zealand.

This rally is an opportunity to honour the courage, determination, and sacrifice of those who fought for change, reflect on the progress that has been made, and celebrate the generations of LGBTQ+ people who have helped shape a more inclusive society.

As we mark this significant milestone, we also recognise that the journey towards equality is not complete. Together, we will raise our voices for the issues that still matter today and inspire the next generation to continue the work of building a fairer, safer, and more inclusive future for all.

Bring your pride, your passion, and your commitment to justice as we celebrate the past, stand together in the present, and look ahead to the future.

Everyone is welcome.

events.name: Distilled Comedy
events.venue: The Bond Store,3C Magrath Ave, Paraparaumu Beach, Paraparaumu 5032, New Zealand, Paraparaumu
events.long_description:
Distilled Comedy
The monthly merriment kicks off on July 29th — and we bring light to the depth of winter.

Welcome to the comedy open mic that politely asks structure to wait outside while we set fire to it.

This is the Home of The Jar — our slightly unhinged, deeply democratic system where the audience randomly selects who goes up next. No lineups. No pecking order. No sacred cows. Just brave humans, questionable decisions, and whatever name comes out of the jar. It’s equal parts comedy show, social experiment, and mild psychological thriller.

You might see a first-timer stepping up for their debut. You might see a seasoned comic testing fresh material. You might see someone absolutely smash it. You might see someone realise, in real time, that jokes are harder than they look. That’s the magic.

Come in from the cooler autumn air, grab some food, sip a cocktail, and settle in. The room fills fast, the energy builds quicker, and being there from the start means you’re fully invested when the jar starts causing trouble.

If you love comedy in its rawest, most unpredictable form — this is your night.
If you’ve ever thought, “I could probably do that” — the jar would love to meet you.

Cheap laughs. Big vibes. Absolute chaos.

events.long_description:
Creative Writing - A Tasting Plate
How often have you said, ‘I wish I could write’? There are many different kinds of writing. Starting is easy so why not give it a go by joining this creative writing ‘tasting plate’.
Each week we’ll focus on a different area of fiction or creative non-fiction. By the end of the programme, you’ll have tried your hand at writing a short story, a narrative poem, a travel memoir, a personal essay drawing from your life, an interview article, a story for children, a short film script and a piece of historical fiction.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
• Create works of fiction 
• Develop creative non-fiction text 
• Explore the natural inner spirit of writing 
• Discover your unique writer’s voice 
• Reflect on your own experiences in writing 
• Investigate different writing strategies
• Discover where your personal writing passions sit and what works for you.
Bring pen and paper or a laptop. 
This course is designed to help you improve your skills, to develop your unique writer's voice and to encourage you to take risks on the page. It is not a course where you'll be asked to read your work out loud, critique other writers work, or hand in your writing to the tutor. This is a safe place where you will be supported to do what writers do best - write.

events.id: Exploring our Shared Humanity-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: Exploring our Shared Humanity
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Join experienced psychotherapist Rohit Grover for a six-week course that invites you to look beyond the surface of everyday life. In these two-hour sessions, we will explore the core tenets of existential therapy, moving away from the conventional focus on self and hedonism. Instead, we'll grapple with life's big questions:
What does it truly mean to live a value-driven life?
Do our personal values matter, or is the search for meaning just an illusion?
What is the "being" part of "human being" all about?
Through guided discussions, reflective exercises, and insights from classic existential thinkers, Rohit will help you navigate this profound territory. This isn't about finding easy answers. It's about developing the courage to ask the right questions, to confront the realities of freedom, responsibility, and meaning, and to discover a more authentic way of living.
This course is for anyone ready to step off the treadmill and begin a deeper exploration of what it means to be alive. Come and find out what it means to truly exist
Upon completion of this course, participants will be able to:
Differentiate between a life driven by external pressures or fleeting pleasures and one rooted in personal values and authentic meaning.
Identify and critically examine the core existential givens of human existence, such as freedom, responsibility, isolation, and the search for meaning.
Articulate a personal understanding of what it means to "be" a human being, moving beyond a purely functional or biological definition.
Arrive at sensing rather than thinking. Sensing this existence, this dance of life. Widen your view of existence.
Note: Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Mindfulness Meditation
Meditation can help us with life’s challenges and is a wise way to work with strong emotions and stress, as well as enlivening the ordinary times. It’s simple and doesn’t need any special resources. Often learning to meditate is presented as something esoteric and mysterious but really it should be a straightforward thing based on our everyday experience.
Come along to this course and learn how to put a meditation practice in place in your life. You’ll be introduced to some different meditation and mindfulness techniques and get an insight into the modern psychology and the ancient wisdom that supports a meditation practice.
The four sessions will provide time to practise different styles of meditation, lots of hints about a fruitful approach to take to set up a regular practice in your life and opportunities to discuss progress with others in the group.
By the end of the course, you’ll be able to:
Describe some ways in which modern psychology and ancient wisdom support meditation
Understand what you need to do to make time for meditation in your life
Describe practical tips to make meditation fruitful
Practise different kinds of guided and silent meditation
Find resources (books, on-line information, other classes and retreats) to support your meditation
Bring a notepad and pen. 
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Qi Gong
Qigong has both psychological and physical components and involves the regulation of the mind, breath, and body’s movement and posture.
In most forms of qigong:
Breath is slow, long, and deep. Breath patterns may switch from abdominal breathing to breathing combined with speech sounds.
Movements are typically gentle and smooth, aimed for relaxation.
Mind regulation includes focusing one’s attention and visualization.
Dynamic (active) qigong techniques primarily focus on body movements, especially movements of the whole body or arms and legs. Meditative (passive) qigong techniques can be practiced in any posture that can be maintained over time and involve breath and mind exercises, with almost no body movement.
Wear loose, comfortable clothing and bring a bottle of water.
[This is a physical activity that involves an element of risk.  While all possible measures are taken to prevent accidents or injury, please note that participation is at your own risk].

The repetitive movements of crochet help the brain make more serotonin, which can decrease tension and feelings of depression. We’ll move through all the steps from the starting slipknot to reading patterns and diagrams and making your first crochet projects.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Photography: Unlocking the Secrets to Captivating Images
Elevate your photography from ordinary to extraordinary and ensure your work stands out in the digital age. Creating captivating photographs and understanding what makes a photograph engaging is something every photographer should master. Camera settings are essential, but once you know them, you need to learn how to take photographs that stir emotions, impact your audience, and leave a lasting impression. After all, isn’t that the true purpose of photography? People don’t want to see the same landscapes or flowers they’ve seen thousands of times. But how do you turn what you love into something that makes people go, "Wow"?
Captivation in photography means stopping a viewer in their tracks, making them look, feel, and connect. It’s about delivering a photograph that enthrals, evokes profound emotions, and shifts perspectives.
In a world brimming with images, only a few have the power to truly captivate and linger in our memories.
 This pioneering course is your gateway to mastering the art of creating captivating photographs at a time when AI-generated images are saturating our visual landscape. Create something genuine and memorable—images that spark curiosity, evoke emotions, and inspire changes in perception. It's time to define your unique style, refine your vision, and make your mark.
 Course Outcomes
 By the end of the course, you’ll be able to: 
Identify the foundational elements that transform an ordinary image into a captivating one.
Create photographs that make people say "Wow" by applying techniques that add a spark of wonder to your shots.
Infuse your photographs with curiosity, making each frame a source of intrigue and interest.
Understand why some images linger in memory and how to make your photographs unforgettable.
Develop a unique style and vision that sets your work apart in the crowded digital landscape.

Improv is theatre without a script and a fun way to build your skills in many areas, including team work, public speaking, storytelling and on-your-feet creative thinking.

events.long_description:
Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society EP release tour (Pōneke/Wgtn) #1
The wave doesn’t conform to the shape of the rock. It smashes it. The sea doesn’t pretend to be hospitable. It summons courage. And a shantyband never licks the captain's boot. They release another EP!

The best shanties invite us to open our hearts along with the bottle. To draw strength from camaraderie and drown our pettinesses. To seek the rough edge of the wave and savour the salt within. And so, the WSSS have issued a call to arms with their new collection: Never Mind the Rowlocks, Here’s the Wellington Sea Shanty Society.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

Lin Seal | Wellington Nautical History Monthly

⚓⚓⚓

The scuttlebutt is true...⛵

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor squall of pure shanty.

ALL SHOWS

WED 3 JUNE - 5Tapped Limited, Waiharakeke/Blenheim
THU 4 JUNE - Scott’s Brewing, Ōamaru
FRI 5 JUNE - Pioneer Hall, Ōtepoti/Dunedin

SUN 7 JUNE - The Dog’s Bone, Whakatū/Nelson

SAT 4 JULY - Leigh Sawmill, Leigh (Arvo show)
SUN 5 JULY - Calliope Sea Scout Hall, Devonport
FRI - 31 JULY - Breaker Bay Hall, Pōneke/Wellington #1
SAT - 1 AUG - Breaker Bay Hall, Pōneke/Wellington (KIDS show)
SAT - 1 AUG - Breaker Bay Hall, Pōneke/Wellington #2

Tickets to all shows: https://wellingtonseashantysociety.com/shows


⚓⚓⚓

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

The Pearl Jam Experience Announces Ultimate Greatest Hits Tour for New Zealand

Kiwi rock fans are in for the ultimate celebration of grunge history as The Pearl Jam Experience crosses the Tasman to deliver a definitive, career-spanning greatest hits set. This special tour will honour the massive catalog of the Seattle icons, delivering a full-throttle, high-energy performance packed to the brim with Pearl Jam’s biggest anthems and fan favourites.
Widely regarded as the premier tribute to Pearl Jam, the band is renowned for recreating the atmosphere, the madness, and most importantly, the sonically accurate music that defined a generation.
Their commitment to the music’s authenticity goes beyond the stage. In a remarkable nod to Pearl Jam’s golden era, the band recently recorded a collaborative cover of the hit song Go with former Pearl Jam drummer Dave Abbruzzese. Abbruzzese, who drove the rhythm section during the band's peak explosive years, lent his signature powerful drumming to the track and mixed it for the group.
The Pearl Jam Experience also maintains a deep connection to the band's philanthropic legacy. They are proud supporters of the EB Research Partnership (EBRP), the largest nonprofit funding research for a cure for Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB), co-founded by Jill and Eddie Vedder.
For New Zealand fans, this is the ultimate chance to experience a high-octane concert that embodies the true sound and spirit of Pearl Jam, delivered with the energy, precision, and respect this legendary rock catalog deserves.

San Fran holds a Supervised License. Minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue.

The Pearl Jam Experience also maintains a deep connection to the band's philanthropic legacy. They are proud supporters of the EB Research Partnership (EBRP), the largest nonprofit funding research for a cure for Epidermolysis Bullosa (EB), co-founded by Jill and Eddie Vedder.

For New Zealand fans, this is the ultimate chance to experience a high-octane concert that embodies the true sound and spirit of Pearl Jam, delivered with the energy, precision, and respect this legendary rock catalog deserves.

events.long_description: How did Wellington become a culinary paradise? Capital of Kai tells the story through 100 years of Wellington's food creatives, restaurant workers, and café culture. It's a love letter to the hospo whānau who have shaped the city. Walk through galleries of heritage treasures: the Green Parrot's working griddle, Hiakai's light-up signage, Il Casino's couch, Shanghai restaurant's 1980s menu, the Matterhorn café's cowbell. You'll see the arc from 1930s British hotel dining (roast mutton, boiled vegetables, milky tea) through European influences brought home by migrants and travellers, and the diverse cuisines - Chinese, Malaysian, Indian, Syrian, Greek, Māori - that define Wellington now. Hungry for more? Feed your curiosity at Capital of Kai.

Expect proper tavern fare built for winter nights and long conversations: slow-braised beef and dark ale pie with mash and winter greens, lamb shoulder with rosemary jus, roasted kūmara and caramelised onion tart. events.id: Wellington Opera — Manon-St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
events.name: Wellington Opera — Manon
events.venue: St James Theatre, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
For its 2026 season, Wellington Opera brings one of the most popular and enduring French operas to life. Manon by Jules Massenet will feature Kiwi-Samoan tenor Pene Pati and Kiwi-Egyptian soprano Amina Edris. Joining this powerhouse duo is another New Zealander, baritone Phillip Rhodes will sing the role of Lescaut. Manon tells the tragic love story of Manon Lescaut and the Chevalier des Grieux. The story unfolds in five acts, exploring themes of love, desire, and the consequences of choices made in pursuit of pleasure. 
Pene Pati is widely known for his Sol3 Mio fame. He is a recent New Zealand Arts Laureate and is the first Samoan tenor to perform on the world’s top stages, including the Opéra national de Paris, Covent Garden, London and the Metropolitan Opera, New York.

events.name: Pāua to the People
events.venue: Cambridge Road Vineyard, 32 Cambridge Road
events.long_description:
For many of us, pāua is widely known, yet rarely tried beyond fritters, or the classic creamed version. Get it right, though, and it deserves a place at any kiwi table. Get it wrong and you may as well sole your boots with it. 

Join a collection of chefs, fishermen, and locals for a deep dive into the life, nutrition, and uses of our most iconic seafood. The masterclass starts with local wine, then into demonstrations of technique in the despatch, preparation, and cooking of pāua, and open forum discussion as you explore ultimate expressions of this taonga. Roll your sleeves up to learn techniques first-hand at a grazing pace, with refreshments to hand. A communal meal follows, celebrating our local oceans and prepared by masterful chefs. Pāua appears eight ways, kelp in all its glory, and smoke, fire, and fish take centre stage. 
Your ticket includes welcome beverages, eight courses featuring pāua in multiple expressions, matched wines or non-alcoholic options throughout.

events.id: Crying Tiger-Tuk Tuk Thai Kitchen, 15 Hartham Place North-WOAP
events.name: Crying Tiger
events.venue: Tuk Tuk Thai Kitchen, 15 Hartham Place North
events.long_description:
Charcoal smoke, sizzling meat, and you're in Nong Khai, a small northeast Thai town where families gather around the grill for Crying Tiger steak. Beef steak marinated 48 hours in coriander root, garlic, black pepper, oyster sauce, palm sugar, whiskey, and mandarin juice, char-grilled until the meat weeps with its own juices.
The chef grew up cooking this dish with family and friends. It arrives with sticky rice and a Northern Thai Isarn dipping sauce of tamarind, lime juice, ground chillies, and fresh coriander. Alongside: a sharp granny smith apple salad dressed with chilli and fish sauce, topped with prawns; and tom zapp, slow-cooked pork soft bones that melt into a soup fragrant with kaffir lime, lemongrass, and ground rice.
This is a three course set menu for $75.  Alcohol can be purchased separately.  Minimum 2 orders per table.

Cultivating true resilience is an intentional practice of the mind, body, and soul. It is rooted in deep self-knowledge and personal empowerment. In our rapidly changing world, the ultimate question we must ask ourselves is: How can I unlock my unique strengths and capacities to not just survive these demanding times, but truly thrive?

events.name: Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society EP release tour (Pōneke/Wgtn) #2

events.long_description:
Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society EP release tour (Pōneke/Wgtn) #2
The wave doesn’t conform to the shape of the rock. It smashes it. The sea doesn’t pretend to be hospitable. It summons courage. And a shantyband never licks the captain's boot. They release another EP!

The best shanties invite us to open our hearts along with the bottle. To draw strength from camaraderie and drown our pettinesses. To seek the rough edge of the wave and savour the salt within. And so, the WSSS have issued a call to arms with their new collection: Never Mind the Rowlocks, Here’s the Wellington Sea Shanty Society.

Never fear if you find yourself adrift on a sea of AI slop, lapping at your hull, lulling you to sleep — Lake Davineer, Vorn dont Le Père Était Marin, Young Nic, Tomas el Largo, and Louis Quatorze are back again to fill your sails and slap the codfish slime clean off your cheeks.

Just when everyone is lamenting the empty galleys of the good ship Wellington, and those ol’ scurvy-mongers are promising renewed bounty if you would only tack five degrees to port or starboard come election time, these songs remind us the sea at least will sustain us, and there’s rum and (metaphorical) guns for them that wants to fight.

Lin Seal | Wellington Nautical History Monthly

⚓⚓⚓

The scuttlebutt is true...⛵

The most seaworthy sea shanty band in the South Pacific is releasing their long-awaited 4th collection of new and old maritime bangers:
'Never Mind the Rowlocks - Here's the Wellington Sea Shanty Society'.

All aboard as we set sail for the salty horizon. Prepare to be battered once again by the 4-sailor squall of pure shanty.


⚓⚓⚓

WELLINGTON SEA SHANTY SOCIETY

Aotearoa New Zealand's Most 'Sea Worthy' Shanty Group™ have been belting out traditional and original sea songs from Aotearoa, France, Spain, the UK and more, since time immemorial (2012).
The W.S.S.S have toured Aotearoa and France multiple times and are known for their rowdy and participatory live shows. They've performed at Paimpol (one of the world's largest shanty festivals), Splore, Albany Folk Festival (Aus), Quebec Sea Shanty Festival (Canada) and a shipload of other festivals in NZ, France & Canada.

They will be playing new classics from their forthcoming EP 'Never Mind the Rowlocks' as well as your foamy favourites from the 'Sea Shanties of the 70s, 80s, & Today!' EP and their 'Now That's What I Call Sea Shanties' series.

South Summit are soon to release their sophomore album, RUN IT BACK on June 12 and to celebrate, they have announced RUN IT BACK NZ TOUR.
Coming to Aotearoa this July and August the band will take on Queenstown hotspot Yonder on Thursday 30 July, The Loons, Lyttleton on Friday 31 July, San Fran, Wellington on Saturday 1 August and Auckland’s Double Whammy on Sunday 2 August. 
Run It Back marks the band's second album, featuring stand out singles ‘TOP OF THE HILL’ and ‘ON THE DASH’ which have sent strong signals toward the confident evolution of their sound. The twelve-track record  represents a period of experimentation for the band; one where they found themselves pulled towards threads of funk, hip hop and R&B, while also driven by a desire to galvanise their signature blend of reggae and rock.
In 2024, they released their highly anticipated debut album The Bliss, a reggae-infused indie rock record that showcased both tight songwriting and a willingness to experiment across styles. It debuted at #2 on the ARIA Album Charts and propelled the band into a new tier, with heavy Triple J support, major festival slots and international touring, including appearances at Falls Festival, Groovin The Moo, SXSW Sydney, Vivid LIVE Debut at the Sydney Opera House plus a huge Australasian headline tour.
After a recent visit to Aotearoa to play at Six 60’s new Country & Roots Festival Sweet Home Aotearoa, South Summit now return to New Zealand for their third headline tour in the country. These four shows promise the bands’ renowned live charisma and classic fan favourites, whilst welcoming fans into a brand new era. 

San Fran holds a Supervised License, meaning minors are welcome to attend events at San Fran so long as they are accompanied by a legal guardian at all times whilst at the venue. Minors are of course not allowed to purchase alcohol under any circumstance.

events.id: Kumutoto Kai me te Kōrero-Graze Wine Bar, 95 Upland Road-WOAP
events.name: Kumutoto Kai me te Kōrero
events.venue: Graze Wine Bar, 95 Upland Road
events.long_description:
Kumutoto Awa was one of the living streams of Pōneke long before the city buried it underground in 1866. This four-hour guided hīkoi traces its path from the Kelburn hills to the waterfront, connecting it through kai, kōrero, and the people who are working to restore the place of the awa in the city's future – The Kumutoto Restoration Project. You'll start with a light lunch and cocktail at Graze in Kelburn which will be a collaboration between Chef Max Gordy and the Kumutoto Community Orchard founder and avid forager Milan Magan. You will also meet your hosts Martin and Micheline who will regale you with stories about Wellington's lost streams. From there, the group walks to the only remaining stretch of the Kumutoto stream still visible above ground, where soup waits alongside more kōrero about the whakapapa of the awa. The route then follows the buried path of Kumutoto down the Terrace to Bert's Bar for a final cocktail created with a foraged ingredients from Kumutoto before finishing at the mouth of the awa on the waterfront. All food and drinks across the event are included in your ticket, with ingredients foraged from the Kumutoto Community Orchard and ngahere. Wear comfortable shoes and dress for the weather. The route covers approximately two kilometres and includes steps.
The ticket price includes an optional foraging workshop with Milan Magan. You'll spend an hour in the orchard and ngahere learning about what you'll be eating and drinking the following day. Saturday 1 & 29 August 9-10am.

events.name: Next Gen Cook Off
events.venue: LTD., Level 1, 60 Dixon Street
events.long_description:
The first four Mondays in August, an up-and-coming chef takes over the Everybody Eats kitchen at LTD and delivers a three-course dinner built from rescued food, cooking it their way and style. Walk in, take a seat, and let the Everybody Eats volunteers whānau take care of the rest. No bookings. Pay what you can. 
Sixth year running, and the model stays simple: good food, good company, and a room full of people making a difference one plate at a time. Every course uses rescued ingredients, because eating is fundamental and everyone deserves access to something . 

3 August — Oscar Little, Hummingbird
Oscar Little started his culinary career five years ago as a commis chef at Shed 5 and The Crabshack, where he learned what it means to commit to a team. He’s since worked his way up to chef de partie at Hummingbird. Along the way he’s volunteered with Everybody Eats, and it’s that spirit of giving back to the community that drives him to compete this year.

10 August — Brayden Puketapu, Koji
At 22, Brayden Puketapu is already developing a cooking voice that’s distinctly his own. Working at Koji, he’s drawn to the creative challenge of transforming overlooked ingredients and putting his own stamp on both classic and contemporary dishes. His heritage is central to that identity, grounding his food in something personal while keeping it fresh and inventive.

17 August — Eugenous Evan, Rosella
Indonesian-born Eugenous Evan came to Wellington five years ago and hasn’t looked back. After stints at Shepherd, Hillside & Daisy’s, and Supra, he’s now chef de partie at Rosella, where he’s been for just over a year. For Eugenous, cooking is an act of care: a way to share something of himself with every person who sits down to eat.

24 August — Aryan Dhankhhar, Mr Go’s
Aryan Dhankhhar’s love of food started young, holding weekend cooking competitions with his sister and himself in their family kitchen in Haryana, India, with their mother as judge. Since then he’s built a career spanning hotels, restaurants, and catering, working across techniques from sous vide to traditional barbecue. A highlight: leading the team at Wilson Barbecue during Wellington On a Plate 2024, where they set a world record selling over 6,000 burgers in a single day. Now at Mr Go’s, he brings that same drive and precision to every plate.

Next Gen Cook Off is proudly supported by The Gas Hub.

For Chef Shuchi dessert has always been the most emotional part of a meal. It's where people slow down, and where conversation softens. For this event you're encouraged to skip right to dessert for this five course dessert tasting menu each tied to a memory. Some from Shuchi's life, some shared in our collective memories, all rooted in the small, often overlooked moments that shape how we experience sweetness.

Raspberry panna cotta tastes like school lunches and summer berries. Rich brownie with hazelnut mousse is the sweet thing you crave after a long day. The lemon cake that became Le Ciel's bestseller without anyone realising. Apple crumble soufflé carries memories of Shuchi's grandmother. Passionfruit posset brings the taste of home from Tanzania. Each course is plated with technique and restraint, refined, but never losing its warmth or intent. You'll spend an evening in the warm, slow space where dessert deserves to be.

Your ticket includes five plated courses plus one palate cleanser.

events.venue: Chow, Level 1, 45 Tory Street
events.long_description:
Chow celebrates the most powerful recommendation of all: the one passed across a family table. Jimmy Mahakit (Isaan, Thailand) and Kunpheng "Ricki" Zhu (Jiangsu, near Shanghai) have each spent ten years as Sous Chefs at Chow. For one night, they cook together, each presenting dishes learned at home through watching, tasting, and being guided at the stove. These are home-learned recipes, passed down through families and remembered rather than written. That's word of mouth in its purest form.

Jimmy's cooking leans bold, herb-heavy, and grilled, with chilli heat and fermentation. Ricki's focuses on balance, braise, clarity, and precision. The evening follows Chow's signature format across eight shared courses: herb-led, grilled, fried, and braised, finishing with a composed dessert from each chef. Portions are substantial and designed for sharing. Then what begins as dinner becomes a proper Chow party, with matched cocktails flowing and a DJ building the energy.

Your ticket includes an eight-course sharing dinner and four half cocktails matched across the courses. Additional drinks and optional matched cocktail pairings are available for purchase.

events.id: Raising Great Kids in an Overindulgent World-Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington-Wellington High School
events.name: Raising Great Kids in an Overindulgent World
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Raising Great Kids in an Overindulgent World
This workshop will be a confronting one that will expose you to the risks that children face in this modern overindulgent world. Many have become used to being the constant centre of attention and are unable to delay gratification and aren’t competent in everyday skills. They have few self-care skills and skills relating to others, can’t take personal responsibility and don’t know what is enough or what is “normal” for others – these children end up having a difficult time of it in life and you will too.
 You’ll take away new insight and knowledge plus strategies that you can apply that very night to help your child to be a responsible, likeable and respectful person.
By the end of the session, you’ll be able to:
• Reflect on the current context parents are faced with today
• Find the relevant research
• Practise the parenting tools and discuss the model
• Know where to go to get support
Aimed at parents, grandparents and caregivers of children of all ages.
Note:  Courses need a minimum number to go ahead so if we don't have enough enrolments a few days before the start date, we have to cancel. We'll let you know by email so please check yours regularly. If you need to cancel your registration, here are our terms and conditions: "What You Need to Know".

events.long_description:
Executive Chef Carl Maunder has spent two decades with truffles: exploring, refining dishes that let them truly shine, building an entire culinary philosophy around one ingredient. 

Indulge in five courses built around Périgord and Bianchetto truffles at the height of their season. Hand-prepared scallops with truffle, beef fillet Rossini reimagined, house-made truffle brie. It's nostalgic and a little tongue-in-cheek: a highbrow, lowbrow take built for people who grew up on battered everything. 
Book a table or walk in for a one-hour sitting between 5–10pm and order from a succinct menu that treats the classics with care, without taking them too seriously. Drinks are there to smash back: Spritzes, crisp whites, and Waikato from the chilli bin. Dishes and drinks range from $6–$16.

Madeira has been too often overlooked. It sits in grandmother's cabinet waiting for cooking or forgotten entirely. But Madeira is built to last, it's a quietly complex wine that deserves discovery. Noble Rot will spend an afternoon proving it to you.
The afternoon begins with a welcome cocktail before settling into a three-course long lunch served sharing style at the table, in the traditional Mediterranean spirit. Your ticket covers a themed arrival cocktail, three generous sharing courses, and six Madeira wines paired throughout the afternoon.

events.venue: Boneface Brewing Co., Unit 14, 27 Blenheim St
events.long_description:
Rodney Scott has been cooking whole-hog barbecue over coals since he was eleven years old. By seventeen, he was working the pits full time. What began as a kid helping out at his parents' roadside business eventually became one of the most celebrated careers in American barbecue. In 2018, Scott was named Best Chef: Southeast by the James Beard Foundation, the second pitmaster ever to win a James Beard chef award. He has appeared alongside Anthony Bourdain in Parts Unknown, and in 2020 was profiled on an episode of Chef's Table: BBQ, showcasing his South Carolina whole hog style. 

Boneface Brewing in Upper Hutt will be transformed for the occasion: American cars out front, whole hogs slow cooking over a fire pit, long trestle tables set up beer-hall style inside, live music, flash tattoos, and a specially brewed Boneface collaboration beer made for the day. Scott will be cooking his signature whole hog alongside a second protein, two hot sides, two cold sides, bread, and condiments. Staff will be dressed for it. So should you!

Your ticket includes food and entertainment. Beverages and flash tattoos are payable on the day.

This International Chef Collaboration is proudly supported by the New Zealand Government’s Events Boost Fund.

events.name: Overcoming Imposter Syndrome for Creatives
events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Overcoming Imposter Syndrome for Creatives
There is a widespread ‘lack of confidence’ epidemic among creatives, and if you have ever felt like your work is not good enough, hesitated to submit your art to competitions, or doubted your skills when applying for creative jobs, you are not alone! Creatives often feel imposter syndrome most acutely. Unlike other industries, those in the creative field produce something new every time, and sharing this with the world can be daunting, even for established artists.
 This pervasive self-doubt, known as imposter syndrome, affects countless artists and creators, often holding them back from realising their full potential. This concise workshop is designed to help you uncover the roots of this inner voice of insecurity and provide you with effective tools to overcome it. Through engaging activities and practical exercises, you will learn how to transform self-doubt into a source of strength, empowering you to confidently share your unique talents with the world.
 What you won't find in this masterclass: This is not a session about general self-growth or self-confidence, and it does not include positive affirmations or self-talk. All the information provided is based on scientific research and is applicable to all creative sectors.
Bring along some examples of your work on the day (eg a painting, a photograph of your work, etc).
 By the end of this workshop, you’ll be able to: 
Identify and challenge the origins of your imposter syndrome.
Apply practical techniques to silence your inner critic.
Share your creative work with increased confidence.
Turn self-doubt into a motivational tool.
Recognise and celebrate your achievements as a creative professional.

events.venue: Wellington High School, 249 Taranaki Street, Te Aro, Wellington
events.long_description:
Retirement Reinvented
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
In your middle years, working, retired or somewhere in between? What’s next? Life is about much more than work or leisure, but most of us have given little thought to what “retirement” might mean.
It’s difficult to speculate what may happen in the future – but we can be proactive and take control.
This course offers insights into how to make the most of our time once we’re less focused on career and/or childrearing. It covers many of the issues people face when considering a move from current employment to a different lifestyle that includes more time to do the things we’ve always promised ourselves we’d do – “when we retire”.
After the workshop, you’ll be able to identify a number of common issues and potential ways to manage them when considering and planning your “rejuvenation”, rather than a retirement. We won’t cover financial planning, but will focus on some of the personal growth opportunities for living and making a conscious contribution to your community.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.
By the end of the day, you’ll have:
Developed your own perspective on ageing and retirement in the 21st Century and identified what’s important to you
Completed a personal life audit exercise and considered your values and your strengths
Considered options to include a sense of purpose and explore choices that can provide you with that sense of purpose
Explored possibilities in the major aspects of your life and identified potential challenges and strategies for overcoming them

events.long_description:
Sculpture - Intro to Creature Sculpting
Join us for a fun day of creature making! Design and sculpt a one-of-a-kind character in your own style from polymer clays in a full spectrum of colours!

Working with oven-cured clays and wrapped wire armatures, this workshop offers a variety of modelling methods and approaches - a great opportunity to turn sketches & ideas into tangible 3D forms. Modern clay inventions mean we can create translucent, glittery, semi-flexible, UV reactive or even glow-in-the-dark elements to add more realism or a touch of the surreal into each creation!

Students will be coached through designing and creating a small-scale creature sculpture, beginning simple, and building to a more complex final form as we get familiar with materials.

The class offers beginner students a fun introduction to sculpting organic forms from scratch, and for those with some hands-on creative experience, it offers a great opportunity to experiment, hone and advance your making skills to new levels.

If you can, bring along some design ideas, sketches or reference images to help kick start the sculpting process on the day.

Please wear closed-in footwear suitable for a workshop environment. bring a work apron if you have one or wear clothes you don’t mind getting a little grubby. Remember to bring your reading glasses if you have them.

2026 Natokbaaj production coming up – mark the date in your calendar!

We’re back again this year with something new! For the first time, Wellington Natokbaaj is going to produce a murder mystery, Nishi-dham Hatya Rahasya (‘Murder at Nishi-dham’).

The plot is adapted from a novel written by the Queen of Crime, Agatha Christie. We have transported the story to the small town of Birpur in the pre-mobile, pre-Internet era of the 1980s. Our two quirky detectives – Tuni and Bulu – solve a murder occurring at the dilapidated mansion ‘Nishi-dham,’ owned by the enigmatic young woman Billie Mullick.

True to the Natokbaaj pledge, we have aimed to blend pure comedy into the narrative; hoping to bring to you an enjoyable experience of fun and excitement with a dash of fear. Come clue-hunting with us!

The Wellington Salsa Ball returns in 2026 to bring together live music and dancers from across the region for the city’s biggest Latin dance social of the year!

There’s a reason Pravda’s scones have a following. This hands-on class lifts the lid on what makes them so good, and gives you the chance to make your own.

events.long_description:
A musical journey through art, stories, and seasonal food, with a touch of opera. 

Bellbird invites you beyond traditional dining into a sensory experience shaped by music, storytelling, and contemporary art. Inspired by the haunting song of the korimako (bellbird), you'll explore purakau (stories) through art and opera. Two-time Burger Wellington winner, Chef-owner Chetan Pangam crafts a menu celebrating Aotearoa's seasonal abundance: thoughtful integration of native ingredients, local produce, and refined Indian influences, all presented with an artistic lens. 

You'll arrive at Bellbird with a welcome drink and specially selected canapés, then move to the Dowse Art Museum for a private, behind-the-scenes guided tour with the gallery director, unlocking unique stories on display. A five-course sit-down dinner follows inspired by the art, matched with wines from Mishas Vineyard. Conversations flow from table to table, and each course reveals a new layer of meaning tied to land, memory, and identity. 

Your ticket includes a welcome drink, canapés, a five-course dinner, and five glasses of matched wine. Additional drinks available for purchase.

events.name: The Grower's Champagne

events.long_description:
Champagne takes on a different voice when it comes from the hands of the grower. In conjunction with Truffle Wine Imports, Noble Rot presents a premium degustation menu dedicated entirely to Grower Champagne. These are wines crafted by the families who farm their own vineyards and bottle under their own names, often in very limited quantities.
The evening unfolds over five courses, each paired exclusively with Grower Champagnes. Expect individuality, texture, and precision, with some bottles rarely seen beyond their cellar doors. These are wines shaped by site, season, and personal philosophy, offering a clear expression of place rather than a large-scale blended house style.
Throughout the evening, the Noble Rot sommelier team will guide each pour, exploring what sets grower producers apart and why their Champagnes have become some of the region’s most compelling, coveted and sought-after wines.
Your ticket includes an amuse bouche on arrival, five courses, and seven grower champagnes paired throughout the evening.

events.venue: The Opera House, Wellington, New Zealand
events.long_description:
She’s been described as having one-of-a-kind humour, boundless energy, and infectious charm. Comedian and actress Atsuko Okatsuka is heading to Wellington with her latest show, ‘The Big Tour’.   
With podcasts, television and film acting, and standup specials on streaming platforms, Atsuko has gained a huge following. Her previous tour, ‘Full Grown’, sold out over 200 shows across 20 countries. Her latest standup special, ‘Father’, premiered on Disney+ and has made it onto its Top 10 list. 
Atsuko’s viral moments are as legendary as her stand-up. She has ridden a Jeepney (a type of public utility vehicle) in the Philippines and started the #DropChallenge, which helped bring Beyoncé’s ‘Partition’ back to the charts. She’s become a true queen of the internet with clips from her live-filmed show, The Intruder, racking up over 100 million views. Fans even turn up to her shows wearing wigs styled as her signature bowl cut as a form of homage. Humour has no borders when you’re that funny.

events.id: France vs New Zealand-Noble Rot Wine Bar, 6 Swan Lane-WOAP
events.name: France vs New Zealand
events.venue: Noble Rot Wine Bar, 6 Swan Lane
events.long_description:
France has long set the benchmark for fine wine. New Zealand, by contrast, is young, confident, and still defining its place on the world stage. For this five-course degustation, Noble Rot places the two side-by-side in a focussed tasting of classic pairs that asks a simple question: has New Zealand earned its seat at the table?

Each course is a head-to-head. A French classic meets its New Zealand counterpart. The food is classic, designed to let the wines show their differences. Expect thoughtful comparison across the varieties, regions and styles that shape both countries’ reputations. The emphasis is on quality producers and wines that speak clearly of place. Five courses means five comparisons, each one letting you taste whether New Zealand's found its own voice or is still chasing France's shadow.

Your ticket includes an amuse bouche on arrival, five courses, ten wines matched head-to-head throughout the evening.

Join NZ cricket legend Grant Elliot for some inspiration, a bit of networking and a drink.

About this Event

This month:
GRANT ELLIOTT is a renowned former cricketer, having played over 100 games for the Blackcaps. Grant enjoyed success on the international stage particularly with white ball cricket.
Widely regarded by his teammates as a hard worker and a reliable player who always put the team first, Grant was written into New Zealand cricketing folklore books when he hit the winning 6 which propelled the Blackcaps into their first ever World Cup final!
An entertaining and insightful speaker, Grant shares his knowledge of team culture, motivation and exactly what it takes to create a high performing team.
Currently working as partnership manager for Life Flight, he has had over 18 years experience in the corporate world. Merging these two sectors is his passion as he believes sports culture plays a big part into creating a high performing corporate culture.

events.venue: The Runholder, 89 Martins Road
events.long_description:
Candlelight is the only way to experience centuries-old music properly, and The Night Watch, Wellington's premier early music ensemble, know this. So for one night only, in collaboration with National Candles, in a concert steeped in candlelight, this is your chance to go back in time. Keep your phones pocketed and let the modern world recede for a few hours.

Bringing together Australasia's top specialists in early music, The Night Watch perform on period instruments: harpsichord, viola da gamba, and others from a tradition that predates the modern orchestra entirely. The evening features countertenor Austin Haynes and soprano Carleen Ebbs, two of New Zealand's top vocalists. Heard live in a candlelit room, you'll experience this music beyond anything a recording could do. The candles themselves are courtesy of National Candles, one of New Zealand's oldest candle makers, handcrafting their wares for over half a century.
At The Runholder in Martinborough, a three-course family-style menu built for sharing and unhurried conversation. The food is warm and generous: rich winter flavours.

Your ticket includes a welcome drink on arrival and three courses. Additional drinks are available to purchase on the night.

events.venue: Union Square, 10 Memorial Square
events.long_description:
From cattle country to oil fields, from dive bars to dinner tables. Tulsa's food tells the story of America's heartland. General Manager Adam Cruz continues his "meets Martinborough" series by bringing the bold, smoky soul of Southern cooking to the Napoleon dining room's intimate fireplace. 
Five courses trace a culinary exploration: start with a Reuben egg roll (sauerkraut, corned beef, Russian dressing), move through fried pork ribs that legend is made of, followed by biscuits swimming in sausage gravy, and then slow-smoked BBQ pulled pork served with cornbread, fried okra, and black-eyed peas — sides that honour the agricultural plains. Strawberry pecan pie closes out the night. Each course pairs with a Martinborough beverage: hand-crafted brews from Martinborough Brewery, award-winning Pinot Noir and Chardonnay from Palliser Estate, a botanical gin from Margrain, and a Noble wine to finish with pie. 
Your ticket includes five courses and four standard drinks (low and non-alcoholic options available).

events.long_description:
Sound Healing Experience at Lotus Yoga Centre
We invite you to a special evening of Sacred Harmonic Sound with multi-instrumentalist Claudio Escutia. This immersive sound journey offers a deeply restorative experience that invites you to settle into stillness, reconnect with the heart, and explore a sense of inner spaciousness through vibration

About the event
Claudio skilfully layers the sounds of gongs, crystal and Tibetan singing bowls, Native American flutes, and other traditional instruments, enhanced through high-quality audio equipment so the sound can be both heard and felt throughout your body.Harmonic sound and vibration offer the nervous system a chance to truly rest. In this state of relaxation, the thinking mind softens, and we find connection to citta — the heart-mind. From this place, silence arises naturally through the vehicle of sound.This experience is open to everyone. No previous yoga or meditation practice is needed.


What to bring:Bring your own yoga mat or camping mattress, small pillows, eye pillows and blanket to assure comfort.

Booking is essential — spaces are limited and this event often fills quickly.

About ClaudioClaudio is a multi-instrumentalist musician originally from Mexico City and now based in Wellington. Born into a family of musicians, he began playing music at a young age and later studied classical guitar. His journey led him to Montreal, where he explored jazz, world music, and spiritual sound traditions.

Extensive travels in Asia and Europe deepened his connection with Indian music and yogic philosophy. He studied Tibetan singing bowls in Kathmandu and Varanasi, and has since worked with a wide range of instruments including the sitar, esraj, bansuri, harmonium, flutes, gongs, and voice.

Claudio’s work blends technical skill, deep presence, and a profound respect for the healing power of sound.

General admission : $45

Learn more buy tickets and listen to Claudio’s music here:

https://www.claudioescutia.com/events/sound-healing-experience-at-lotus-yoga-centre-2

SoundCloud https://soundcloud.com/claudioescutiasounds

Instagram

Facebook

events.long_description:
You’ll definitely feel better if you come and have a sing with a few thousand strangers. That’s what New Zealand-born vocalist, conductor, and composer Astrid Jorgensen thinks. Astrid is the brainchild behind the touring show Pub Choir — Just Think About It. The premise is simple — come to the Michael Fowler Centre on 19 August and learn one popular song in three-part harmony. What began as a small gathering in a pub has now grown to fill concert halls around the world. No prior training is required — just bring your voice and a sense of humour. 
Astrid established Pub Choir in Brisbane in 2017. Her work associated with the show has gone on to win her several awards. This includes one of the 40 Under 40 Most Influential Asian-Australians by the Asian-Australian Leadership Summit in 2021 and a Medal of the Order of Australia (OAM) in 2023.

events.name: Entre Calles
events.venue: Cuba Street Tavern, 172 Cuba Street
events.long_description:
Cuba Street Tavern owner Rich spent eight trips wandering Barcelona's backstreets, finding treasured and memorable venues, not because they were advertised but because someone leaned in and said, "trust me, you need to try this place". Entre Calles recreates that feeling through shared tapas, Spanish-inspired drinks and music. 

Tapas arrive in waves across shared tables while DJs spin Spanish tracks. Nobody's ordering from a menu, plates just come, each one designed for passing and picking at, the kind of eating where the conversation flows as easily as the Spanish-inspired drinks. Expect pinchos that hit hard, dishes that layer and surprise, and the feeling of being somewhere because someone recommended it rather than because you planned. It's tight, vibey, and a little chaotic in the best possible way. 

Your ticket includes eight courses of shared tapas and three paired Spanish-inspired drinks.

events.venue: Noble Rot Wine Bar, 6 Swan Lane
events.long_description:
For this five-course degustation, Head Chef Nicolas Mentzas draws on his Greek heritage to present the flavours and textures of home through a refined, fine-dining lens. Often perceived as relaxed and informal, there is a quiet depth to Greek cuisine. It is shaped by season, coastline, mountain herbs, and generations gathered around the table.
Dinner unfolds as a carefully composed menu that honours tradition while embracing precision in one of the world’s oldest wine cultures. Rather than a shared feast, expect elevated dishes rooted in Greek culinary history, reinterpreted with elegance and detail. Each course is paired with Greek wines, highlighting distinctive indigenous grape varieties and the growing confidence of the country’s modern producers.
Throughout the evening, the Noble Rot sommelier team will introduce each pairing, exploring how Greece’s food and wine traditions complement one another in perfect harmony, at the highest level.
Your ticket includes an amuse bouche on arrival, five courses, an arrival wine, and seven Greek wines paired throughout the evening.

Another fact is that Pub Choir is the world’s biggest, best, funniest, hottest music lesson. This fact has been verified by independent* sources (*we paid a guy on fiverr to say it).

An actually true fact is that Pub Choir is an opt-in experience. You don’t HAVE to buy a ticket and you are allowed to rot at home like you always do. But you PROBABLY should come and have a sing with a few thousand strangers. You would DEFINITELY feel better if you did. And hasn’t your sister-in-law been asking for years to go with you? It couldn’t be that bad could it?!? Everybody keeps bloody going on about it, maybe it’s worth a look. Anyway, just think about it.

What I'm saying is that Pub Choir will be touring across the world this year and Astrid is brewing some truly great arrangements, which I can claim with some authority, because I am her. We'll start in July in Australia, then head to NZ, Europe, the UK, and Asia. More info to come! In the meantime, the tour is called ‘Just Think About It’. And if you could, that'd be great.

events.long_description:
Women's Health and Aging Workshop
This course is free for NZ citizens and residents.  Please enrol online and bring photo ID when attending the workshop.
If you are not a NZ citizen or resident, a fee of $120 applies and you must phone the office on 04 385 8919 to register.
An interactive workshop presented by experienced physiotherapist Sara Dore, focusing on how movement and function can be challenging for women as they age. Particularly for women, there is more to the core than abdominal muscles and strength and we explore these broader aspects.  Most importantly, you will come to understand that movement is medicine and we can make a difference.
You will be able to make a positive difference for yourself! The objective of this workshop is to give you knowledge and understanding about how you can manage the effects on your health and wellbeing as we age as women.  Knowledge is power!
In this one-day workshop you will discover:
- The base of the pelvic floor. Anatomy of the pelvic floor, and the common conditions urinary incontinence, and pelvic organ prolapse will be discussed. Education on basic pelvic floor advice and management as well as appropriate exercises will also be covered.
- The middle deep abdominal muscles. Trunk stability versus core strength as we age and the impact on our other core muscles and pelvic floor will be discussed. The principles of Clinical Pilates versus traditional Pilates will be presented together with the key principles of movement is medicine.
-The importance of the diaphragm and breathing well will also be discussed to enhance optimal movement and function for women.
Please wear comfortable clothes and socks as this is an interactive workshop, and bring a yoga mat or beach towel.
Tea and coffee provided, please bring your lunch and snacks.
NOTE: This course is subsidised with funding from the Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) and you must provide photo ID when you attend your first session, if applicable.

events.long_description:
A Day in the Heart - One Day Silent Yoga and Meditation Retreat
An invitation to press "pause" for a day, and just Be.

To drop from the busy mind into the silence of the Heart.

And to remember the freedom of who you are, when you're not in a role.


This lovingly crafted offering is a day immersion into practice, providing a glimpse of what the experience of silence can offer.

Suitable for complete beginners in meditation and yoga, as well as for advanced practitioners who'd like to unplug and enjoy retreat-time.


The schedule will include:

- Multiple seated meditation sessions with guidance

- Walking meditation

- Mindful Hatha Yoga and Restorative Yoga sessions

- Yoga Nidra

- Cacao to open the Heart

- Time to journal, walk in nature, or just be


Cost for a whole day program + 2 meals: $195


Food:

breakfast and lunch - nutritious vegan meals prepared with love + tea and cacao


Location:

the Lotus Yoga Centre in Paraparaumu


Date: 22nd August 2026 Saturday

Duration: 7.30am - 5.30pm

please arrive at 7.15am to settle in and start on time


To book, please purchase your ticket below or email Radha for more info at


*WHY IS THIS A SILENT RETREAT? A silent retreat means that everyone participating observes mauna, noble silence (apart from the teacher/ the guide). This means no casual chats and conversations, but also no use of phone or any devices during the day. The practice of silence allows the the mind to quieten down significantly, it is a very unique, deeply purifying and enlightening experience. It creates space for a deep insight and a proper reset, even in the short span of one day.


*WHY MEDITATION? Meditation is known for thousands of years as one of the most powerful practices, within and outside of spiritual context. It is good not only for creating a state of calm or relaxation, but also is the best known path to self-knowledge and self-love. When we retreat into silence beyond mind, there is an unmistakable feeling of being back home, in the heart of being, a sense of connection and purpose.


*WHY "A DAY IN THE HEART"? The Heart/ Hridaya in Sanskrit is a synonym of awareness or presence. According to the great yogis and the non-dual philosophy, the Heart is a place to centre in our meditations, but also an organ of knowledge and the seat of our true Self. When the mind is quiet and we centre within, the Heart can awaken - bringing a sense of being back home, back to what truly matters, back to our Self.

As Rumi said, "Close your eyes, fall in love, stay there"

events.long_description:
Dark Sky Trek Wainuiomata
We’ve teamed up with the Wellington Astronomical Society to bring you this exclusive FREE behind-the-scenes event.

Walk deep into untouched native forest, through some of the oldest trees in the Wellington region as darkness falls. You may even hear the calls of kiwi and rūrū (morepork). Explore an area not normally open to the public, including a glowworm-filled tunnel that links to the Orongorongo Valley.

The Wellington Astronomical Society will share insights on Dark Sky awareness and preservation and provide a telescope for viewing the Moon and the Southern Cross. Talk to Remutaka Conservation Trust volunteers about their Kiwi release programme and nest monitoring efforts.

Wainuiomata Regional Park is working towards dark sky reserve accreditation, one of only three in the Southern Hemisphere. Light pollution from the city washes out most stars, but the park offers one of the best stargazing experiences in the region.

What to bring:
• Torches/headlamps (red lenses preferred)
• Sturdy waterproof footwear
• Warm and wet weather clothing

Note: This event includes a steep hill walk in the dark. A moderate level of fitness is required, and it is not suitable for children under 15.

This event is strictly limited to 30 people. Registrations for this event will be on a first in first served basis and opens at 10am on Tuesday 14 July via this link:

events.long_description:
At Cicio Cacio Osteria, the Mediterranean comes to the table in an intimate dinner shaped by memory and place. Inspired by the owner's childhood on a Mediterranean island, this dinner traces a path from Italy to Spain, across Greece and into the Middle East, with dishes from each region reflecting the shared spirit of the Mediterranean: the sun, the sea, the music, the nostalgia, the being in the moment. The food is uncomplicated and entirely enjoyable, simple, fare focused on freshness and simplicity, letting the ingredients speak for themselves. Expect the most perfect hummus with grilled pita, the best Spanish tortilla, uncommon seafood like octopus and sardines, couscous, lamb, and goat, pastas, and colourful salads, a true insight into the Mediterranean spirit. 

You'll be seated at a long communal table in front of a real fire for a progressive nine-course menu, each plate paired with a matched wine selected to reflect its origin and character. Throughout the evening, the chef shares stories behind the dishes, offering insight into flavours, traditions, and personal history. You're invited to come into the kitchen and share the secrets of each recipe, cooking alongside the chef. A final musical touch ends an evening dedicated to the beauty, spontaneity, and simplicity of the Mediterranean. 

Your ticket includes nine courses, nine matched wines, storytelling, hands-on cooking, and recipe sharing.

events.name: George Motz: Burger Scholar
events.venue: The Opera House, 113/111 Manners Street
events.long_description:
Anyone that fancies themselves a smash burger expert knows who George Motz is. He has dedicated his life to burgers - he has written about them, made films about them, and cooked them for the masses. This has rightfully earned him the Burger Scholar title. Now he is bringing that knowledge to this burger loving city, at the bottom of the world, to share with all of you.

On stage, Motz will present his world famous "History of the Burger" starting from his research into the origins of the sandwich from 13th-century Mongolia to its rise as an American staple and now a favourite all over the world. You’ll then get a full demonstration of the burger that gave him a global following - the Oklahoma Onion burger. The demonstration will be projected overhead live to capture all the detail and he's holding no secrets back. The night will conclude with a Q&A

Your ticket includes the presentation, live cooking demonstration and Q&A. No food will be served. A cash bar and merch will be available to purchase on the night.

This International Chef Collaboration is proudly supported by the New Zealand Government’s Events Boost Fund.

events.venue: Boomrock Lodge, 292 Boom Rock Road
events.long_description:
Be one of the first in the country to taste the 2023 vintage single vineyard wines from Martinborough's Pinot Noir superstars, Escarpment. From the gravels and windswept terraces of Martinborough, Escarpment has built a devoted following through word of mouth, shared by locals, championed by sommeliers, and remembered long after the last glass. 

Presented by winemaker Tim Bourne against the wild outlook of Boomrock's coastal position, you'll sample their wines paired with locally sourced wild ingredients including wild boar, Cook Strait snapper, tītī (mutton bird), venison, and Wairarapa cheese. 

The afternoon opens with Rosé on arrival and canapés of wild boar arancini and ceviche, then moves to a three-course long lunch. Expect leek, tītī, and Mānuka honey pasta with kawa kawa butter; tart cherry venison loin with purple kūmara gratin and Kikorangi Blue; and a Wairarapa cheese course with dark chocolate and blackberry jelly. Each course is matched with Escarpment's range, celebrating the magic of Wairarapa. Your ticket also includes return bus transport.

events.id: Songs from the Deep-Little Beer Quarter, 6 Edward Street-WOAP
events.name: Songs from the Deep
events.venue: Little Beer Quarter, 6 Edward Street
events.long_description:
LBQ drops anchor for one night, trading its usual warmth for something saltier. Long communal tables, low light, rope and timber, and the Pōneke Shanty Club leading the room through some rousing singalongs.
Sea shanties were never written down. They travelled port to port, voice to voice, and that's exactly how the evening works. By the second set the room is carrying the chorus. Between the music, anonymous dockside confessions are read aloud and become part of the night's folklore.

Food is hearty and built for winter: slow-braised beef cheek and dark ale pie, or roasted kūmara and caramelised onion pie to start. Char-grilled market fish or a smoked mushroom and lentil wellington to follow, and a spiced rum sticky pudding or dark chocolate and sea salt tart to close.

Your ticket includes three courses and three drinks. Choose from curated beer, rum, or non-alcoholic ginger beer.

events.id: Hidden Ferments-Chaat Street, 171 Willis Street-WOAP
events.name: Hidden Ferments
events.venue: Chaat Street, 171 Willis Street
events.long_description:
Indian fermentation has long lived in home kitchens and ancient texts, yet rarely takes centre stage in restaurants, especially on the global stage. This collaborative event invites you into that quieter, largely unseen world as chefs Saavni Krishnan and Sriram Aditya from Melbourne's Saadi restaurant, and chef Vaibhav Vishen, from Wellington's Chaat Street, bring a fine-dining lens to India's deep fermentation traditions, set against Wellington's wild, coastal produce. Across an intimate evening, the menu combines age-old techniques and new terroir: cultured grains, pickles, kanji-style ferments, and lacto-preserved fruits.

For both chefs their cooking is rooted in memory and comfort but expressed with restraint, clarity, and precision. Think fermented rice and lentil batters reimagined as delicate snacks, vegetables transformed through lactic fermentation to echo both Indian aachar and Wellington's coastal flora, and broths built on aged, cultured bases for depth and length. The journey traces a loose path from the grain and pulse-based ferments that underpin everyday Indian eating, through preserved vegetables and fruits, to experimental applications responding to Wellington's climate and producers. 

Your ticket includes a five-course tasting menu with thoughtful beverage pairings designed to echo ferment-forward flavours. Non-alcoholic options feature pickled, infused, and cultured elements without overpowering the palate. This event has shared seating.
